children.title: Oracle-Cost Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Cost accounting across component, batch, and full-gradient queries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Undeclared Cost Weights Prevent Scalar Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of scalar oracle-complexity comparison without a common primitive-cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Two algorithms with count vectors \(N\) and \(N'\) need not admit an implementation-independent scalar ordering. If, for example, \(N=(1,0)\) and \(N'=(0,1)\) for component and full-gradient calls, then
\[
C_c(N)=c_{\mathrm{comp}},\qquad C_c(N')=c_{\mathrm{full}}.
\]
Either algorithm can be cheaper under admissible choices of these weights. Thus heterogeneous call counts are not scalar-comparable until a common cost convention is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different oracle-count vectors cannot generally be ranked by one scalar cost without declared primitive weights.
assumptions_latex: At least two oracle types have independently specified nonnegative costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separated count vectors may be incomparable before a common scalarization \(c\) is declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Undeclared Cost Weights Prevent Scalar Comparison

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separated Counts and Weighted Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector and scalar representations of heterogeneous finite-sum oracle usage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\) be the declared set of oracle types and let \(N_q\in\mathbb N_0\) count calls of type \(q\). The separated oracle cost is the vector \(N=(N_q)_{q\in Q}\). Given declared nonnegative unit weights \(c_q\), it may be scalarized as
\[
C_c(N)=\sum_{q\in Q}c_qN_q.
\]
A component-equivalent convention may set \(c_{\mathrm{comp}}=1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{full}}=n\) when a full gradient is stipulated to be reconstructed from \(n\) component calls. That normalization is not intrinsic when the full-gradient primitive has reusable structure, parallel implementation, caching, or a separately priced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heterogeneous oracle calls should be retained as a count vector until explicit unit costs are chosen; assigning a full gradient cost n is conditional on the reconstruction model.
assumptions_latex: The unit weights \(c_q\ge0\) and included oracle types are declared.
Any component-equivalent normalization is part of the computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=(N_q)_{q\in Q}\) is the convention-free count representation and \(C_c(N)=\sum_qc_qN_q\) is its declared scalarization.

notation.meaning: number of queries of type q

knowledge_statements.title: Separated Counts and Weighted Oracle Cost
Oracle-Cost Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted accounting of heterogeneous finite-sum oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an algorithm make \(N_{\mathrm{comp}}\) component queries, \(N_{\mathrm{full}}\) aggregate-gradient queries, and \(N_{\mathrm{prox}}\) proximal queries. Given nonnegative declared unit costs \(c_{\mathrm{comp}},c_{\mathrm{full}},c_{\mathrm{prox}}\), its oracle cost is represented by
\[
C_{\mathrm{oracle}}=c_{\mathrm{comp}}N_{\mathrm{comp}}+c_{\mathrm{full}}N_{\mathrm{full}}+c_{\mathrm{prox}}N_{\mathrm{prox}}.
\]
Under reduction to component-gradient evaluations, the conventional normalization is \(c_{\mathrm{comp}}=1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{full}}=n\). Any complexity claim using this interface must state the included query types and cost weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle-cost interface converts counts of different query types into a declared weighted resource total; a full gradient conventionally costs n component gradients.
assumptions_latex: All query counts are nonnegative integers and all declared unit costs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{oracle}}=\sum_q c_qN_q\), with the component-equivalent convention \(c_{\mathrm{comp}}=1\) and \(c_{\mathrm{full}}=n\).

notation.meaning: number of queries of type q
declared unit cost of query type q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental component access supplemented by explicitly managed persistent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A memory-augmented finite-sum oracle interface consists of a component response map and persistent state \(M\). A query \((i,x,M)\) returns
\[
(q_i(x),M^+)=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mem}}(i,x,M),
\qquad M^+=U(i,x,q_i(x),M),
\]
where initialization, readable state, update map, and permitted update scope are declared parts of the interface. Component-indexed tables are the special case \(M=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\); restricting an update to \(m_i\) is a common convention, not a consequence of memory augmentation itself. Storage cost is accounted for separately from the oracle response contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A memory-augmented oracle combines a component response with persistent state whose initialization and transition rule must be declared.
assumptions_latex: The initial state and update map are specified.
Persistent state remains available between calls.
The interface declares whether updates may affect only the selected entry or broader state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every query produces component information and a uniquely specified successor state \(M^+\).
review_flags: single-entry replacement treated as a special convention rather than a universal requirement
knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Augmented Component-Oracle Contract

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintenance of an aggregate statistic after one component-memory entry is replaced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\) and \(\bar m=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n m_j\). If one update replaces \(m_i\) by \(m_i^+\) and leaves the other entries unchanged, then
\[
\bar m^+=\bar m+\frac1n(m_i^+-m_i).
\]
Thus storing both \(M\) and \(\bar m\) permits exact incremental maintenance of the average, provided initialization is exact and every replacement applies the corresponding correction. An omitted or incorrect correction makes the cache inconsistent with the table.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When one memory entry changes, its cached average can be updated exactly from the old and new entries; missed corrections make the cache stale.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one entry is replaced and its old value is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar m^+=\bar m+n^{-1}(m_i^+-m_i)\), with exactness contingent on consistent initialization and updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cached-Aggregate Update
Memory-Augmented Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental oracle access supplemented by persistent component-indexed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A memory-augmented finite-sum oracle interface consists of an incremental oracle and a mutable state \(M=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\). On query \((i,x,M)\), it returns the component information \(q_i(x)\), reads the current state, and applies a declared update
\[
\bigl(q_i(x),M^+\bigr)=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mem}}(i,x,M),
\qquad
m_i^+=U_i(m_i,q_i(x),x),
\qquad
m_j^+=m_j\ \text{for }j\ne i,
\]
unless the interface explicitly permits broader updates. The stored entries may contain past gradients, points, or sufficient statistics, and their initialization and storage cost are part of the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A memory-augmented oracle combines component queries with persistent indexed state, updating stored information according to an explicit rule after each query.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is initialized before the first query and remains available between oracle calls.
The response map \(q_i\) and update map \(U_i\) are specified by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each query returns component information and a well-defined successor memory state \(M^+\).

notation.meaning: declared update map for the selected memory entry

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Epoch-SVRG Complexity
Epoch-Based Snapshot Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVRG-type control variate with a snapshot fixed throughout each epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). At epoch \(s\), choose a snapshot \(\widetilde x_s\), compute \(\mu_s=
abla F(\widetilde x_s)\), and initialize \(x_{s,0}=\widetilde x_s\) or the preceding epoch's output. For \(t=0,\ldots,m-1\), sample \(i_{s,t}\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), form \[v_{s,t}=
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(x_{s,t})-
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(\widetilde x_s)+\mu_s,\] and update \(x_{s,t+1}=x_{s,t}-\eta v_{s,t}\). The snapshot remains fixed within the epoch and is replaced only at an epoch boundary. Output a prescribed inner iterate, an average of inner iterates, or the final epoch endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a full gradient at each epoch snapshot, then use component-gradient differences plus that full gradient for all inner updates in the epoch.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
Indices are sampled uniformly and conditionally independently within each epoch.

notation.meaning: number of inner updates per epoch

For v=
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(\widetilde x)+
abla F(\widetilde x) with uniform i, \mathbb E\|v-
abla F(x)\|^2\le L^2\|x-\widetilde x\|^2 when every component is L-smooth.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every f_i is convex and L-smooth and F is \mu-strongly convex, then a standard loopless-SVRG regime with p=\Theta(1/n) and a valid constant step attains \mathbb E[F(x)-F_*]\le\varepsilon in O\!\left((n+L/\mu)\log((F(x_0)-F_*)/\varepsilon)\right) expected component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard loopless SVRG matches the order n plus condition-number linear-convergence complexity without deterministic epochs.
assumptions_latex: Every f_i is convex and L-smooth.
The refresh timing, step, and output follow a valid loopless-SVRG contraction regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Oracle Cost Per Loopless Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-gradient accounting for Bernoulli full-gradient refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each estimator update separately evaluates \nabla f_{i_k}(x_k) and \nabla f_{i_k}(w_k), while an independent Bernoulli-p refresh computes a full gradient costing n component gradients, then the expected per-iteration cost is 2+pn, excluding initialization and any coincident-point reuse. Thus p=\Theta(1/n) gives \Theta(1) expected component-gradient work per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loopless iteration costs two sampled gradients plus an expected p full gradients.
assumptions_latex: A full gradient is charged as n component-gradient evaluations.
The two indexed gradients are separately charged unless reused.
The refresh indicator has success probability p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of constant-step exact convergence when the refresh probability is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let n=2, f_1(x)=0, f_2(x)=x^2, and F(x)=x^2/2. Fix w\ne0 forever by taking p=0. At x=0, the snapshot estimator is w or -w with equal probability. Hence a constant-step update obeys \mathbb E[x_+^2\mid x=0]=\eta^2w^2>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With no refresh, a stale snapshot can retain estimator noise at the minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The component index is uniform on \{1,2\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh-time structure induced by independent Bernoulli snapshot replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the snapshot is refreshed independently at each iteration with probability p\in(0,1]. Let T count iterations from one refresh through the next, including the successful iteration. Then \Pr(T=t)=(1-p)^{t-1}p for t\ge1, \mathbb E[T]=p^{-1}, and the probability of no refresh in the next r iterations is (1-p)^r.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent loopless refreshes have geometrically distributed inter-refresh times with mean one over the refresh probability.
assumptions_latex: Refresh indicators are independent Bernoulli-p variables.

Let \(\delta_i=\nabla f_i(x)-y_i\), \(\bar\delta=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_i\), \(\bar y=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i\), and let \(J\) be uniform. For \(v=\delta_J+\bar y\), \[\mathbb E[\|v-\nabla F(x)\|^2\mid x,(y_i)]=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\delta_i-\bar\delta\|^2=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\delta_i\|^2-\|\bar\delta\|^2.\]

assumptions_latex: \(J\) is conditionally uniform after the table is fixed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAGA-type unbiased correction of an averaged component-gradient memory table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Initialize \(x_0\), table entries \(y_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), and \(\bar y^0=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i^0\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(j_k\) uniformly and form \[v_k=\nabla f_{j_k}(x_k)-y_{j_k}^k+\bar y^k.\] Update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta v_k\), replace \(y_{j_k}^{k+1}=\nabla f_{j_k}(x_k)\), retain all other entries, and update their average. Stop under a prescribed rule and return the designated iterate.

\(j_k\) is uniform conditional on the current iterate and memory table.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the unbiased table-correction leaf, and the SAGA-type formula has the stated conditional expectation under uniform sampling. No source or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Surrogate-Memory Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MISO/Finito-type memory of primal component surrogates for a regularized finite sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+(\lambda/2)\lVert x\rVert^2\) with \(\lambda>0\). Store primal surrogates \(z_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and set \(x_k=n^{-1}\sum_i z_i^k\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(j_k\) uniformly, compute \[z_{j_k}^{k+1}=x_k-\frac{1}{\lambda n}\nabla f_{j_k}(x_k),\] retain \(z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k\) for \(i\ne j_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=n^{-1}\sum_i z_i^{k+1}\). Stop under a prescribed rule and output the designated averaged primal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store componentwise primal surrogates, refresh one using its current gradient, and define the iterate as their average.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
The objective contains quadratic regularization with \(\lambda>0\).

notation.meaning: stored primal surrogate for component i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the factor 1/(lambda n) is not reliably determined by the displayed objective and varies with MISO/Finito component and regularization conventions. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed diagonal sketch correction for sampled Jacobian columns with arbitrary inclusion probabilities.

Define I_C=\sum_{i\in C}e_ie_i^{\mathsf T} and B_C=\sum_{i\in C}p_i^{-1}e_ie_i^{\mathsf T}. The memory refresh J^+=J+(G-J)I_C and estimator v_C=n^{-1}[J\mathbf1+(G-J)B_C\mathbf1] satisfy \mathbb E[v_C]=n^{-1}G\mathbf1. Uniform singleton sampling gives B_C=ne_je_j^{\mathsf T}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-level component-gradient complexity for smooth nonconvex finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an L-smooth finite sum F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i with F_*>-\infty, a standard finite-sum SPIDER regime with exact periodic refreshes and suitably chosen difference batches, period, and steps produces x_{\mathrm{out}} satisfying \mathbb E\|\nabla F(x_{\mathrm{out}})\|\le\varepsilon using O\!\left(n+\sqrt n\,L(F(x_0)-F_*)\varepsilon^{-2}\right) component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard finite-sum SPIDER reaches expected epsilon-stationarity in order n plus square-root-n over epsilon-squared component gradients.
assumptions_latex: Exact periodic refreshes and a valid finite-sum SPIDER parameter regime are used.

abla f_J(x_{k-1}), where I,J are independent uniform indices. Then \mathbb E|
abla f_I(1)-
abla f_J(1)|^2=2, whereas L^2|x_k-x_{k-1}|^2=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Refresh Bias Prevents Vanishing Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when periodic SPIDER-style refreshes have a fixed nonzero bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), and suppose every refresh sets \(v=x+c\) for a fixed \(c\neq0\), while recursive differences are exact: \(v_k=v_{k-1}+x_k-x_{k-1}\). Then throughout every cycle \(v_k=x_k+c\). With a constant step \(0<\eta<2\), \(x_{k+1}=(1-\eta)x_k-\eta c\) converges to \(-c\), where \(|\nabla F(-c)|=|c|>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed bias in every SPIDER-style refresh is propagated by exact recursive differences and can force convergence to a nonstationary point.
assumptions_latex: Every refresh has the same additive bias \(c\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Refresh Bias Prevents Vanishing Stationarity

abla F(x_k)\|^2.\] An exact full-gradient refresh instead sets this error to zero. Thus a cycle begins with either zero error or a refresh error determined by the stated sampling law.

Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Fix a refresh period \(q\). At iteration \(k\), if \(k\equiv0\pmod q\), sample a refresh batch \(S_k\) and set \(v_k=|S_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_k}
abla f_i(x_k)\), using the full index set when an exact refresh is required. Otherwise sample a batch \(B_k\) and set \[v_k=v_{k-1}+ rac1{|B_k|}\sum_{i\in B_k} igl(
abla f_i(x_k)-
abla f_i(x_{k-1}) igr).\] Choose a prescribed step length \(\alpha_k\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k v_k\), and output the designated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodically refresh a gradient estimate with a large batch, and between refreshes accumulate small-batch gradient differences.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
Refresh and difference batches are sampled according to the finite-sum sampling convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-level stationarity complexity for the standard constant-step SpiderBoost regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an L-smooth finite sum F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i with F_*>-\infty, a standard SpiderBoost regime using \eta=\Theta(1/L), exact refreshes, q=\Theta(\sqrt n), and difference batches of size \Theta(\sqrt n) produces an output with \mathbb E\|\nabla F(x_{\mathrm{out}})\|^2\le\varepsilon^2 in O(L(F(x_0)-F_*)\varepsilon^{-2}) iterations and O(n+\sqrt n\,L(F(x_0)-F_*)\varepsilon^{-2}) component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With square-root-n periods and batches and a smoothness-scaled constant step, standard SpiderBoost has the usual nonconvex finite-sum stationarity complexity.
assumptions_latex: The stated order-level parameter regime, exact refreshes, and a valid output convention are used.
knowledge_statements.title: SpiderBoost Nonconvex Finite-Sum Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oversized Constant Steps Diverge on a Scalar Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic stability boundary for the unnormalized SpiderBoost-form update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let n=1 and F(x)=Lx^2/2 with L>0, so v_k=Lx_k. Then x_{k+1}=(1-\eta L)x_k. The iterates converge for 0<\eta L<2, oscillate without decay at \eta L=2 when x_0\ne0, and diverge in magnitude for \eta L>2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with an exact estimator, an unnormalized constant step is unstable at and beyond the scalar quadratic threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Constant Steps Diverge on a Scalar Quadratic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SPIDER recursion paired with a fixed-scale gradient step under smoothness control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) and choose a period \(q\), batches, and a constant \(\eta>0\). At refresh iterations \(k\equiv0\pmod q\), set \(v_k\) to a full-gradient or prescribed large-batch estimate at \(x_k\). Otherwise sample \(B_k\) and set \[v_k=v_{k-1}+\frac1{|B_k|}\sum_{i\in B_k}\bigl(\nabla f_i(x_k)-\nabla f_i(x_{k-1})\bigr).\] Apply the unnormalized update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta v_k\). Stop using the prescribed gradient-estimation or stationarity criterion and return the designated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the SPIDER recursive estimator with an ordinary constant gradient step instead of normalizing the step by the estimator norm.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
The step size and batch schedule satisfy the chosen SpiderBoost convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterate update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta v_k\), while the estimator recursion is the SPIDER recursion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the SpiderBoost estimator leaf, and the fixed unnormalized step distinguishes the intended architecture. The batch schedule, refresh rule, and admissible constant-step regime are not fixed sufficiently to identify the named variant without an exact source.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F have an L-Lipschitz gradient and let x^+=x-\eta v. If 0<\eta\le 1/L, then F(x^+)\le F(x)-\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla F(x)\|^2+\frac{\eta}{2}\|v-\nabla F(x)\|^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Estimator Sharing Does Not Alone Transfer Trajectories or Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on transferring results when SPIDER and SpiderBoost share only an estimator formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two methods using the same recursive estimator formula need not generate the same estimator sequence, because their sampled differences are evaluated along method-dependent iterates. Unless their update maps coincide at every step, matching initial states and random samples do not imply matching later iterates, estimator values, descent inequalities, or convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared recursive formula does not transfer trajectories or convergence rates when different step rules create different evaluation points.
assumptions_latex: The methods start from the same state and are coupled with the same sampled indices.
At some iteration their update maps produce different next iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}^{(1)}\ne x_{k+1}^{(2)}\Longrightarrow\text{later recursive differences and rate arguments need not coincide}.
knowledge_statements.title: Estimator Sharing Does Not Alone Transfer Trajectories or Rates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Numerical Step Parameters Do Not Transfer Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete divergence between normalized and unnormalized updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(x)=x^2/2, n=1, x_0=2, and v_0=\nabla F(x_0)=2. A normalized displacement \eta=1/2 gives x_1^{\mathrm{norm}}=2-(1/2)v_0/|v_0|=3/2, whereas an unnormalized coefficient \gamma=1/2 gives x_1^{\mathrm{plain}}=2-(1/2)v_0=1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical estimators and equal numerical parameters need not give identical normalized-SPIDER and SpiderBoost iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: Equal Numerical Step Parameters Do Not Transfer Trajectories
SPIDER-to-SpiderBoost Transfer Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic boundary between normalized SPIDER steps and fixed-step SpiderBoost updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a SPIDER-type method uses the recursive estimator \(v_k\) and the normalized update \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_k\frac{v_k}{\lVert v_k\rVert}\] whenever \(v_k\ne0\). If, on a regime of iterations, \(\eta_k=\gamma\lVert v_k\rVert\) for a constant \(\gamma>0\), then those updates coincide exactly with the SpiderBoost-form updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\gamma v_k\). Conversely, a constant normalized displacement \(\eta_k\equiv\eta\) corresponds to an effective gradient-step coefficient \(\gamma_k=\eta/\lVert v_k\rVert\), which is generally not constant and is undefined at \(v_k=0\) unless a stopping convention is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized SPIDER and fixed-step SpiderBoost updates coincide precisely when the normalized displacement scales with the estimator norm.
assumptions_latex: The two methods use the same estimator sequence \((v_k)\).
\(v_k\ne0\) on every iteration where a normalized update is taken.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the transfer-regime leaf, and the displayed equivalence is algebraically correct for v_k not equal to zero. A source is still required to support presenting this algebraic reparameterization as the named SPIDER-to-SpiderBoost transfer regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Recursive Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multilevel recursive estimator with level-dependent refresh periods and batch sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), choose levels \(\ell=0,\ldots,L\), refresh periods \(q_\ell\), and batch sizes \(b_\ell\). Maintain increments \(u_k^{(\ell)}\). At iteration \(k\), refresh each level whose schedule triggers: level \(0\) receives a full-gradient or large-batch estimate, while a higher level receives a batch average of \(\nabla f_i(x_k)-\nabla f_i(x_{r_\ell(k)})\), where \(r_\ell(k)\) is that level's preceding refresh point. Retain unrefreshed increments, form \[v_k=\sum_{\ell=0}^L u_k^{(\ell)},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_k v_k,\] and return the iterate selected by the prescribed stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine several recursively refreshed gradient increments, using longer periods and larger batches at coarser levels.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
Each level has a specified sampling law, refresh schedule, and reference iterate.
The level increments are dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_k\) is the sum of the current levelwise refresh increments \(u_k^{(0)},\ldots,u_k^{(L)}\).

notation.meaning: gradient increment stored at level ell
previous refresh index for level ell

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the nested-recursive-estimator leaf, but the level refresh equations, reference hierarchy, sampling laws, and handling of overlapping refreshes are too underdetermined to specify one reliable estimator family. An exact source is needed to select and state a concrete recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: PAGE Estimator Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic refresh-and-recursion estimator for smooth finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PAGE probabilistically replaces its gradient estimate by an unbiased refresh-batch average or updates it using same-sample gradient differences, and then returns an iterate according to the applicable convergence criterion.
assumptions_latex: Each refresh or difference batch is sampled so that its average is conditionally unbiased for the corresponding finite-population average.
The refresh coin and newly sampled batches are conditionally independent of the pre-sampling history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_t\) is the PAGE refresh-and-recursion estimator used in \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta g_t\).

Including initialization, \(T\) updates cost \[b+T\bigl[pb+2(1-p)b'\bigr]\] in expectation when no cached evaluations are credited.

No cross-iteration gradient cache is credited.

Finite-Sum STORM-Type Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Same-sample momentum estimator specialized to finite-sum gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), let \(T\in\mathbb N\), and choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\), an initial estimator \(v_0\in\mathbb R^d\), stepsizes \(\eta_t>0\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), and weights \(a_t\in(0,1]\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T-1\). Set \(x_1=x_0-\eta_0v_0\). For \(t=1,\ldots,T-1\), sample \(I_t\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), use the same index at \(x_t\) and \(x_{t-1}\), and set \[v_t=\nabla f_{I_t}(x_t)+(1-a_t)\bigl(v_{t-1}-\nabla f_{I_t}(x_{t-1})\bigr),\qquad x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t v_t.\] A mini-batch version replaces the two component gradients by averages over the same sampled batch. Output the iterate prescribed by the stationarity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-sum STORM-type method first takes a step using an initial estimate and then blends each fresh component gradient with a momentum-corrected previous estimate, using the same sample at consecutive points.
assumptions_latex: For each \(t\geq1\), \(I_t\) is uniform and conditionally independent of the pre-sampling history.
The two component gradients in each correction use the same sampled index or batch.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the recursive cancellation when consecutive-point gradients use independent indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let n=2, f_1(x)=0, f_2(x)=cx, and suppose x_t=x_{t-1}=x. Replace the same-sample difference by independent uniform indices I,J and take a_t=0. Then v_t=v_{t-1}+\nabla f_I(x)-\nabla f_J(x). The increment has mean zero but variance c^2/2, whereas the required same-index increment is identically zero. Thus independent samples inject noise even when the two query points coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using independent indices in the two STORM correction terms destroys exact cancellation and can add noise even at identical consecutive points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Unbiasedness Does Not Imply Conditional Unbiasedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an unconditional mean identity to control adaptive-history bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be Rademacher, \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(H)\), \(\nabla f(x_t)=0\), and \(v_t=H\). Then \(\mathbb E[v_t]=0\), but \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=H\neq0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimator can be unbiased after averaging over history while being biased conditional on that history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[v_t]=0\) but \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]\neq0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Unbiasedness Does Not Imply Conditional Unbiasedness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent error formulation and orthogonality consequence of conditional unbiasedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(e_t=v_t-\nabla f(x_t)\), conditional unbiasedness is equivalent to \(\mathbb E[e_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=0\) almost surely. If \(e_t\) and an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable vector \(Y_t\) are square-integrable, then \(\mathbb E\langle e_t,Y_t\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional unbiasedness is exactly the martingale-difference property of the estimation error and gives orthogonality to square-integrable history-measurable vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(e_t\) and \(Y_t\) are square-integrable for the orthogonality statement.
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale-Difference Error Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-moment identity for conditionally unbiased gradient estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(v_t\) is conditionally square-integrable and \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=
abla f(x_t)\), then \[\mathbb E[\|v_t-
abla f(x_t)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]=\mathbb E[\|v_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]-\|
abla f(x_t)\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a conditionally unbiased estimator, mean-square estimation error equals conditional variance and the second moment minus the squared target norm.

Conditionally Unbiased Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiasedness relative to the information available before the current sample is drawn.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\geq0}\) be a filtration, let \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable, and let \(v_t\) be an integrable estimator of \(
abla f(x_t)\). The estimator is conditionally unbiased at time \(t\) precisely when \[\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=
abla f(x_t)\quad	ext{almost surely}.\] Equivalently, for every bounded \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable scalar random variable \(Z\), \(\mathbb E[Zv_t]=\mathbb E[Z
abla f(x_t)]\). Conditional unbiasedness implies ordinary unbiasedness after taking expectations, but it does not require \(v_t\) to be independent of the history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given the pre-sampling history, the estimator's conditional mean must equal the gradient at the history-measurable current iterate.

notation.meaning: information available before the current estimator sample

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional expectation characterization is standard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is standard and precisely stated, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the conditional-unbiasedness characterization required by the review contract.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of geometric forgetting when the contraction factor equals one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho=1\), take \(x_t=x_0\) and \(e_t=e_0\neq0\) deterministically. Then \(\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]=\|e_{t-1}\|^2\), yet the estimation error never decays.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero constant error satisfies the recursion at contraction factor one, so strict contraction is necessary for geometric forgetting.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Contraction Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of conditional mean-square contraction with iterate drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e_t=v_t-\nabla f(x_t)\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\rho\|e_{t-1}\|^2+C\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|^2\) almost surely with \(0\leq\rho<1\), then \[\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2\leq\rho^t\mathbb E\|e_0\|^2+C\sum_{k=1}^t\rho^{t-k}\mathbb E\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|^2.\] Consequently, a uniform drift bound \(\mathbb E\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|^2\leq D\) gives \(\limsup_t\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2\leq CD/(1-\rho)\), while drift converging to zero gives \(\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The contraction recursion yields a geometrically weighted tracking bound, a drift-dependent error floor, and vanishing estimation error when iterate drift vanishes.
assumptions_latex: The conditional contraction holds almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrolled Tracking-Error Bound
Biased Contracting Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional mean-square contraction allowing nonzero estimator bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_t=v_t-\nabla f(x_t)\), where \(x_t\) and \(v_{t-1}\) are measurable with respect to the pre-sampling filtration \(\mathcal F_t\). A biased estimator sequence is contracting with parameters \(\rho\in[0,1)\) and \(C\geq0\) when, for every \(t\geq1\), \[\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq \rho\|e_{t-1}\|^2+C\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|^2\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Bias is permitted: \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]\) need not equal \(\nabla f(x_t)\). When the iterates stop moving, the inequality yields geometric decay of conditional mean-square estimation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A biased estimator contracts when its conditional squared error shrinks geometrically, apart from an additive term caused by iterate movement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent, but competing estimator-contraction definitions exist and no source supports this exact conditional mean-square form or terminology.

children.title: History-Dependent Estimators
children.top_down_role: Estimators whose statistical structure depends on prior iterates or stored history.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: History Dependence Is Compatible with Conditional Unbiasedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between adaptation to the past and bias relative to the past.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v_t=V_t(x_t,\xi_t,H_t)\) with history-conditioned kernel \(K_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_t)\), history dependence creates no conditional bias exactly when \[\int V_t(x_t,\xi,H_t)\,K_t(d\xi\mid\mathcal F_t)=\nabla f(x_t)\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Independence from the past is therefore sufficient in many constructions but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimator may adapt to the past and remain unbiased when its mean under the actual conditional sampling law equals the current gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=\nabla f(x_t)\) if and only if the displayed kernel integral equals \(\nabla f(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.title: History Dependence Is Compatible with Conditional Unbiasedness
History-Dependent Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator sampling laws and values allowed to depend on past iterates, samples, and estimator states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a filtered probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t),\mathbb P)\), let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and let \(\xi_t\) have a conditional sampling kernel \(K_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_t)\). An estimator is history-dependent when \[v_t=V_t(x_t,\xi_t,H_t),\qquad H_t\in\mathcal F_t,\] and either \(V_t\) depends nontrivially on \(H_t\) or \(K_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_t)\) is not almost surely constant as a function of the history. Thus the conditional law of \(v_t\) may change with earlier iterates, indices, gradients, or internal estimator states; conditional moment statements must consequently be taken relative to \(\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-dependent estimator uses past algorithmic information in its value or in the conditional law of its current sample.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)\) contains the algorithmic history before sampling at time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional law \(\mathcal L(v_t\mid\mathcal F_t)\) may depend nontrivially on \(\mathcal F_t\).

notation.meaning: history state available at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The filtration-based definition is plausible and the definition kind fits, but no citation establishes that this is the intended local meaning of history-dependent estimators.

children.title: Coupled-Sample Estimators
children.top_down_role: Estimators using linked samples across related evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent-Sample Differences Lose the Vanishing Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of displacement-sensitive variance without shared sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_t=y_t=x\) and let \(I_t,J_t\) be conditionally independent uniform indices. For \(D_t=
abla f_{I_t}(x)-
abla f_{J_t}(x)\), \[\mathbb E[\|D_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]=2\,\mathbb E[\|
abla f_{I_t}(x)-
abla f(x)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t].\] This is positive when component gradients disagree, whereas the shared-index difference is identically zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent samples retain twice the component-gradient variance at identical points, while shared sampling makes the difference vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t=y_t\) does not imply vanishing difference variance without sample coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Sample Differences Lose the Vanishing Property

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Displacement-sensitive moment control for a shared-index gradient difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For conditionally uniform \(I_t\), let \(\Delta_t=
abla f_{I_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{I_t}(y_t)\). If each \(
abla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz, then \[\mathbb E[\|\Delta_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\left( rac1n\sum_{i=1}^nL_i^2ight)\|x_t-y_t\|^2.\] Its conditional variance is no larger and vanishes when \(x_t=y_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second moment and variance of a shared-index gradient difference scale quadratically with the distance between its query points.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Difference Second-Moment Bound
Coupled-Sample Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient differences evaluated with a shared random index or batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I_t\) be sampled uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), conditionally independently of \(\mathcal F_t\), and let \(x_t,y_t\) be \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable. The coupled-sample gradient-difference estimator is \[\Delta_t=
abla f_{I_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{I_t}(y_t).\] Because the same index is used at both points, \[\mathbb E[\Delta_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=
abla f(x_t)-
abla f(y_t).\] For a uniform mini-batch, the corresponding average has the same conditional mean. If every \(
abla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz, then \(\|\Delta_t\|\leq L_{I_t}\|x_t-y_t\|\), so coupling ties difference variability to displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the same random component at two points gives an unbiased gradient-difference estimate whose size is controlled by the points' separation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz for the norm bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The same-index representation, conditional expectation identity, and Lipschitz bound are correct under the stated assumptions, but the record has no inspectable variance-reduction source.

children.title: Dependence-Induced Bias Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Statistical limits created by temporal dependence or sample coupling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correction for history-adaptive single-component sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse conditional-probability weighting restores unbiasedness under adaptive sampling; an unweighted draw generally targets a probability-weighted gradient.
assumptions_latex: The weighted gradient is conditionally integrable.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Importance-Weight Correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of positive inclusion for general unbiased single-component estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If, on an event \(A\in\mathcal F_t\) of positive probability, \(q_{t,j}=0\) for some component \(j\), then no estimator based only on the selected component gradient and pre-sampling history can be conditionally unbiased for \(n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_t)\) uniformly over arbitrary values of \(\nabla f_j(x_t)\). Changing only the unobserved component changes the target without changing the conditional distribution of the observed data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component with zero conditional chance of observation cannot have an arbitrary contribution recovered unbiasedly from that sample alone.
assumptions_latex: \(q_{t,j}=0\) on an event of positive probability.
Only the selected component gradient and pre-sampling history are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: General conditional unbiasedness requires positive inclusion or separate information about every excluded contribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Inclusion Impossibility Boundary
Dependence-Induced Bias Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional unbiasedness fails when adaptive sampling probabilities are ignored.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n=2\), \(f_1(x)=x\), and \(f_2(x)=-x\), so \(
abla f(x)=0\) for \(f=(f_1+f_2)/2\). Suppose a history event \(A_t\in\mathcal F_t\) has positive probability and the adaptive sampler sets \(I_t=1\) on \(A_t\). For the unweighted estimator \(v_t=
abla f_{I_t}(x_t)\), \[\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=1\quad	ext{on }A_t,\] although \(
abla f(x_t)=0\). Hence marginally balanced or historically adaptive sampling does not ensure conditional unbiasedness. Unbiasedness can be restored only by an appropriate conditional sampling rule or valid importance weights with positive inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive component selection can create conditional bias even when the full finite-sum gradient is zero; valid conditional weighting or sampling is required.
assumptions_latex: The event \(A_t\in\mathcal F_t\) has positive probability.
The estimator ignores conditional selection probabilities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly demonstrates dependence-induced conditional bias and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the common contract requires external evidence for the bias and importance-weighting boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical SVRG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-sample snapshot SVRG for a differentiable finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Choose a snapshot \(\widetilde x\), stepsize \(\eta>0\), and inner-loop length \(m\). Compute \(\widetilde\mu=
abla f(\widetilde x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
abla f_i(\widetilde x)\), initialize \(x_0=\widetilde x\), and for \(t=0,\ldots,m-1\) sample \(I_t\) uniformly and set \[v_t=
abla f_{I_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{I_t}(\widetilde x)+\widetilde\mu,\qquad x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta v_t.\] Select the next snapshot from the inner iterates according to the stated SVRG option and repeat epochs; return the final snapshot or the iterate required by the convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical SVRG periodically computes a snapshot full gradient and corrects each sampled gradient by its component's change from that snapshot.
assumptions_latex: The snapshot full gradient is evaluated exactly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical epochwise rate of single-sample snapshot SVRG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every \(f_i\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth and \(f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. With parameters and an epoch-output rule satisfying the classical SVRG contraction condition, there is \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\mathbb E[f(\widetilde x_s)-f_\star]\leq \rho^s(f(\widetilde x_0)-f_\star).\] Parameters may be chosen with \(\eta=\Theta(L^{-1})\) and \(m=\Theta(L/\mu)\), giving \[N_{\nabla f_i}=O\!\left((n+L/\mu)\log\frac{f(\widetilde x_0)-f_\star}{\varepsilon}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Properly parameterized classical SVRG converges geometrically on smooth strongly convex finite sums.
assumptions_latex: The stepsize, epoch length, and output rule satisfy a valid SVRG contraction condition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variance control for the single-sample classical SVRG estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every \(
abla f_i\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(v=
abla f_I(x)-
abla f_I(\widetilde x)+
abla f(\widetilde x)\) for uniform \(I\), then \[\mathbb E\|v-
abla f(x)\|^2\leq  rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(\widetilde x)\|^2\leq L^2\|x-\widetilde x\|^2.\] Hence \(v=
abla f(x)\) deterministically when \(x=\widetilde x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical SVRG variance vanishes at the snapshot and is bounded by squared distance from the snapshot under component smoothness.
assumptions_latex: The sampled index is conditionally uniform.
knowledge_statements.title: Snapshot-Centered Variance Bound

children.title: Mini-Batch SVRG
children.top_down_role: SVRG variants using multiple component evaluations per inner iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch SVRG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVRG inner updates formed from a batch of corrected component gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), choose snapshot \(\widetilde x\), compute \(\widetilde\mu=
abla f(\widetilde x)\), and set \(x_0=\widetilde x\). At inner iteration \(t\), sample a batch \(B_t\) of size \(b\) and form \[v_t=\widetilde\mu+ rac1b\sum_{i\in B_t} igl(
abla f_i(x_t)-
abla f_i(\widetilde x) igr),\qquad x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta v_t.\] If the batch average is unbiased for the population average, then \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid x_t,\widetilde x]=
abla f(x_t)\). After \(m\) inner updates, choose the next snapshot by the specified epoch rule and repeat until the stopping criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mini-batch SVRG averages several snapshot-corrected component gradients per inner update while retaining unbiasedness under unbiased batch sampling.
assumptions_latex: The batch-average sampling rule is conditionally unbiased.
The snapshot full gradient is exact.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mini-batch estimator and conditional-mean claim are correct for an unbiased batch-average rule, but no source supports the named variant or distinguishes its replacement convention.

children.title: SVRG Batch-Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs across mini-batch scales.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Batch Exactness Does Not Reduce Serial Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint distinction between estimator variance and serial component-gradient work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an SVRG inner batch \(B=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \[v=
abla f(\widetilde x)+ rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n igl(
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(\widetilde x) igr)=
abla f(x),\] so its conditional variance is zero. Even when the snapshot gradients are cached, forming the update requires the \(n\) component gradients at \(x\), hence \(\Theta(n)\) serial component-gradient evaluations per inner update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full inner batch eliminates SVRG estimator variance but makes every inner update full-gradient-scale serial work.
assumptions_latex: Serial oracle cost charges every component gradient evaluated at the current point.
No additional structure provides the current full gradient more cheaply.

notation.meaning: serial component-gradient cost of one inner update

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Batch Exactness Does Not Reduce Serial Oracle Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-inner-update work and ideal parallel query depth as SVRG batch size varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SVRG inner estimator using a batch of size \(b\), assume the snapshot component gradients needed by the correction are cached. A dense implementation evaluates \(b\) current component gradients and performs \(O(bd)\) aggregate arithmetic. Thus its serial component-gradient cost is \(\Theta(b)\), whereas with at least \(b\) workers and simultaneous component-oracle calls its ideal component-query depth is one. Consequently, variance reduction from increasing \(b\) does not by itself imply a serial-work speedup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SVRG batch costs linearly in batch size serially but can have constant ideal query depth with enough workers; lower variance alone is not a serial speedup theorem.
assumptions_latex: Snapshot component gradients used in the correction are cached.
Component-gradient calls can be issued simultaneously for the parallel-depth statement.
Communication, synchronization, and reduction depth are excluded from ideal component-query depth.

notation.meaning: serial component-gradient cost of one inner update

knowledge_statements.title: SVRG Batch Serial–Parallel Cost Regimes
SVRG Batch-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional variance scaling for uniform SVRG mini-batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x,\widetilde x\in\mathbb R^d\) and define \(y_i=
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(\widetilde x)\) and \( ar y=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i\). For the SVRG estimator \(v=
abla f(\widetilde x)+b^{-1}\sum_{i\in B}y_i\), independent sampling with replacement gives \[\mathbb E\|v-
abla f(x)\|^2= rac1b rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|y_i- ar y\|^2.\] Uniform sampling without replacement with \(1\leq b<n\) gives the same population variance multiplied by \((n-b)/(b(n-1))\). Thus \(b=1\) is classical SVRG, increasing \(b\) reduces estimator variance, and \(b=n\) yields the exact gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SVRG mini-batch variance decreases as one over batch size, with a finite-population correction under sampling without replacement and zero variance at full batch.
assumptions_latex: The batch is uniform with the stated replacement convention.
\(x\) and \(\widetilde x\) are fixed under the sampling expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The variance factor is \(1/b\) with replacement and \((n-b)/(b(n-1))\) without replacement.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact variance of a sample mean

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The with-replacement and without-replacement variance factors are mathematically consistent with the stated population-variance normalization, but the record lacks the citation required for this nontrivial property.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal SVRG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Snapshot SVRG with a proximal update for composite finite-sum minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+h(x)\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), where each \(f_i\) is differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex. At snapshot \(\widetilde x\), compute \(\widetilde\mu=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
abla f_i(\widetilde x)\) and initialize \(x_0=\widetilde x\). For \(t=0,\ldots,m-1\), sample \(I_t\) uniformly, set \[v_t=
abla f_{I_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{I_t}(\widetilde x)+\widetilde\mu,\qquad x_{t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta h}(x_t-\eta v_t),\] where \(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta h}(z)=\arg\min_u\{h(u)+\|u-z\|^2/(2\eta)\}\). Choose the next snapshot by the prescribed epoch rule and repeat until stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal SVRG applies the proximal map of the nonsmooth term to an SVRG-corrected gradient step for the smooth finite sum.
assumptions_latex: The sampled index is conditionally uniform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta h}(x_t-\eta v_t)\) with \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid x_t,\widetilde x]=\nabla(n^{-1}\sum_i f_i)(x_t)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit obstruction when the snapshot is never renewed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(n=2\), \(f_1(x)=0\), \(f_2(x)=Lx^2/2\), and fix a nonzero snapshot \(w\). At the minimizer \(x_*=0\), the fixed-snapshot SVRG estimator equals \(Lw/2\) or \(-Lw/2\) with equal probability. Thus when \(p=0\), the estimator has variance \(L^2w^2/4\) at the optimum, so a constant-step iteration cannot converge to zero in mean square through variance reduction alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero refresh probability, a nonoptimal snapshot can produce persistent noise even at the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Refresh Persistent-Noise Example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Renewal structure induced by independent Bernoulli snapshot refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the snapshot is refreshed independently each iteration with probability \(p\), then the inter-refresh count \(T\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(T=t)=(1-p)^{t-1}p\) for \(t\geq1\), \(\mathbb ET=1/p\), and \(\mathbb P(T>t)=(1-p)^t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loopless SVRG replaces deterministic epochs by geometric refresh intervals.
assumptions_latex: Refresh coins are independent Bernoulli\((p)\) trials with \(p\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Loopless Refresh-Age Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Snapshot-dependent variance control for the loopless estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(f_i\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth, then for uniform \(i_k\), \[\mathbb E[\|v^k-\nabla f(x^k)\|^2\mid x^k,w^k]\leq4L\bigl(f(x^k)-f_*+f(w^k)-f_*\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The loopless estimator has the usual snapshot-dependent SVRG variance bound; random renewal controls its snapshot term.
assumptions_latex: The component index is conditionally uniform.
knowledge_statements.title: Loopless SVRG Variance Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Oracle Cost of Bernoulli Snapshot Refreshes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected component-gradient accounting for loopless SVRG under an explicitly declared refresh implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each loopless-SVRG iteration evaluates \(\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)\) and \(\nabla f_{i_k}(w^k)\), and independently recomputes an \(n\)-component full gradient with probability \(p\). Over \(T\) iterations, the expected number of component-gradient evaluations is \[\mathbb E N_{\mathrm{IFO}}(T)=2T+npT,\] apart from any separately declared initial full-gradient computation. Thus \(p=1/n\) gives three expected component-gradient evaluations per iteration under this accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bernoulli refreshes add np expected component-gradient evaluations per iteration to the two evaluations used by the SVRG control variate.
assumptions_latex: The two component gradients in the control variate are evaluated rather than retrieved from a table.
Each triggered refresh recomputes a full gradient at cost \(n\) component-gradient evaluations.

notation.meaning: Component-gradient evaluations during T iterations, excluding separately declared initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Oracle Cost of Bernoulli Snapshot Refreshes
Loopless SVRG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-loop SVRG with Bernoulli snapshot refresh for smooth finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Choose \(x^0=w^0\in\mathbb R^d\), stepsize \(\eta>0\), and refresh probability \(p\in(0,1]\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), sample \(i_k\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), form \(v^k=
abla f_{i_k}(x^k)-
abla f_{i_k}(w^k)+
abla f(w^k)\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta v^k\). Independently set \(w^{k+1}=x^k\) with probability \(p\), and \(w^{k+1}=w^k\) otherwise; whenever the snapshot changes, compute and store \(
abla f(w^{k+1})\). Stop by a prescribed iteration or accuracy rule and output the latest iterate or a specified averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loopless SVRG uses the SVRG control variate every iteration and refreshes its full-gradient snapshot independently with fixed probability.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
The component index and snapshot-refresh coin are sampled independently.
A full gradient is available whenever the snapshot is refreshed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[v^k\mid x^k,w^k]=\nabla f(x^k)\), and the expected number of iterations between snapshot refreshes is \(1/p\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf and the estimator is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the particular snapshot-update ordering, refresh convention, or output rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional order-level linear-convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(L\)-smooth components and a \(\mu\)-strongly convex average, Loopless SVRG with \(p\asymp1/n\) and a suitable \(\eta\asymp1/L\) is reported to contract a Lyapunov function geometrically and require \(O((n+L/\mu)\log(C_0/\varepsilon))\) component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With refresh probability about one over n, Loopless SVRG is reported to match n-plus-condition-number logarithmic complexity without explicit epochs.
assumptions_latex: The selected theorem's update order and parameter constants are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Loopless-SVRG Complexity

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns Bernoulli snapshot renewal, geometric refresh ages, snapshot-dependent variance, and the zero-refresh counterexample. Classical epoch SVRG and proximal updates were excluded to their dedicated leaves. Exact update ordering, Lyapunov certificate, and complexity remain unresolved.

children.title: S2GD Family
children.top_down_role: Snapshot-based methods identified with the S2GD family.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of vanishing variance with a fixed nonoptimal snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=2\), \(f_1(x)=0\), and \(f_2(x)=Lx^2/2\). Then \(x_*=0\). For a fixed snapshot \(w\neq0\), the S2GD estimator at \(x_*\) equals \(Lw/2\) when \(i=1\) and \(-Lw/2\) when \(i=2\). It is unbiased but has variance \(L^2w^2/4>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the optimum, a nonoptimal fixed snapshot can leave strictly positive estimator variance despite unbiasedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Snapshot Persistent Variance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex smooth variance control for the seeded inner estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume every \(f_i\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth, and let \(x_*\) minimize \(f\). For \(v_i(x,w)=
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(w)+
abla f(w)\) with uniform \(i\), \[\mathbb E_i\|v_i(x,w)-
abla f(x)\|^2\leq4L igl(f(x)-f(x_*)+f(w)-f(x_*) igr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The S2GD estimator variance shrinks when both the inner point and snapshot approach an optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: S2GD Control-Variate Variance Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work–memory accounting for the snapshot estimator described by the deferred seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An epoch that computes an exact snapshot full gradient and performs \(m\) single-index corrected inner steps uses \(n+2m\) component-gradient evaluations when each step separately evaluates \(\nabla f_i(y_t)\) and \(\nabla f_i(w)\). If all snapshot component gradients are stored during the full pass, the count becomes \(n+m\), at the cost of \(\Theta(nd)\) vector storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncached S2GD costs one full pass plus two component-gradient evaluations per inner step; caching saves one inner evaluation at gradient-table storage cost.
assumptions_latex: The uncached implementation reevaluates the selected snapshot component gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{IFO}}^{\mathrm{uncached}}=n+2m\), while caching gives \(n+m\) evaluations and \(\Theta(nd)\) storage.
knowledge_statements.title: S2GD Epoch Primitive Work
S2GD Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epoch-based semi-stochastic gradient method for smooth finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). At epoch \(s\), take a snapshot \(w_s\), compute \(g_s=
abla f(w_s)\), and initialize \(y_{s,0}=w_s\). For \(t=0,\ldots,m_s-1\), sample \(i_{s,t}\) uniformly and update \(y_{s,t+1}=y_{s,t}-\eta_s[
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(y_{s,t})-
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(w_s)+g_s]\). Select the next snapshot \(w_{s+1}\) from the inner iterates according to the stated S2GD epoch convention, such as the terminal or a prescribed randomly selected iterate. Stop after a prescribed number of epochs or evaluations and output the designated snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: S2GD alternates full-gradient snapshots with stochastic inner steps using a snapshot-based unbiased gradient correction.
assumptions_latex: Inner component indices are sampled uniformly, conditionally independently of the past.
The epoch lengths \(m_s\) and snapshot-selection convention are specified in advance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits S2GD Family, but the next-snapshot rule is left as a menu of variants and no source identifies which convention belongs to S2GD.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional order-level strongly convex guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(L\)-smooth components and a \(\mu\)-strongly convex average, a standard S2GD parameterization is reported to attain geometric expected objective-gap decay with \(O((n+L/\mu)\log((f(w_0)-f_*)/\varepsilon))\) component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: S2GD is reported to have n-plus-condition-number logarithmic complexity in the smooth strongly convex regime, subject to its exact epoch convention.
assumptions_latex: The selected theorem's stepsize, epoch, and snapshot rules are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex S2GD Linear Complexity
