children.title: S2GD Snapshot Relatives
children.top_down_role: Closely related snapshot methods distinguished from canonical S2GD.

knowledge_statements.title: S2GD Snapshot Relatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Control-variate template shared by S2GD and closely related snapshot methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), a snapshot-relative method maintains an inner point \(x\), a snapshot \(w\), and \(g=
abla f(w)\). Given a sampled index \(i\), its canonical estimator is \(v_i(x,w)=
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(w)+g\), followed by \(x^+=x-\eta v_i(x,w)\). Methods in this template differ only through the schedule for recomputing \((w,g)\), the number or distribution of inner steps, and the rule selecting the next snapshot. Under uniform component sampling, the estimator satisfies \(\mathbb E_i[v_i(x,w)]=
abla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: S2GD relatives share the same snapshot control variate while differing in refresh timing, epoch length, and snapshot selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role is plausible, but the assertion that relatives differ only in three listed features overstates an uncited and undefined family boundary.

children.title: S2GD Epoch-Structure Variants
children.top_down_role: Variants organized by snapshot and epoch scheduling choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional equivalence between random snapshot selection and pre-sampled epoch termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inner iterates \(y_0,\ldots,y_M\) and a probability vector \(q\), selecting \(w^+=y_J\) with \(\mathbb P(J=t)=q_t\) is distributionally equivalent to drawing \(J\) before the epoch, executing exactly \(J\) inner updates, and returning the terminal iterate, provided \(J\) is independent of the component samples used by the executed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random next-snapshot selection can be implemented equivalently as a pre-sampled random epoch length.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is independent of the inner component samples.
Only updates through time \(J\) are required to construct \(y_J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two implementations produce the same distribution for \(w^+\).

notation.meaning: selected output index or random epoch length

knowledge_statements.title: Random Epoch-Length Representation
S2GD Epoch-Structure Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S2GD template with explicit epoch-length and snapshot-output choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At epoch \(s\), compute \(g_s=
abla f(w_s)\), draw or prescribe an inner length \(M_s\geq1\), and set \(y_{s,0}=w_s\). For \(t<M_s\), draw \(i_{s,t}\) uniformly and set \(y_{s,t+1}=y_{s,t}-\eta_s[
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(y_{s,t})-
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(w_s)+g_s]\). An epoch-structure variant specifies a probability vector \((q_{s,0},\ldots,q_{s,M_s})\) and chooses \(w_{s+1}=y_{s,J_s}\), where \(\mathbb P(J_s=t)=q_{s,t}\); terminal-output variants use \(q_{s,M_s}=1\). The stopping rule and reported snapshot are fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epoch variants alter S2GD’s inner-loop length and the distribution used to choose the next snapshot.
assumptions_latex: \(M_s\), \(q_{s,t}\), and \(\eta_s\) are specified for every epoch.
Inner indices are sampled uniformly conditional on the epoch history.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is suitable, but no source supports treating every prescribed distribution over all inner iterates as an S2GD epoch-structure variant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete conditional bias under empty-memory initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=2\), \(f_1(x)=f_2(x)=x^2/2\), \(x^0=1\), and \(a_1^0=a_2^0=0\). After replacing one uniformly selected table entry, the SAG direction is deterministically \(d^0=1/2\), whereas \(\nabla f(x^0)=1\). Thus the first direction is biased by \(-1/2\), even though the identical components produce no sampling variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a zero-initialized table, SAG can be biased even when all components are identical and the direction has no sampling variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Table SAG Bias Example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional mean of the updated gradient-table average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \( ar a^k=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^k\). After drawing \(i_k\) uniformly, form \[d^k= ar a^k+ rac1n igl(
abla f_{i_k}(x^k)-a_{i_k}^k igr).\] Conditional on \(x^k\) and the old table, \[\mathbb E[d^k]=\left(1- rac1night) ar a^k+ rac1n
abla f(x^k).\] Hence the direction is generally biased; it is unbiased exactly when \(n=1\) or \( ar a^k=
abla f(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unlike SAGA, SAG's updated table average is generally biased, with bias determined exactly by the stale table average.
assumptions_latex: All stored vectors and component gradients are finite.

notation.meaning: average stored component gradient before replacement
average gradient table after the sampled replacement

knowledge_statements.title: SAG Conditional Bias Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental representation of the updated gradient-table average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let s^k=\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^k. If the sampled entry is replaced by g_k=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k), then s^{k+1}=s^k+g_k-a_{i_k}^k and the updated SAG direction is d^k=s^{k+1}/n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAG maintains its updated table average by subtracting the overwritten memory and adding the fresh component gradient.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one table entry is replaced at iteration k.
The stored vectors and fresh component gradient are finite.

notation.meaning: sum of stored component gradients before replacement

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental SAG Table-Average Maintenance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variance of the updated SAG table-average direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta_i^k=\nabla f_i(x^k)-a_i^k\), \(\bar\delta^k=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_i^k\), and let \(i_k\) be conditionally uniform. For \(d^k=\bar a^k+n^{-1}\delta_{i_k}^k\), where \(\bar a^k=n^{-1}\sum_i a_i^k\), \[d^k-\mathbb E[d^k\mid x^k,(a_i^k)]=\frac1n(\delta_{i_k}^k-\bar\delta^k),\] and hence \[\mathbb E\!\left[\|d^k-\mathbb E[d^k\mid x^k,(a_i^k)]\|^2\mid x^k,(a_i^k)\right]=\frac1{n^3}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\delta_i^k-\bar\delta^k\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAG’s updated table-average direction has variance equal to the population variance of gradient-memory errors scaled by one over \(n^2\).
assumptions_latex: The component gradients and stored vectors are finite.

notation.meaning: fresh component gradient minus its stored value

knowledge_statements.title: SAG Exact Conditional Variance
SAG Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-table method using the average of stored component gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and stored vectors \(a_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(i_k\) uniformly, set \(a_{i_k}^{k+1}=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)\) and \(a_j^{k+1}=a_j^k\) for \(j\neq i_k\), then update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_k n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^{k+1}\). The stored sum may be maintained incrementally. Stop according to a prescribed iteration or accuracy rule and output the latest or a specified averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAG replaces one stored component gradient per iteration and steps using the average of the updated gradient table.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits SAG and the update is recognizable, but the assumption contains the malformed set \(\{1,,n\}\), while the initialization and update convention have no supporting locator.

children.title: Classical SAGA
children.top_down_role: Canonical SAGA for smooth finite-sum objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary stability boundary inherited from the one-component case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=1\) and \(f_1(x)=Lx^2/2\), the Classical-SAGA estimator is exactly \(v^k=Lx^k\), regardless of its memory value. Hence \(x^{k+1}=(1-\eta L)x^k\). At \(\eta=2/L\) the objective does not decrease, and for \(\eta>2/L\) it increases whenever \(x^k\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical SAGA cannot be stable for arbitrary constant stepsizes: its one-component specialization already has the gradient-descent threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Stepsize Classical-SAGA Instability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact table-error representation for uniform single-index SAGA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Condition on \(x\) and memories \(a_i\), define \(\delta_i=
abla f_i(x)-a_i\) and \( ar\delta=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_i\). For \(v=\delta_I+n^{-1}\sum_i a_i\) with uniform \(I\), \[v-
abla f(x)=\delta_I- ar\delta,\qquad \mathbb E\|v-
abla f(x)\|^2= rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\delta_i- ar\delta\|^2.\] The estimator is exact exactly when all \(\delta_i\) are equal, including when every memory equals its current component gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical SAGA variance is exactly the population variance of the componentwise gradient-memory errors.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is conditionally uniform given \(x\) and the memory table.
All component gradients and memories are finite.

notation.meaning: component-gradient error relative to stored memory

knowledge_statements.title: Classical SAGA Exact Conditional Variance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration state update for the uniform single-index implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With memories a_i^k\in\mathbb R^d and s^k=\sum_i a_i^k, one iteration forms v^k=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)-a_{i_k}^k+s^k/n and updates s^{k+1}=s^k+\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)-a_{i_k}^k. A dense standard implementation therefore uses one fresh component-gradient query and O(d) vector arithmetic per iteration; its explicit gradient table occupies O(nd) auxiliary storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical SAGA uses one fresh component gradient and incrementally updates its memory sum, while retaining an explicit gradient table.
assumptions_latex: Component gradients and memories are dense vectors in \mathbb R^d.
No problem-specific compression or shared representation is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical SAGA Incremental State Cost
Classical SAGA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform single-index SAGA for differentiable finite-sum objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and gradient memories \(a_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(i_k\) uniformly and form \(v^k=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)-a_{i_k}^k+n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^k\). Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv^k\), update \(a_{i_k}^{k+1}=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)\), and leave all other memories unchanged. Maintain the memory average incrementally, stop by a prescribed rule, and output the designated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical SAGA combines a fresh component-gradient difference with the average gradient memory, yielding an unbiased search direction.
assumptions_latex: \(i_k\) is uniform conditional on the iteration history.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Classical SAGA and the displayed estimator is coherent, but no source supports the stated memory initialization and update convention.

children.title: Proximal SAGA
children.top_down_role: SAGA variants for objectives with proximal structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbiased Gradient Does Not Give an Unbiased Proximal Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinearity boundary for interpreting the Proximal-SAGA iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(r=\iota_{[0,\infty)}\), \(x=0\), \(\nabla g(x)=0\), and let \(v\) equal \(1\) or \(-1\) with probability \(1/2\). Although \(\mathbb Ev=0\), for every \(\eta>0\), \[\mathbb E[\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(-\eta v)]=\eta/2\neq0=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(-\eta\mathbb Ev).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased SAGA gradient estimator generally produces a biased proximal iterate because the proximal map is nonlinear.

notation.meaning: convex indicator of the nonnegative half-line

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Gradient Does Not Give an Unbiased Proximal Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of SAGA gradient-estimation error to proximal displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), let \(r\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define \(x_v^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta v)\) and \(x_g^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta
abla g(x))\). Then \[\|x_v^+-x_g^+\|\leq\eta\|v-
abla g(x)\|.\] Consequently, for \(\widehat G_\eta(x;v)=\eta^{-1}(x-x_v^+)\) and \(G_\eta(x)=\eta^{-1}(x-x_g^+)\), \[\|\widehat G_\eta(x;v)-G_\eta(x)\|\leq\|v-
abla g(x)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal nonexpansiveness transfers SAGA gradient-estimation error directly to proximal-step and gradient-mapping error.

notation.meaning: proximal step formed with the SAGA estimator

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Step Perturbation Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order inclusion certified by an estimator-driven proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta v), where r is proper, closed, and convex and \eta>0, define q=(x-x^+)/\eta-v. Then q\in\partial r(x^+) and v+q=(x-x^+)/\eta. This exactly certifies the estimator-based inclusion 0\in v+\partial r(x^+) only when the residual vanishes; it is not by itself a certificate for 0\in\nabla g(x^+)+\partial r(x^+) unless the gradient-estimation and point-displacement errors are controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Proximal-SAGA step supplies an exact regularizer subgradient and an estimator-based inclusion residual, but not automatically a true composite-stationarity certificate.
assumptions_latex: r is proper, closed, and convex.
The proximal point x^+ is evaluated exactly.

notation.meaning: regularizer subgradient certified by the proximal step

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-SAGA Step Inclusion
Proximal SAGA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAGA with a proximal step for a nonsmooth convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+r(x)\), initialize \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}r\) and memories \(a_i^0\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(i_k\) uniformly and compute \(v^k=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)-a_{i_k}^k+n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^k\). Set \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta_k r}(x^k-\eta_kv^k)\), where \(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(z)=\arg\min_u\{r(u)+(2\eta)^{-1}\|u-z\|^2\}\). Finally update \(a_{i_k}^{k+1}=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^k)\), retain the other memories, and output an iterate selected by the prescribed stopping convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal SAGA applies SAGA’s unbiased estimator before a proximal step for the nonsmooth regularizer.
assumptions_latex: \(r:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The sampled index is uniform conditional on the past.

notation.meaning: SAGA estimator of the smooth gradient
proximal mapping of the scaled regularizer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Proximal SAGA, but the update ordering lacks a source and \(\mathcal F_k\) is used in the conclusion without being introduced.

children.title: SAGA Composite-Objective Regimes
children.top_down_role: Objective structures governing the transition from classical to proximal SAGA.

knowledge_statements.title: SAGA Composite-Objective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective structure under which the proximal SAGA update is well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The composite SAGA regime consists of objectives \(F(x)=f(x)+r(x)\), where \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), every \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, and \(r:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map. The smooth convex regime additionally requires convex \(f_i\) with Lipschitz gradients; a strongly convex regime requires \(F\), or the components under the chosen analysis, to satisfy the stated strong-convexity condition. The algorithmic split assigns only \(f_i\) to the stochastic gradient estimator and treats \(r\) through one proximal evaluation per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite SAGA applies when the finite-sum part is differentiable and the remaining proper closed convex term has a computable proximal map.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable.
Any claimed convergence rate separately states smoothness and convexity constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta v)\) is the composite SAGA update whenever \(\eta>0\) and \(v\) estimates \(\nabla f(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the regime leaf, but the uncited strong-convexity clause ambiguously blends objective-level and component-level assumptions from potentially different analyses.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: SAGA with Arbitrary Sampling
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Arbitrary-sampling variants
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: SAGA with Arbitrary Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp feasibility boundary for unbiased arbitrary-sampling corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If index \(i\) has inclusion probability \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)=0\), then \(\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\theta_S^i=0\) almost surely for every finite weighting convention, so \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\theta_S^i]=0\neq1\). Thus universal unbiasedness requires positive inclusion probability for every component with nonzero objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component that is never sampled cannot receive a finite bias correction, so positive inclusion is necessary for universal unbiasedness.
assumptions_latex: Correction weights are finite on sampled subsets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_i=0\Longrightarrow \text{no finite weights satisfy }\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\theta_S^i]=1.

notation.meaning: marginal inclusion probability of index i

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Inclusion Necessity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional second moment induced by subset inclusion and correction weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on \(x\) and memories \(a_i\), put \(\delta_i=\nabla f_i(x)-a_i\), \(I_i=\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\), and assume \(\mathbb E[I_i\theta_S^i]=1\). For \[v=\bar a+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n I_i\theta_S^i\delta_i,\] one has \[\mathbb E\|v-\nabla f(x)\|^2=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^n\left(\mathbb E[I_iI_j\theta_S^i\theta_S^j]-1\right)\langle\delta_i,\delta_j\rangle.\] Marginal inclusion identities determine unbiasedness, whereas joint inclusion moments determine variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary-sampling SAGA variance is governed by the full joint-inclusion law, not marginal probabilities alone.
assumptions_latex: The displayed second moments are finite.
\(x\) and the memory table are fixed under the sampling expectation.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary-Sampling SAGA Covariance Formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal unbiased correction obtained from positive marginal inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a random subset S with p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0, choose \theta_S^i=p_i^{-1} whenever i\in S. Then \mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\theta_S^i]=1, and v=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n a_j+\frac1n\sum_{i\in S}\frac{\nabla f_i(x)-a_i}{p_i} satisfies \mathbb E[v\mid x,(a_i)]=\nabla f(x). Dependence among inclusion indicators does not affect this mean identity but does affect the variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse marginal-inclusion weights give an unbiased SAGA correction for every proper subset sampling, while joint inclusions still govern variance.

notation.meaning: marginal inclusion probability of component i

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-Inverse Arbitrary-Sampling Weights

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Serial and Fixed-Size Specializations of Marginal-Inverse Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reductions of arbitrary-sampling SAGA corrections under common proper samplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For serial sampling with \(\mathbb P(S=\{i\})=p_i>0\), marginal-inverse weighting contributes \((np_i)^{-1}(
abla f_i(x)-a_i)\) to the estimator. For a uniform fixed-size subset of cardinality \(b\), each marginal is \(p_i=b/n\), so \[ rac1n\sum_{i\in S} rac{
abla f_i(x)-a_i}{p_i}= rac1b\sum_{i\in S}(
abla f_i(x)-a_i).\] Both are unbiased specializations, although their joint inclusion laws and variances differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse marginal weights reduce to inverse-probability correction for serial sampling and an ordinary correction average for a uniform fixed-size subset.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-size subset is uniform among subsets of cardinality \(b\).

notation.meaning: sampled correction added to the memory average

knowledge_statements.title: Serial and Fixed-Size Specializations of Marginal-Inverse Weights
Arbitrary-Sampling SAGA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAGA estimator for random subset sampling with bias-correcting weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), and let \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be drawn from a fixed proper sampling. Choose weights \(\theta_S^i\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\theta_S^i]=1\) for every \(i\). With memories \(a_i^k\), form \(v^k=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^k+n^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_k}\theta_{S_k}^i(\nabla f_i(x^k)-a_i^k)\), set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv^k\), and replace \(a_i^{k+1}=\nabla f_i(x^k)\) for \(i\in S_k\), leaving other memories unchanged. Stop by a prescribed rule and output the designated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary-sampling SAGA updates a sampled subset and weights its corrections so the gradient estimator remains unbiased.
assumptions_latex: Every index has positive inclusion probability.
The correction weights satisfy the displayed unbiasedness identities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Arbitrary-Sampling SAGA and the stated weighting identity implies unbiasedness, but the definition of proper sampling and the weighting convention require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Finito Family
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum surrogate methods associated with Finito.

knowledge_statements.title: Finito Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory-point finite-sum method for smooth strongly convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), with each \(f_i\) strongly convex with common modulus \(\mu>0\). Maintain points \(\phi_i^k\). Define \(\bar\phi^k=n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_i^k\) and \(x^k=\bar\phi^k-(\alpha\mu n)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(\phi_i^k)\), where \(\alpha>0\) is prescribed. Sample \(j_k\) uniformly, set \(\phi_{j_k}^{k+1}=x^k\), and retain \(\phi_i^{k+1}=\phi_i^k\) for \(i\neq j_k\). Recompute the maintained averages incrementally, stop by a prescribed criterion, and output the latest constructed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finito stores one point per component, constructs an aggregate point from stored points and gradients, then refreshes one memory point.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
The component index is sampled uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k=\bar\phi^k-(\alpha\mu n)^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(\phi_i^k)\), followed by exactly one memory-point replacement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Finito Family, but the aggregate scaling and unrestricted claim that \(\alpha>0\) is prescribed require source verification against the original algorithmic parameterization.

children.title: MISO Family
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum surrogate methods associated with MISO.

knowledge_statements.title: MISO Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental minimization of stored component surrogate functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), maintain tractable surrogates \(q_i^k:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) and define \(Q^k(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i q_i^k(x)\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(i_k\), build a new surrogate \(q_{i_k}^{k+1}\) from component \(f_{i_k}\) at the current evaluation point according to the selected MISO rule, retain \(q_j^{k+1}=q_j^k\) for \(j\neq i_k\), and set \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x Q^{k+1}(x)\). The surrogate class must make this aggregate minimization computable. Stop by a prescribed iteration or accuracy rule and output the latest aggregate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MISO replaces one stored component surrogate and computes the next iterate by minimizing the average of all current surrogates.
assumptions_latex: Each component admits a surrogate from the selected tractable class.
The average stored surrogate has a computable minimizer.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is plausible, but the surrogate construction is not mathematically specified and no source establishes that this broad template exactly characterizes the MISO family.

children.title: Finito–MISO Surrogate Variants
children.top_down_role: Related surrogate-memory variants spanning the two families.

knowledge_statements.title: Finito–MISO Surrogate Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-surrogate representation linking memory-point Finito and MISO updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given stored points \(\phi_i\) and a curvature parameter \(c>0\), define quadratic component surrogates \(q_i(x)=f_i(\phi_i)+\langle\nabla f_i(\phi_i),x-\phi_i\rangle+(c/2)\|x-\phi_i\|^2\). Their average has the unique minimizer \(x^+=n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_i-(cn)^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(\phi_i)\). A Finito–MISO surrogate variant samples an index \(j\), replaces \(\phi_j\) by the current aggregate minimizer or evaluation point, rebuilds only \(q_j\), and minimizes the updated average. Different variants choose \(c\), sampling, update ordering, and whether the surrogates are required to be lower bounds or majorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic stored surrogates yield Finito’s aggregate formula; variants differ in curvature, sampling, ordering, and surrogate-bound requirements.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is differentiable at its stored point \(\phi_i\).
Only one or a prescribed sampled block of surrogates is replaced per iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the leaf and the quadratic minimizer formula is internally correct, but no source supports the claimed Finito–MISO family boundary or the inclusion of both lower-bound and majorant conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: JacSketch Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic Jacobian-sketching template for smooth finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), let \(G(x)=[\nabla f_1(x),\ldots,\nabla f_n(x)]\), and store \(J^k\in\mathbb R^{d\times n}\). Sample a sketch \(S_k\), form its associated projector \(\Pi_{S_k}\), and choose a bias correction \(\theta_{S_k}\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[\theta_S\Pi_S\mathbf 1]=\mathbf 1\). Set \[J^{k+1}=J^k+(G(x^k)-J^k)\Pi_{S_k},\qquad g^k=\frac1nJ^k\mathbf 1+\frac{\theta_{S_k}}n(G(x^k)-J^k)\Pi_{S_k}\mathbf 1,\] and update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_k g^k\). The output is a prescribed iterate or an iterate selected by the convergence criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: JacSketch updates a sketched portion of a stored gradient Jacobian and uses a bias-corrected residual to construct an unbiased finite-sum gradient estimator.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) is sampled independently conditional on the current state.

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns are component gradients
stored approximation of the gradient Jacobian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the JacSketch family container, and the estimator claim is internally coherent. However, no citation is supplied for the sketch-induced projector convention, Jacobian update, or bias-correction identity; these conventions are source-dependent and materially determine the formula.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator representation inside an epoch initialized by an exact full gradient.

For \(v_0=
abla f(x_0)\) and \(v_t=v_{t-1}+
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1})\), \[v_t=
abla f(x_0)+\sum_{j=1}^t igl(
abla f_{i_j}(x_j)-
abla f_{i_j}(x_{j-1}) igr).\] With \(e_t=v_t-

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within an epoch, SARAH telescopes sampled gradient changes from the initial full gradient; its conditional error is propagated rather than reset until the next refresh.
assumptions_latex: The epoch begins with an exact full-gradient estimator.
Each inner index is conditionally uniform and shared across the two consecutive points.

Let \(e_t=v_t-
abla f(x_t)\), \(v_0=
abla f(x_0)\), and \(v_t=v_{t-1}+
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1})\). Then \[\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t]=\|e_{t-1}\|^2+\mathbb E_i\|\Delta_{i,t}-\Delta_t\|^2,\] where \(\Delta_{i,t}=
abla f_i(x_t)-

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An epoch with an exact full-gradient initialization and \(m\) single-index SARAH corrections uses \(n+2m\) component-gradient evaluations when each correction evaluates its selected component at both consecutive iterates. Thus \(S\) equal-length epochs use \(S(n+2m)\) evaluations, excluding separately charged terminal evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each epoch costs one full pass plus two component-gradient evaluations per recursive inner step.
assumptions_latex: Every epoch starts with an exact full gradient.

Epoch-Based SARAH
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-loop SARAH with deterministic full-gradient epoch refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), initialize an epoch at \(x_{s,0}\) with \(v_{s,0}=
abla f(x_{s,0})\). For \(t=0,\ldots,m-1\), set \(x_{s,t+1}=x_{s,t}-\eta v_{s,t}\), sample \(i_{s,t+1}\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and compute \[v_{s,t+1}=
abla f_{i_{s,t+1}}(x_{s,t+1})-
abla f_{i_{s,t+1}}(x_{s,t})+v_{s,t}.\] Choose the next epoch point \(x_{s+1,0}\) according to the prescribed last-iterate or randomized-inner-iterate rule, refresh its full gradient, and repeat. Return the prescribed final or sampled iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epoch-based SARAH periodically computes a full gradient, then recursively updates its estimator using one component-gradient difference per inner iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and two-loop recursion match the Epoch-Based SARAH container. A primary source with an algorithm-level locator is required to establish the epoch transition and output-selection conventions.

children.title: Loopless SARAH
children.top_down_role: SARAH variants using randomized refresh without explicit epochs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for geometric refresh and bias-contraction identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(p=0\), no full-gradient refresh occurs and inter-refresh time is infinite. If refresh decisions are history-dependent or have varying conditional probabilities, inter-refresh spacings need not be geometric; if decisions are coupled with sampled component indices, the standard conditional-error identity requires a new joint-law calculation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The geometric schedule and simple bias recursion require a positive constant independent refresh probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Loopless Refresh Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loopless SARAH Refresh and Error Laws
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule and conditional first-moment properties of independent Bernoulli full-gradient refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With independent refresh indicators of probability \(p\in(0,1]\), the number \(T\) of iterations from one refresh through the next satisfies \(\Pr(T=t)=(1-p)^{t-1}p\) for \(t\ge1\), so \(\mathbb E[T]=p^{-1}\). If a refresh sets \(v^{k+1}=\nabla f(x^{k+1})\) and a nonrefresh step uses the same-index SARAH correction, then for \(e^k=v^k-\nabla f(x^k)\), \[\mathbb E[e^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k,x^{k+1}]=(1-p)e^k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent loopless refreshes have geometric spacing and contract the estimator's conditional bias by one minus the refresh probability.
assumptions_latex: Refresh indicators are independent Bernoulli variables with \(p\in(0,1]\).
Nonrefresh component indices are conditionally uniform and shared at consecutive points.
knowledge_statements.title: Loopless SARAH Refresh and Error Laws

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-moment recursion induced by exact Bernoulli refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e^k=v^k-
abla f(x^k)\). If iteration \(k+1\) refreshes exactly with probability \(p\), then \(e^{k+1}=0\); otherwise it applies a same-index SARAH correction. Hence \[\mathbb E[\|e^{k+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k,x^{k+1}]=(1-p)\left(\|e^k\|^2+\mathbb E_i\|\Delta_i^k-\Delta^k\|^2ight),\] where \(\Delta_i^k=
abla f_i(x^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x^k)\). Under average \(L\)-smoothness this is at most \((1-p)(\|e^k\|^2+L^2\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact loopless refresh annihilates estimator error; a nonrefresh step propagates it and adds path-difference variance.
assumptions_latex: The refresh indicator is conditionally independent Bernoulli(p).
A refresh computes the exact full gradient.
Nonrefresh indices are conditionally uniform and used at both consecutive points.
knowledge_statements.title: Loopless SARAH Mean-Square Error Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected component-gradient cost under exact Bernoulli full-gradient refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a refresh computes all \(n\) component gradients and a nonrefresh correction evaluates \(b\) components at both consecutive iterates, then \[\mathbb E[N_{\mathrm{IFO}}^{\mathrm{transition}}]=pn+2(1-p)b.\] Including an initial full gradient, \(K\) transitions cost \[n+K\bigl[pn+2(1-p)b\bigr]\] in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loopless SARAH trades occasional full gradients against two evaluations per correction component.
assumptions_latex: Refresh decisions are Bernoulli with probability \(p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Loopless SARAH Expected Oracle Cost
Loopless SARAH
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-loop SARAH with independent randomized full-gradient refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), initialize \(x^0\) and \(v^0=
abla f(x^0)\). At iteration \(k\), set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta v^k\). Independently draw \(B_{k+1}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\). If \(B_{k+1}=1\), set \(v^{k+1}=
abla f(x^{k+1})\); otherwise sample \(i_{k+1}\) uniformly and set \[v^{k+1}=v^k+
abla f_{i_{k+1}}(x^{k+1})-
abla f_{i_{k+1}}(x^k).\] Stop under the prescribed budget or accuracy rule and return the designated current or sampled iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loopless SARAH replaces fixed epochs by Bernoulli full-gradient refreshes and otherwise performs the usual recursive component-gradient correction.
assumptions_latex: Indices and refresh variables are conditionally independent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the Loopless SARAH leaf, and the geometric refresh-spacing conclusion follows from the stated independent Bernoulli schedule. A specific primary citation is still required to support the method name, update ordering, independence convention, and output rule.

children.title: SARAH Refresh-Schedule Regimes
children.top_down_role: Refresh organizations connecting epoch-based and loopless designs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the periodic-versus-independent-Bernoulli comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The geometric-spacing formulas require a constant positive refresh probability and independent decisions. At \(p=0\) the expected spacing is infinite. State-dependent, history-dependent, or time-varying probabilities generally produce neither independent nor identically distributed geometric gaps, even if their long-run average refresh frequency equals \(1/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching a long-run refresh frequency does not make an adaptive schedule geometrically distributed or equivalent to fixed epochs.
knowledge_statements.title: Nongeometric Refresh Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Periodic and Bernoulli Refresh Cost and Tail Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-level comparison under component-gradient accounting, independent of a particular SARAH convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a full refresh cost \(n\) component-gradient evaluations. A periodic schedule refreshing once every \(m\) iterations has amortized refresh cost \(n/m\) per iteration. An independent Bernoulli schedule with probability \(p\) has expected refresh cost \(pn\) per iteration. Setting \(p=1/m\) matches these averages. For Bernoulli inter-refresh spacing \(T\), \[\Pr(T=t)=(1-p)^{t-1}p,\quad \operatorname{Var}(T)=\frac{1-p}{p^2},\quad \Pr(T>q)=(1-p)^q,\] whereas periodic spacing is deterministically \(m\) and has zero variance. Equal average frequency therefore does not imply equal gap tails or iterate distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing p equal to one over m matches expected refresh work, but randomized refreshes retain geometric variance and tails absent from fixed epochs.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\), \(p\in(0,1]\), and Bernoulli refresh decisions are independent.
A full-gradient refresh is charged as \(n\) component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.title: Periodic and Bernoulli Refresh Cost and Tail Comparison
SARAH Refresh-Schedule Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence and cost parameters for periodic and randomized SARAH refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A SARAH refresh schedule partitions iterations into refresh times, at which \(v^k=
abla f(x^k)\), and recursive times, at which \(v^k=v^{k-1}+
abla f_{i_k}(x^k)-
abla f_{i_k}(x^{k-1})\). A periodic schedule with spacing \(m\) has exactly one refresh per \(m\) iterations. An independent Bernoulli schedule with probability \(p\) has geometrically distributed spacings with mean \(p^{-1}\). Thus \(p=1/m\) matches the expected refresh frequency, although the two schedules do not generate identical trajectories or identical tail behavior for epoch lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic spacing m and Bernoulli probability p equalize average refresh frequency when p=1/m, but their epoch-length distributions and algorithm trajectories differ.
assumptions_latex: Bernoulli refresh decisions are independent with \(p\in(0,1]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role is appropriate for a refresh-schedule comparison. The periodic-versus-geometric distinction is mathematically precise, but the record has no source supporting its placement and terminology as SARAH refresh-schedule regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-refresh ProxSARAH epoch costs one full gradient, two component-gradient evaluations per correction, and one proximal evaluation per inner step.

Proximal SARAH

Consider \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+r(x)\), where the component functions are differentiable and the proximal map of \(r\) is computable. At each epoch start, set \(v_{s,0}=

abla f_{i_{s,t+1}}(x_{s,t+1})-
abla f_{i_{s,t+1}}(x_{s,t}).\] Refresh the full gradient at the prescribed epoch boundary. Return the designated iterate, commonly selected randomly from all proximal updates in nonconvex analysis.

assumptions_latex: \(r:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous with a computable proximal map.

children.title: ZeroSARAH
children.top_down_role: SARAH-style variants avoiding initial full-gradient computation.

knowledge_statements.title: ZeroSARAH
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-gradient-free SARAH variant with component-gradient memory and mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), maintain \(v^{k-1}\) and memories \(y_i^{k-1}\). Sample a batch \(I_k\) of size \(b_k\), evaluate its component gradients at \(x^k\) and \(x^{k-1}\), and set \[v^k= rac1{b_k}\sum_{i\in I_k} igl(
abla f_i(x^k)-
abla f_i(x^{k-1}) igr)+(1-\lambda_k)v^{k-1}+\lambda_k\left[ rac1{b_k}\sum_{i\in I_k} igl(
abla f_i(x^{k-1})-y_i^{k-1} igr)+ rac1n\sum_{j=1}^n y_j^{k-1}ight].\] Set \(y_i^k=
abla f_i(x^k)\) for sampled indices, retain other memories, and update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ZeroSARAH combines recursive gradient differences with a memory-based correction, allowing initialization and subsequent operation without computing a full gradient.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^k\) is computable using sampled component gradients and stored memories without evaluating \(\nabla f(x^k)\).

children.title: Full-Gradient-Free SARAH Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum settings motivating SARAH variants without full-gradient initialization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Gradient Freedom Does Not Bound Cumulative Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating the absence of an exact full-gradient operation from component-gradient-equivalent cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\). A schedule may query one proper singleton batch in each of \(n\) consecutive iterations, at possibly different iterates. It performs \(n\) component-gradient evaluations—one full-gradient equivalent—without ever prescribing all \(n\) component gradients at a common iterate or forming an exact full gradient. Repeating the schedule gives arbitrarily many full-gradient equivalents while remaining full-gradient-free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-gradient-free method can cumulatively spend one or many full-gradient equivalents; the term describes operations, not total work.
assumptions_latex: Full-gradient-free means no prescribed exact aggregate of every component at one common iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Gradient Freedom Does Not Bound Cumulative Work

assumptions_latex: Oracle cost counts individual component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Every prescribed refresh batch is proper and no exact aggregate is formed}\Longrightarrow\text{the regime is full-gradient-free}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational criterion excluding every exact finite-sum gradient evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), a SARAH-type regime is full-gradient-free if every estimator initialization and refresh uses batches \(I_k\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), component-gradient memories, or both, and no step forms \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(x)\) at a common iterate \(x\). Equivalently, under component-gradient oracle accounting, the algorithm contains no iteration whose prescribed operation requires all \(n\) component gradients solely to construct an exact full-gradient refresh. The condition concerns the algorithmic prescription, not the accidental event that randomized batches collectively cover all indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is full-gradient-free when neither initialization nor refresh explicitly evaluates every component gradient at one iterate to form the exact finite-sum gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Gradient-Free SARAH Regimes

children.title: SPIDER Family
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum methods associated with SPIDER estimators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator-error accumulation between refreshes under same-batch gradient differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a refresh at \(k_0\) produces \(v^{k_0}\), and for \(k>k_0\), \[v^k=v^{k-1}+ rac1b\sum_{i\in S_k}(
abla f_i(x^k)-
abla f_i(x^{k-1})),\] with conditionally independent uniform with-replacement batches. Writing \(e^k=v^k-
abla f(x^k)\), average \(L\)-smoothness gives \[\mathbb E\|e^k\|^2\le \mathbb E\|e^{k_0}\|^2+ rac{L^2}{b}\sum_{j=k_0+1}^k\mathbb E\|x^j-x^{j-1}\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Between refreshes, SPIDER estimator error is bounded by refresh error plus mini-batch-scaled squared path length.
assumptions_latex: Difference batches are conditionally independent and uniform with replacement.
Each sampled batch is evaluated at both consecutive points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-definedness and certification boundary for normalized SPIDER steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv^k/\|v^k\|\) is undefined when \(v^k=0\). Moreover, \(v^k=0\) does not alone certify stationarity: an estimator may be zero while \(
abla f(x^k)
eq0\). A zero-estimator stopping rule is sound only when exactness or a quantitative error bound implies \(\|
abla f(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized SPIDER step needs an explicit zero-estimator action, and stopping at zero is unsafe without estimator-error control.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^k=0\not\Rightarrow\nabla f(x^k)=0\) without exactness or estimator-error control.

SPIDER Family

abla f_i(x^k)\), using the full set or a prescribed large batch. Otherwise sample a mini-batch \(S_k\) and set \[v^k=v^{k-1}+ rac1{|S_k|}\sum_{i\in S_k} igl(

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SPIDER periodically estimates the gradient with a large batch and recursively transports it using mini-batch gradient differences along the iterate path.

children.title: SpiderBoost Family
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum methods associated with SpiderBoost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-step obstruction for the unnormalized update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=Lx^2/2\) and the exact estimator \(v=\nabla f(x)\), the update is \(x^+=(1-\eta L)x\). If \(\eta=2/L\), the objective is unchanged, and if \(\eta>2/L\), it increases. Recursive variance reduction therefore cannot compensate for an arbitrarily large unnormalized step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact estimator fails to decrease a scalar quadratic when the unnormalized step reaches or exceeds the classical stability threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Stepsize Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step relation supporting an unnormalized recursive-estimator step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth and \(x^+=x-\eta v\), then \[f(x^+)\leq f(x)-\frac\eta2\|\nabla f(x)\|^2-\frac\eta2(1-L\eta)\|v\|^2+\frac\eta2\|v-\nabla f(x)\|^2.\] Hence, for \(0<\eta\leq1/L\), estimator mean-square error controls the loss term without normalizing \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothness explains why SpiderBoost can use an ordinary constant-order step: estimator error enters additively in the descent bound.
knowledge_statements.title: SpiderBoost Descent–Error Inequality
SpiderBoost Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SPIDER recursion coupled to an unnormalized constant-order descent step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), initialize or periodically refresh \(v^k\) by a full gradient or prescribed large-batch gradient. Between refreshes, sample a mini-batch \(S_k\) and compute \[v^k=v^{k-1}+\frac1{|S_k|}\sum_{i\in S_k}\bigl(\nabla f_i(x^k)-\nabla f_i(x^{k-1})\bigr).\] Perform the unnormalized update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta v^k\), with \(\eta\) chosen on the order allowed by smoothness rather than scaled by the target stationarity tolerance. Return an iterate selected by the prescribed terminal or randomized rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SpiderBoost uses the SPIDER recursive estimator with an ordinary unnormalized gradient step whose stepsize is chosen at the smoothness scale.
assumptions_latex: Mini-batches follow the prescribed uniform sampling rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits SpiderBoost, and the unnormalized update correctly captures its intended distinction from normalized SPIDER variants. The smoothness-scale stepsize, refresh rule, and output convention require a specific primary-source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional order-level nonconvex finite-sum guarantee.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reported SpiderBoost order is n plus square-root-n over epsilon squared, but the exact theorem conventions require a primary source.

The selected theorem's component assumptions and parameter rules hold.

children.title: SNVRG Family
children.top_down_role: Nested variance-reduced methods associated with SNVRG.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform variance control without levelwise batch–distance balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Average smoothness alone does not make a nested estimator uniformly accurate. If a level permits \(\|x^{(\ell)}-x^{(\ell-1)}\|^2/|B_\ell|\) to be arbitrarily large, the standard variance bound contains the uncontrolled term \(L^2\|x^{(\ell)}-x^{(\ell-1)}\|^2/|B_\ell|\); nesting alone therefore supplies no uniform small-error guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale reference paired with too small a level batch can dominate the estimator error.
assumptions_latex: Only average \(L\)-smoothness and the seeded independent-level estimator are assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbounded levelwise distance-to-batch ratios preclude a uniform guarantee from the standard variance bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Staleness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance allocation across independently sampled nested correction levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the seeded nested estimator, set \(\Delta_{\ell,i}=
abla f_i(x^{(\ell)})-
abla f_i(x^{(\ell-1)})\). Conditional on fixed reference points, mutually independent uniform with-replacement batches satisfy \[\mathbb E\|v-
abla f(x^{(K)})\|^2= rac{\operatorname{Var}_i(
abla f_i(x^{(0)}))}{|B_0|}+\sum_{\ell=1}^K rac{\operatorname{Var}_i(\Delta_{\ell,i})}{|B_\ell|}.\] Under average \(L\)-smoothness this is at most the base term plus \(L^2\sum_{\ell=1}^K\|x^{(\ell)}-x^{(\ell-1)}\|^2/|B_\ell|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent nesting levels contribute additive variance, linking each level's batch size to the separation of its reference points.
assumptions_latex: Level batches are mutually independent and uniform with replacement.
Reference points are fixed conditional on the history for this estimator evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Estimator Variance Decomposition

assumptions_latex: Batches at each level obey the prescribed unbiased sampling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[v\mid x^{(0)},\ldots,x^{(K)}]=\nabla f(x^{(K)})\) under unbiased levelwise sampling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested variance reduction with multiple reference points and refresh scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Maintain nested reference points \(x^{(0)},\ldots,x^{(K)}\), with \(x^{(K)}=x\), and independently sampled batches \(B_0,\ldots,B_K\). Construct \[v= rac1{|B_0|}\sum_{i\in B_0}
abla f_i(x^{(0)})+\sum_{\ell=1}^K rac1{|B_\ell|}\sum_{i\in B_\ell} igl(
abla f_i(x^{(\ell)})-
abla f_i(x^{(\ell-1)}) igr),\qquad x^+=x-\eta v.\] Refresh level \(\ell\) and all finer levels according to its prescribed nested period; output the iterate selected by the method's randomized or terminal rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SNVRG telescopes gradient estimates across several reference levels, refreshing coarse levels rarely and fine levels frequently before taking a descent step.

children.title: Recursive-Family Applicability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes distinguishing the three recursive families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative error-budget condition for recursive estimators between refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a refresh at \(r\) satisfies \(\mathbb E\|v_r-\nabla f(x_r)\|^2\leq\sigma_r^2\), then under the recursive error identity and average \(L\)-smoothness, \[\mathbb E\|v_k-\nabla f(x_k)\|^2\leq\sigma_r^2+L^2\sum_{t=r+1}^k\frac{\mathbb E\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|^2}{|S_t|}.\] Thus the interval through \(k\) meets root-mean-square error budget \(\delta\) whenever the right-hand side is at most \(\delta^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive regime is admissible when refresh error plus accumulated batch-scaled path drift stays within the estimator-error budget.
assumptions_latex: Same sampled components are evaluated at consecutive points.
Correction batches satisfy the stated conditional sampling rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Refresh–Drift Applicability Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of vanishing correction noise without same-index coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For independent uniform indices \(i,j\), \[\operatorname{Var}(

abla f_i(x))\), which can be positive even though the iterate displacement is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent indices destroy the vanishing-difference property: a zero step can inject twice the component-gradient variance.
assumptions_latex: Component gradients have finite second moments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional error propagation for same-sample recursive gradient-difference estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_k=v_{k-1}+|S_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_k}(
abla f_i(x_k)-
abla f_i(x_{k-1}))\), with \(S_k\) sampled uniformly with replacement conditional on \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\). If \(e_k=v_k-
abla f(x_k)\) and \(\Delta_i=
abla f_i(x_k)-
abla f_i(x_{k-1})\), then \[\mathbb E[\|e_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]=\|e_{k-1}\|^2+ rac1{|S_k|}\mathbb E_i\|\Delta_i-\mathbb E_j\Delta_j\|^2.\] Under average \(L\)-smoothness, the added term is at most \(L^2\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|^2/|S_k|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled recursive correction adds only the variance of a same-component gradient difference, which average smoothness bounds by batch-scaled squared step length.

notation.meaning: history before the correction batch is sampled

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Estimator Error Identity
Recursive-Family Applicability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions supporting recursive gradient-difference variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A recursive finite-sum estimator is applicable when component-gradient differences \(
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(y)\) are available under coupled sampling and their mean-square variation is controlled along algorithmic steps. A standard sufficient condition is average smoothness: \[ rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(y)\|^2\leq L^2\|x-y\|^2\qquad	ext{for all }x,y\in\mathbb R^d.\] Together with periodic or randomized refreshes, this condition controls accumulation of recursive estimator error. Convexity is not required for defining SPIDER-, SARAH-, or PAGE-type recursions, although particular convergence guarantees may impose convexity, bounded variance, or additional regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursive variance reduction applies when coupled component-gradient differences can be sampled and their mean-square change is controlled; convexity depends on the desired guarantee, not the recursion itself.
assumptions_latex: The same sampled index can be evaluated at consecutive or reference iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n^{-1}\sum_i\|\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla f_i(y)\|^2\leq L^2\|x-y\|^2\) controls recursive difference noise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is suitable for an applicability-regime leaf, and the average-smoothness inequality is explicitly quantified. A recursive-method source is required to support the broader claim that this condition controls accumulated estimator error across the named families and to delimit which convergence regimes require additional assumptions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal boundaries for the standard PAGE conditional identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(p=0\), no refresh ever removes initialization error; at \(p=1\), PAGE reduces to repeated refresh estimation and has no recursive branch. Biased refresh batches or biased gradient-difference batches add their conditional biases to the error recursion, and independently sampled batches at the two correction points lose same-batch variance cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate refresh probabilities and biased or improperly coupled batches change the defining PAGE error recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: PAGE Sampling Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional first-moment identity for unbiased refresh batches and same-batch gradient-difference corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e^k=g^k-
abla f(x^k)\). If the refresh estimator is conditionally unbiased at \(x^{k+1}\), the correction batch is conditionally unbiased for \(
abla f(x^{k+1})-
abla f(x^k)\), and refresh occurs independently with probability \(p\), then \[\mathbb E[e^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k,x^{k+1}]=(1-p)e^k.\] PAGE estimators therefore need not be conditionally unbiased at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PAGE refresh clears conditional bias in expectation, while a recursive correction carries the preceding bias; averaging the branches contracts it by one minus the refresh probability.
assumptions_latex: Refresh and correction batches are conditionally unbiased under the declared filtration.
The refresh indicator is conditionally independent with probability \(p\in(0,1]\).
The same correction batch is evaluated at both consecutive iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: PAGE Conditional Error Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-moment identity for PAGE refresh and recursive branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e^k=g^k-\nabla f(x^k)\). Suppose the refresh branch has conditionally centered error \(\rho_{k+1}\), while the correction branch gives \(e^{k+1}=e^k+\delta_{k+1}\) with conditionally centered \(\delta_{k+1}\). If refresh occurs conditionally independently with probability \(p\), then \[\mathbb E[\|e^{k+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k,x^{k+1}]=p\,\mathbb E\|\rho_{k+1}\|^2+(1-p)\left(\|e^k\|^2+\mathbb E\|\delta_{k+1}\|^2\right).\] For an independent uniform with-replacement same-batch correction of size \(b'\), average \(L\)-smoothness gives \(\mathbb E\|\delta_{k+1}\|^2\le L^2\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2/b'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PAGE resets estimator error to refresh variance with probability p and otherwise carries old error plus correction variance.
assumptions_latex: The refresh and correction estimators are conditionally unbiased.
The refresh indicator is conditionally independent.
The correction batch is sampled uniformly with replacement and used at both consecutive iterates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-gradient cost of the PAGE refresh-or-correction transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a refresh batch has size \(b\), a correction batch has size \(b'\) and is evaluated at both consecutive iterates, and refresh occurs with probability \(p\), then \[\mathbb E[N_{\mathrm{IFO}}^{\mathrm{transition}}]=pb+2(1-p)b'.\] Excluding initialization, \(K\) transitions cost \(K[pb+2(1-p)b']\) in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PAGE refresh costs b component gradients, while a correction costs two evaluations for each of its b-prime components.
assumptions_latex: Each correction component is evaluated at both consecutive iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: PAGE Expected Per-Transition Oracle Cost

assumptions_latex: Refresh and correction batches follow the prescribed unbiased sampling schemes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g^{k+1}\) is a refresh estimator with probability \(p\) and a recursive correction with probability \(1-p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic gradient estimation with randomized refresh and recursive correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), initialize \(x^0\) and a prescribed batch estimator \(g^0\). Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta g^k\). Independently, with probability \(p\), sample a refresh batch \(I_{k+1}\) and set \[g^{k+1}= rac1{|I_{k+1}|}\sum_{i\in I_{k+1}}
abla f_i(x^{k+1});\] otherwise sample a correction batch \(J_{k+1}\) and set \[g^{k+1}=g^k+ rac1{|J_{k+1}|}\sum_{i\in J_{k+1}} igl(
abla f_i(x^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x^k) igr).\] Stop under the prescribed budget or stationarity rule and return the designated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PAGE probabilistically chooses between a fresh batch-gradient estimate and a cheaper recursive gradient-difference correction after each primal update.
knowledge_statements.title: PAGE Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for the exact conditional-error recursion of a finite-sum STORM correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If independent indices \(i_t\) and \(j_t\) replace the shared index in \(\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)-(1-a_t)\nabla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1})\), the two component terms no longer form a same-component gradient difference. The conditional-bias identity may remain after averaging, but the standard mean-square control by \(\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|^2\) does not follow from component smoothness because an additional cross-component sampling variance remains even when \(x_t=x_{t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent samples can preserve a mean identity while destroying the same-sample variance cancellation used by STORM analysis.
assumptions_latex: At least two component gradients differ at some common point.
The two correction indices are sampled independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Same-Sample Coupling Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Bias Recursion for the STORM Estimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator identity for the displayed same-sample finite-sum STORM recursion; it does not select a particular stepsize policy or convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e_t=v_t-
abla F(x_t)\). For the recursion \(v_t=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)+(1-a_t)(v_{t-1}-
abla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1}))\), conditionally uniform sampling gives \[\mathbb E[e_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t]=(1-a_t)e_{t-1}.\] Thus the estimator is generally biased conditionally, with its conditional bias contracted by \(1-a_t\); it is conditionally unbiased at step \(t\) when \(a_t=1\) or \(e_{t-1}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The STORM recursion contracts, rather than generally eliminates, the previous estimator's conditional bias.
assumptions_latex: \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\) and every \(f_i\) is differentiable at the queried points.
\(i_t\) is conditionally uniform and the same index is used at \(x_t\) and \(x_{t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Bias Recursion for the STORM Estimator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error decomposition for the same-sample finite-sum STORM estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e_t=v_t-
abla F(x_t)\), \(\xi_i(x)=
abla f_i(x)-
abla F(x)\), and \(v_t=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)+(1-a_t)(v_{t-1}-
abla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1}))\). Then \[\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t]=(1-a_t)^2\|e_{t-1}\|^2+\mathbb E_i\|a_t\xi_i(x_t)+(1-a_t)(\xi_i(x_t)-\xi_i(x_{t-1}))\|^2.\] If \(\mathbb E_i\|\xi_i(x)\|^2\le\sigma^2\) and \(\mathbb E_i\|
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(y)\|^2\le L^2\|x-y\|^2\), the final term is at most \(2a_t^2\sigma^2+2(1-a_t)^2L^2\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: STORM trades contraction of inherited estimator error against fresh sampling noise and same-sample path variation.
assumptions_latex: i_t\text{ is conditionally uniform and is used at both }x_t\text{ and }x_{t-1}.
knowledge_statements.title: STORM Conditional Mean-Square Error Recursion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Momentum Weight Leaves Estimator Noise at a Noninterpolating Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise-floor boundary for the finite-sum STORM estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1(x)=	frac12(x-1)^2\), \(f_2(x)=	frac12(x+1)^2\), and \(F=(f_1+f_2)/2\), whose minimizer is \(x^*=0\). Suppose \(x_t=x_{t-1}=0\), \(v_{t-1}=
abla F(0)=0\), and use fixed \(a\in(0,1]\) in the same-sample STORM recursion. Then \[v_t=a
abla f_{i_t}(0)\in\{-a,a\},\qquad \mathbb E[v_t]=0,\qquad \mathbb E|v_t-
abla F(0)|^2=a^2.\] Hence a fixed positive refresh weight injects nonvanishing estimator variance at a noninterpolating optimum even when the preceding estimator is exact and the iterate does not move.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a noninterpolating optimum, a fixed positive STORM refresh weight creates a persistent estimator-noise floor.
assumptions_latex: The two components are sampled uniformly.
The same sampled component is used at the two equal points.
\(a\in(0,1]\) is fixed and the preceding estimator is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Momentum Weight Leaves Estimator Noise at a Noninterpolating Optimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Per-Iteration Component-Gradient Cost of the Single-Sample STORM Recursion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact oracle accounting for the table-free same-sample finite-sum STORM estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the recursion \[v_t=\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)+(1-a_t)\bigl(v_{t-1}-\nabla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1})\bigr),\] each iteration \(t\ge1\) evaluates the sampled component gradient at two points. If \(v_0\) uses one component-gradient evaluation and no cached component gradients supply later evaluations, producing \(v_0,\ldots,v_{T-1}\) costs exactly \[N_{\mathrm{IFO}}(T)=1+2(T-1)=2T-1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A table-free single-sample STORM run uses two component-gradient evaluations per recursive update after a one-call initialization.
assumptions_latex: The same sampled component is evaluated at both consecutive points.
No cached component gradient supplies either evaluation.

notation.meaning: Component-gradient evaluations used to construct T estimators.

Finite-Sum STORM-Type Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical single-sample STORM recursion for a differentiable finite sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\). Choose \(x_0\), sample \(i_0\), and set \(v_0=
abla f_{i_0}(x_0)\). For \(t\geq1\), choose \(a_t\in(0,1]\), sample \(i_t\) uniformly, and compute \[v_t=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)+(1-a_t) igl(v_{t-1}-
abla f_{i_t}(x_{t-1}) igr),\qquad x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t v_t.\] The same index \(i_t\) is used at both points in the correction. Stop according to a prescribed budget and output either the final iterate or an iterate sampled from \(\{x_t\}\) under a declared rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: STORM recursively blends the previous estimator with a same-sample gradient difference, then takes a stochastic-gradient step.
assumptions_latex: The sampled index \(i_t\) is conditionally uniform given the past.
Stepsizes satisfy \(\eta_t>0\) and momentum weights satisfy \(a_t\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t\) is the STORM-type recursive estimator used in the update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t v_t\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical geometric convergence and component-gradient work for a standard proximal snapshot regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every \(f_i\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth, \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable, and \(\Phi=F+r\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. For a standard proximal-SVRG variant with stepsize \(\eta=\Theta(L^{-1})\), epoch length \(m=\Theta(L/\mu)\), and a snapshot-output rule covered by its contraction theorem, there is \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\mathbb E[\Phi(\widetilde x_s)-\Phi_\star]\le\rho^s[\Phi(\widetilde x_0)-\Phi_\star].\] Hence \(O((n+L/\mu)\log((\Phi(\widetilde x_0)-\Phi_\star)/\varepsilon))\) component-gradient evaluations suffice for expected objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under component convexity and smoothness plus composite strong convexity, a standard proximal-SVRG variant contracts geometrically with order n plus condition number work per logarithmic accuracy factor.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This proximal-SVRG variant starts each epoch at its snapshot, computes one full snapshot gradient, performs corrected proximal steps, and refreshes to the average inner iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sufficient contraction condition for the averaged-snapshot algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume every f_i is convex and L-smooth, r is proper, closed, and convex, and \Phi=F+r is \mu-strongly convex. For Averaged-Snapshot Proximal SVRG, let 0<\eta<1/(4L) and define \rho=\frac{1}{\mu\eta(1-4L\eta)m}+\frac{4L\eta(m+1)}{(1-4L\eta)m}. If \rho<1, then \mathbb E[\Phi(\widetilde x_{s+1})-\Phi_\star]\le\rho\,\mathbb E[\Phi(\widetilde x_s)-\Phi_\star]. Consequently, S\ge\left\lceil\log((\Phi(\widetilde x_0)-\Phi_\star)/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil epochs suffice for expected gap at most \varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical Lyapunov contraction for uniform proximal table variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(f_i\) be convex and \(L\)-smooth, let \(r\) be proper, closed, convex, and proximable, and suppose \(\Phi=F+r\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. For a standard uniformly sampled proximal-SAGA variant with stepsize \(\eta\le c_0/L\), there exist universal constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and a Lyapunov function \(\mathcal L_t\) combining primal and table errors such that \[\mathbb E[\mathcal L_t]\le\bigl(1-c_1\min\{1/n,\mu/L\}\bigr)^t\mathcal L_0.\] Consequently \(O((n+L/\mu)\log(\mathcal L_0/\varepsilon))\) component-gradient and proximal evaluations suffice for Lyapunov error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform proximal SAGA converges linearly under component smoothness and composite strong convexity, with order n plus condition number times logarithmic accuracy work.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable.
Indices are sampled uniformly and the stepsize lies in the selected proximal-SAGA contraction regime.

notation.meaning: A standard variant-specific Lyapunov function combining primal and table errors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining state representation of proximal SAGA-type table methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proximal table method maintains stored component gradients \(y_i^t=\nabla f_i(\alpha_i^t)\) and their mean \(\bar y_t=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i^t\). If only the sampled entry \(i_t\) changes, then the aggregate is maintained exactly by \[\bar y_{t+1}=\bar y_t+\frac1n\bigl(y_{i_t}^{t+1}-y_{i_t}^t\bigr).\] This persistent state distinguishes table methods from epoch snapshots and recursive difference estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A table method persistently stores one reference gradient per component and updates their exact running mean when one sampled entry changes.
assumptions_latex: Only the sampled table entry changes at an iteration.
\(\bar y_t\) initially equals the mean of the stored table.

notation.meaning: Persistent stored gradient for component i.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(i_t\) be sampled conditionally with probabilities \(p_i>0\), let \(y_i^t\) be stored component gradients, and let \(\bar y_t=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i^t\). Then \[v_t=\frac{\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)-y_{i_t}^t}{np_{i_t}}+\bar y_t\] satisfies \[\mathbb E[v_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=\nabla F(x_t).\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal SAGA-type method with a table of component-gradient reference values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical nonconvex composite complexity for an exact-refresh proximal SPIDER regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi=F+r\) be bounded below, where \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable, and suppose \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla f_i(y)\|^2\le L^2\|x-y\|^2\). For a standard exact-refresh proximal SPIDER variant using refresh cost \(n\), refresh period and inner minibatch size \(\Theta(\sqrt n)\), and stepsize \(\Theta(L^{-1})\), a randomized output \(x_R\) can satisfy \(\mathbb E\|G_\eta(x_R)\|\le\varepsilon\) after \(O\!\left(n+\sqrt n\,L(\Phi(x_0)-\inf\Phi)\varepsilon^{-2}\right)\) component-gradient evaluations. The number of proximal evaluations is \(O\!\left(L(\Phi(x_0)-\inf\Phi)\varepsilon^{-2}\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-refresh proximal SPIDER reaches expected proximal-gradient norm epsilon using order n plus square-root n times epsilon-to-the-minus-two component gradients, while proximal calls scale with the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable.
The selected variant uses exact full-gradient refreshes and its declared randomized output rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_t\) contain \(b\) conditionally independent uniform indices and set \(v_t=v_{t-1}+b^{-1}\sum_{i\in B_t}(
abla f_i(x_t)-
abla f_i(x_{t-1}))\). With \(e_t=v_t-
abla F(x_t)\) and \(\Delta_i=
abla f_i(x_t)-
abla f_i(x_{t-1})\), \[\mathbb E_t[e_t]=e_{t-1},\qquad \mathbb E_t\|e_t\|^2=\|e_{t-1}\|^2+ rac1b\mathbb E_i\|\Delta_i-\mathbb E_j\Delta_j\|^2.\] Thus the update preserves any preceding conditional bias and adds the minibatch variance of component-gradient differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive difference update preserves its preceding conditional bias and adds exactly the current minibatch difference variance to its conditional mean-square error.
assumptions_latex: The minibatch consists of \(b\) conditionally independent uniform samples with replacement.

For \(\Phi(x)=F(x)+r(x)\), \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), fix \(\eta>0\), refresh period \(q\), minibatch size \(b\), and horizon \(T\). For \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), set \[v_t= egin{cases}
abla F(x_t),&t\equiv0\pmod q,\v_{t-1}+b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^b\left(
abla f_{i_{t,j}}(x_t)-
abla f_{i_{t,j}}(x_{t-1})ight),&	ext{otherwise},\end{cases}\] where nonrefresh indices are conditionally independent and uniform, and update \[x_{t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x_t-\eta v_t).\] Return \(x_R\), where \(R\) is uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\) and independent of the history generating the iterates.

Nonrefresh samples are conditionally independent and uniform with replacement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh-accuracy requirement for a recursive finite-sum gradient estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a recursive epoch begins at \(s\) with \(\mathbb E\|v_s-
abla F(x_s)\|^2\le\delta_s^2\), and \[ rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(y)\|^2\le L^2\|x-y\|^2.\] For conditionally independent uniform minibatches of size \(b\), every \(t\) before the next refresh satisfies \[\mathbb E\|v_t-
abla F(x_t)\|^2\le\delta_s^2+ rac{L^2}{b}\sum_{j=s+1}^{t}\mathbb E\|x_j-x_{j-1}\|^2.\] Thus an analysis seeking estimator mean-square error of order \(\varepsilon^2\) through this bound must control both the refresh error and accumulated movement at that scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate refresh error persists through the recursive epoch and is augmented by movement-dependent component-difference variance.
assumptions_latex: The recursive update uses conditionally independent uniform minibatches of size \(b\).

Consider \(r\equiv0\) and \(F(x)=x^2/2\). Suppose every iteration is a refresh returning \(v_t=
abla F(x_t)+b=x_t+b\) for fixed \(b
e0\). For \(0<\eta<2\), the update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta v_t\) satisfies \[x_t\longrightarrow-b,\qquad 
abla F(x_t)\longrightarrow-b
e0.\] Thus nonvanishing refresh bias can make a smooth strongly convex instance converge to a nonstationary point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite mirror-descent step driven by a snapshot-corrected finite-sum gradient estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+r(x)\) on a closed convex set \(X\), and let \(h\) be differentiable and strongly convex on \(X\). Given snapshot \(\widetilde x\), full gradient \(\widetilde g=
abla F(\widetilde x)\), current point \(x_t\), and uniform index \(i_t\), form \[v_t=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{i_t}(\widetilde x)+\widetilde g.\] Define \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\langle v_t,xangle+r(x)+\eta_t^{-1}D_h(x,x_t)ight\}.\] Refresh the snapshot under a declared schedule and return the prescribed terminal or randomized iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variance-reduced mirror descent combines a snapshot-corrected gradient with a Bregman-proximal mirror step.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable, while \(r\) is proper and convex on \(X\).
The mirror map \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear convergence and gradient complexity of variance-reduced mirror descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded parameter specialization of the source-defined variance-reduced mirror-descent potential bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set
\[
\gamma=\frac{1}{21L},\qquad q_i=\frac{L_i}{\sum_{j=1}^m L_j},\qquad T\ge 2,
\qquad \theta_t=\left(1-\frac{\mu}{21L}\right)^{-t}\quad(t\ge 0).
\]
Then, for every \(s\ge 1\),
\[
\Delta_s\le\left(\max\left\{\left(1-\frac{\mu}{21L}\right)^T,\frac12\right\}\right)^s\Delta_0,
\]
where \(\Delta_s\) is defined by the source's variance-reduced mirror-descent potential. In particular, if \(T\) is chosen as a constant multiple of \(m\), the number of gradient evaluations needed to obtain an \(\varepsilon\)-solution is
\[
\mathcal O\!\left(\left(\frac{L}{\mu}+m\right)\log\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With step size 1/(21L), sampling probabilities proportional to the component smoothness constants, epoch length at least 2, and the stated geometric weights, the source-defined potential converges linearly. If the epoch length is a constant multiple of the number of components, the gradient complexity is O((L/mu + m) log(Delta_0/epsilon)).
