children.title: Geometric Refresh Timing
children.top_down_role: Memoryless refresh schedules expressed through geometrically distributed intervals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Memoryless Characterization of Geometric Refresh Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent characterizations of a constant-hazard refresh gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) take values in \(\{1,2,\ldots\}\) and let \(p\in(0,1]\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(\mathbb P(G=j)=(1-p)^{j-1}p\) for every \(j\geq1\); (ii) \(\mathbb P(G>m+\ell\mid G>m)=\mathbb P(G>\ell)\) whenever \(\mathbb P(G>m)>0\), with \(\mathbb P(G=1)=p\); and (iii) \(\mathbb P(G=j\mid G\geq j)=p\) for every \(j\) with \(\mathbb P(G\geq j)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-integer refresh gap is geometric exactly when it is memoryless, equivalently when its conditional refresh hazard is constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\sim\operatorname{Geometric}(p)\iff G\text{ has the discrete memoryless property with hazard }p.

notation.meaning: number of iterations between consecutive refreshes

knowledge_statements.title: Memoryless Characterization of Geometric Refresh Gaps
Geometric Refresh Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent Bernoulli refreshes and their induced inter-refresh times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in(0,1]\) and let \((B_k)_{k\geq 1}\) be independent Bernoulli random variables with \(\mathbb P(B_k=1)=p\), where \(B_k=1\) denotes a reference refresh after iteration \(k\). Define \(T_0=0\) and \(T_{r+1}=\inf\{k>T_r:B_k=1\}\). Then the gaps \(G_r=T_{r+1}-T_r\) are independent and satisfy \[\mathbb P(G_r=j)=(1-p)^{j-1}p,\qquad j\in\{1,2,\ldots\}.\] Consequently, \(\mathbb E[G_r]=p^{-1}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(G_r)=(1-p)p^{-2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent refresh decisions with probability p produce geometric inter-refresh times having mean 1/p and variance (1-p)/p².

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The geometric-gap statement is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports it.

children.title: General Randomized Refresh
children.top_down_role: Random refresh schedules using non-geometric event distributions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Marginal Refresh Probabilities Do Not Ensure Renewal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable-hazard failure boundary for randomized refresh schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent refresh decisions have \(q_k=2^{-(k+1)}>0\). Because \(\sum_kq_k<\infty\), \[\mathbb P(B_k=0\text{ for every }k\ge0)=\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}(1-q_k)>0.\] Therefore positivity of every individual refresh probability guarantees neither an eventual refresh nor infinitely many refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized policy can assign positive probability at every iteration and nevertheless never refresh with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Marginal Refresh Probabilities Do Not Ensure Renewal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictable accounting identity for general randomized refresh decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(B_k\in\{0,1\}\), \(q_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and \(\mathbb E[B_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=q_k\), then \[M_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(B_k-q_k)\] is a martingale. Thus \[N_K=\sum_{k<K}B_k=A_K+M_K,\qquad A_K=\sum_{k<K}q_k,\] and \(\mathbb E[N_K]=\mathbb E[A_K]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The realized refresh count equals predictable cumulative intensity plus a martingale fluctuation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_K=A_K+M_K\), where \((M_K)\) is a martingale, and \(\mathbb E[N_K]=\mathbb E[A_K]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Refresh-Count Compensator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Next-refresh survival identity for predictable adaptive hazards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a deterministic iteration \(t\), let \(T=\inf\{k\ge t:B_k=1\}\), and assume \(q_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable with \(\mathbb P(B_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)=q_k\). Then, for every \(j\ge t\), \[\mathbb P(T>j\mid\mathcal F_t)=\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbf 1_{\{T>j-1\}}(1-q_j)\mid\mathcal F_t\right],\] where \(\mathbf 1_{\{T>t-1\}}=1\). When later hazards depend on earlier decisions, this recursion cannot in general be replaced by conditioning on realized future hazards and multiplying \(\prod_{r=t}^j(1-q_r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive-hazard survival is computed recursively by weighting surviving paths by the next no-refresh probability; a naive future-hazard product is generally invalid when hazards react to earlier decisions.

notation.meaning: first refresh time at or after t
history available before the k-th refresh decision

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Hazard Survival Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General randomized reference update with explicit timing and oracle charging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration k, let q_k be \mathcal F_k-measurable and draw B_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_k). If B_k=1, evaluate a declared routine \mathcal C_k to obtain \widehat R_{k+1} and set R_{k+1}=\widehat R_{k+1}; otherwise do not evaluate \mathcal C_k and set R_{k+1}=R_k. Then compute x_{k+1}=\mathcal U_k(x_k,R_{k+1},\xi_k). If the candidate and ordinary update cost c_k and u_k component calls, the realized cost is u_k+B_kc_k and its conditional expectation is u_k+q_kc_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw first, construct a candidate only after successful refresh, and then update using the selected reference.
assumptions_latex: \xi_k is sampled after R_{k+1} is determined.
c_k and u_k are nonnegative \mathcal F_k-measurable counts.

notation.meaning: optimization update using the selected reference

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Decision-First Randomized Refresh Protocol
General Randomized Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictable randomized policies for replacing a stored reference state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0}\) describe the algorithmic history, and let \(q_k\in[0,1]\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable. A general randomized refresh policy draws \(B_k\), conditionally on \(\mathcal F_k\), according to \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_k)\), and updates a stored reference \(R_k\) by \[R_{k+1}=B_k\widehat R_{k+1}+(1-B_k)R_k,\] where \(\widehat R_{k+1}\) is the newly computed reference state. Thus \(\mathbb P(B_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)=q_k\); constant, time-varying, and state-dependent refresh probabilities are special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized policy refreshes a stored reference with a history-measurable probability and otherwise retains the previous reference.

notation.meaning: history available before the k-th refresh decision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the randomized-refresh leaf, but the filtration and update-timing convention has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Refresh-Frequency Variability
children.top_down_role: Effects of randomized interval variability on work balance and estimator freshness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct variance accounting for predictable adaptive refresh probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^K\) be a filtration, let \(q_k\in[0,1]\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(B_k\in\{0,1\}\) be \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable with \(\mathbb E[B_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=q_k\). Put \(N_K=\sum_{k<K}B_k\), \(A_K=\sum_{k<K}q_k\), and \(M_K=\sum_{k<K}(B_k-q_k)\). Then \((M_k)\) is a martingale, \(\mathbb E[N_K]=\mathbb E[A_K]\), and \[\operatorname{Var}(N_K)=\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{k<K}q_k(1-q_k)\right]+\operatorname{Var}(A_K)+2\operatorname{Cov}(M_K,A_K).\] The covariance term need not vanish. If all \(q_k\) are deterministic, then \(\operatorname{Var}(N_K)=\sum_{k<K}q_k(1-q_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive refresh-count variance contains conditional Bernoulli noise, variability of the predictable refresh budget, and a covariance term that vanishes for deterministic probabilities but not generally.
assumptions_latex: All displayed second moments are finite.

notation.meaning: number of refreshes in the first K decisions

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Adaptive Refresh-Count Variance Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of refresh-count moments to a fixed-cost work model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(K\) base iterations cost \(c_{\mathrm{base}}\) each and each refresh adds deterministic cost \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\). If \(W_K=Kc_{\mathrm{base}}+c_{\mathrm{ref}}N_K\), then \(\mathbb E[W_K]=Kc_{\mathrm{base}}+c_{\mathrm{ref}}\mathbb E[N_K]\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(W_K)=c_{\mathrm{ref}}^2\operatorname{Var}(N_K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fixed per-refresh cost, count variance transfers exactly to work variance, so equal mean refresh frequency does not imply equal workload variability.
assumptions_latex: Every refresh has the same additive cost \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Refresh-Count Variability as Work Variability
Refresh-Frequency Variability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variability of refresh counts under randomized timing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a predictable randomized refresh policy with \(B_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_k)\), define the refresh count \(N_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}B_k\). Then \[\mathbb E[N_K]=\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_k\right].\] Moreover, the centered process \(M_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(B_k-q_k)\) is a martingale whose predictable quadratic variation is \[\langle M\rangle_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_k(1-q_k).\] Hence \(\operatorname{Var}(N_K)=\mathbb E[\langle M\rangle_K]+\operatorname{Var}(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh-count variability combines Bernoulli decision noise with variability in the predictable refresh probabilities.

notation.meaning: number of refreshes before iteration K
predictable quadratic variation of the count martingale

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the stated variance decomposition is not valid for a general adaptive predictable sequence: a covariance term between the martingale sum and the random compensator can remain.

children.title: State-Dependent Refresh
children.top_down_role: Refresh decisions keyed to observable optimization or estimator state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trajectory-level condition preventing a state-dependent trigger from suppressing refresh forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\) and \(q(S_k)\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and let \(B_k\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(B_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)=q(S_k)\). If \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}q(S_k)=\infty\quad\text{almost surely},\] then \(B_k=1\) infinitely often almost surely. In particular, \(\inf_{s\in\mathcal S}q(s)>0\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state-dependent policy refreshes infinitely often when its accumulated conditional hazard diverges; a uniform positive floor is sufficient.

notation.meaning: conditional refresh hazard at that state

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Refresh Along State Trajectories

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endogenous state-dependent trigger with positive probability of never refreshing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S_0=0, q(s)=2^{-(s+1)}, and B_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q(S_k)). Update the observable state by S_{k+1}=0 when B_k=1 and S_{k+1}=S_k+1 when B_k=0. On the event of no refresh, S_k=k and \[\mathbb P(B_k=0\ \forall k\ge0)=\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}(1-2^{-(k+1)})>0,\] because \(\sum_{k\ge0}2^{-(k+1)}<\infty\). Thus a strictly positive state-dependent trigger need not prevent permanent starvation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trigger that decays as the time-since-refresh state grows remains positive everywhere yet has positive probability of never refreshing.
assumptions_latex: S_0=0 and S_{k+1}=0 if B_k=1, while S_{k+1}=S_k+1 if B_k=0.

notation.meaning: number of consecutive nonrefresh decisions in the constructed state process

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Hazard State Trigger Can Starve

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictable Survival Recursion for State-Dependent Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-horizon recursion for survival under an endogenous predictable state trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S_k be \mathcal F_k-measurable and let B_k\in\{0,1\} satisfy \mathbb E[B_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=q(S_k). For a bounded stopping time \tau, define H_{\tau,0}=1 and H_{\tau,r}=\prod_{j=\tau}^{\tau+r-1}(1-B_j). Then \[\mathbb E[H_{\tau,r+1}\mid\mathcal F_{\tau+r}]=H_{\tau,r}(1-q(S_{\tau+r})),\qquad \mathbb P(B_\tau=\cdots=B_{\tau+r-1}=0\mid\mathcal F_\tau)=\mathbb E[H_{\tau,r}\mid\mathcal F_\tau].\] Future hazards generally cannot be multiplied along the realized, unconditioned future state path because that path may itself reveal earlier refresh decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No-refresh survival obeys a one-step predictable-hazard recursion; a simple product of hazards along the realized endogenous future path is generally invalid.

notation.meaning: indicator of no refresh during the r decisions starting at tau

knowledge_statements.title: Predictable Survival Recursion for State-Dependent Refresh

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Executable state-dependent snapshot policy with fixed update timing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x). Store w_k and g_k=
abla F(w_k). Sample i_k uniformly, form v_k=
abla f_{i_k}(x_k)-
abla f_{i_k}(w_k)+g_k, and set x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta v_k. Then set q_k=\min\{1,q_0+\alpha\|x_{k+1}-w_k\|\}, draw B_k\mid\mathcal F_k^+\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_k), and set (w_{k+1},g_{k+1})=(x_{k+1},
abla F(x_{k+1})) when B_k=1 and (w_k,g_k) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take the current step with the old snapshot, then refresh the next snapshot with probability increasing in iterate-to-snapshot distance.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F_k^+ contains the history through x_{k+1} and precedes B_k.

notation.meaning: stored full gradient at the snapshot

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Triggered Post-Step Snapshot Refresh
State-Dependent Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh probability selected from the current observable algorithmic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial reference \(R_0\), a measurable state map \(S_k=S(x_k,R_k,\mathcal F_k)\), and a measurable trigger \(q:\mathcal S\to[0,1]\), iteration \(k\) computes \(q_k=q(S_k)\), draws \(B_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_k)\), constructs \(\widehat R_{k+1}\) only when \(B_k=1\), and sets \[R_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\widehat R_{k+1},&B_k=1,\\R_k,&B_k=0.\end{cases}\] The optimization update uses \(R_{k+1}\) or \(R_k\) according to the method’s declared timing convention, and the algorithm outputs the prescribed final iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The refresh probability is a measurable function of the current iterate, stored reference, and observable history.

notation.meaning: observable state used by the trigger

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the optimization-update timing is explicitly left method-dependent and no source identifies a precise supported algorithm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictable Survival Law for State-Dependent Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected proposed product formula for an endogenous predictable state trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S_k be \mathcal F_k-measurable and B_k=\mathbf 1\{U_k\le q(S_k)\}, where U_k is uniform on [0,1] and independent of \mathcal F_k. The proposed identity was \[\mathbb P(B_\tau=\cdots=B_{\tau+r-1}=0\mid\mathcal F_\tau)=\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j=\tau}^{\tau+r-1}(1-q(S_j))\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_\tau\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed formula averages hazards along the realized future state path.
assumptions_latex: U_k is uniform on [0,1] and independent of \mathcal F_k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed multi-step identity is not valid for a general endogenous state process.}
review_flags: future realized states can depend on earlier refresh decisions, so averaging the product over all realized branches does not equal survival probability
knowledge_statements.title: Predictable Survival Law for State-Dependent Refresh

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns refresh hazards selected from observable optimization state, including endogenous survival, persistence, and starvation behavior. The proposed realized-path product formula was deferred as false and replaced by the correct predictable survival recursion; the new endogenous finite-hazard construction completes the local failure boundary. A timed executable optimization policy remains missing. Generic frequency calculus and signal robustness were excluded to sibling scopes.

children.title: Adaptive Refresh Frequencies
children.top_down_role: Refresh frequencies adjusted as computational or statistical conditions change.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Adaptive Frequencies Permit Permanent Starvation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp starvation boundary when adaptive refresh probabilities have no persistent lower intensity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent Bernoulli decisions with deterministic probabilities \(0\le q_k<1\), if \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}q_k<\infty\), then for every \(K\), \[\mathbb P(B_k=0\text{ for all }k\ge K)=\prod_{k=K}^{\infty}(1-q_k)>0.\] Thus requiring \(q_k>0\) separately at every iteration does not guarantee any future refresh.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive but summable refresh probabilities leave positive probability of never refreshing again.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Adaptive Frequencies Permit Permanent Starvation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cumulative Refresh Intensity and Starvation Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh-count and waiting-time consequences of predictable adaptive frequencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_k)\), with \(q_k\) \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(N_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}B_k\). Then \(\mathbb E[N_K]=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\mathbb E[q_k]\). If \(q_k\ge q_{\min}>0\) almost surely, then for every almost surely finite stopping time \(\tau\) and integer \(r\ge1\), \[\mathbb P(B_\tau=\cdots=B_{\tau+r-1}=0\mid\mathcal F_\tau)\le(1-q_{\min})^r.\] Consequently, the conditional expected waiting time from \(\tau\) to the next refresh is at most \(1/q_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected refresh work equals cumulative expected refresh intensity, while a positive probability floor gives geometric delay tails and bounded mean waiting time.
assumptions_latex: For the delay bound, \(q_k\ge q_{\min}>0\) almost surely and \(\tau\) is almost surely finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[N_K]=\sum_{k<K}\mathbb E[q_k]\) and the next-refresh waiting time has conditional tail at most \((1-q_{\min})^r\).

notation.meaning: number of refreshes before iteration K

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Refresh Intensity and Starvation Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Martingale representation, predictable variance, and concentration of refresh work under history-adapted frequencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0} be the pre-decision filtration, let q_k\in[0,1] be \mathcal F_k-measurable, and let B_k\in\{0,1\} satisfy \mathbb E[B_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=q_k. Define M_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(B_k-q_k). Then (M_K)_{K\ge0} is a martingale with increments bounded above by one and predictable quadratic variation \langle M\rangle_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_k(1-q_k). For t,v>0, \[\mathbb P\!\left(M_K\ge t,\ \langle M\rangle_K\le v\right)\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(v+t/3)}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The realized refresh count minus its cumulative predictable intensity is a bounded-increment martingale, so refresh work concentrates around its adaptive budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_K=\sum_{k<K}(B_k-q_k)\text{ is a martingale},\quad \langle M\rangle_K=\sum_{k<K}q_k(1-q_k),\quad \mathbb P(M_K\ge t,\langle M\rangle_K\le v)\le e^{-t^2/(2(v+t/3))}.

notation.meaning: compensated refresh count through iteration K
predictable quadratic variation of the compensated count

knowledge_statements.title: Compensated Adaptive Refresh Count

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Divergent Predictable Intensity Forces Infinitely Many Refreshes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional Borel–Cantelli guarantee for history-adapted refresh frequencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the pre-decision filtration, let \(q_k\in[0,1]\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(B_k\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(B_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)=q_k\). Then, up to null events, \[\left\{\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}q_k=\infty\right\}\subseteq\{B_k=1\text{ infinitely often}\}.\] Thus \(\sum_kq_k=\infty\) almost surely implies infinitely many refreshes almost surely; a uniform positive probability floor is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive policy refreshes infinitely often whenever its cumulative predictable refresh intensity diverges almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Divergent Predictable Intensity Forces Infinitely Many Refreshes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Realized Adaptive Refresh Frequency Tracks Predictable Frequency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Long-run calibration of realized refresh counts under predictable adaptive probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be the pre-decision filtration, let \(q_k\in[0,1]\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(B_k\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[B_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=q_k\). With \(N_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}B_k\), \[\frac{N_K-\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_k}{K}\longrightarrow0\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Consequently, if \(K^{-1}\sum_{k<K}q_k\to\bar q\) almost surely, then \(N_K/K\to\bar q\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The long-run realized refresh fraction tracks the average predictable refresh probability.
assumptions_latex: \(q_k\) is measurable before the kth refresh decision.

notation.meaning: Number of refreshes before iteration K.

knowledge_statements.title: Realized Adaptive Refresh Frequency Tracks Predictable Frequency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtration-consistent feedback adaptation followed by a Bernoulli refresh decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all information available before refresh decision \(B_k\). Choose an initial \(\mathcal F_0\)-measurable \(q_0\in[0,1]\). For \(k\ge1\), observe an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable statistic \(Z_k\) and set \[q_k=\Phi_k(q_{k-1},Z_k)\in[0,1],\] where \(\Phi_k\) is measurable. After \(q_k\) is fixed, draw \(B_k\in\{0,1\}\) with \[\mathbb P(B_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)=q_k.\] Persistent exploration means \(q_k\ge q_{\min}>0\) almost surely; the weaker cumulative-intensity condition is \(\sum_kq_k=\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observe feedback, compute a history-measurable refresh probability, and only then draw the refresh indicator with that conditional probability.
assumptions_latex: Each refresh draw occurs after \(q_k\) is fixed and has the stated conditional Bernoulli law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[B_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=q_k,\qquad q_k\text{ is predictable relative to decision }B_k.

notation.meaning: Information available before the kth refresh draw.
Observed feedback used to adapt the probability.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictable Adaptive Refresh Frequency
Adaptive Refresh Frequencies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-driven evolution of the conditional refresh frequency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive refresh-frequency policy consists of an initial probability \(q_0\in[q_{\min},q_{\max}]\), observable feedback statistics \(Z_{k+1}\), and measurable update maps \(\Phi_k\). It recursively sets \[q_{k+1}=\Phi_k(q_k,Z_{k+1})\in[q_{\min},q_{\max}],\qquad B_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_{k+1}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_{k+1}),\] where \(0<q_{\min}\leq q_{\max}\leq1\) and \(Z_{k+1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable. The bounds prevent refresh starvation and exclude probabilities exceeding one, while \(\Phi_k\) may increase or decrease frequency according to observed estimator quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive policy updates its refresh probability from observable feedback while maintaining prescribed lower and upper probability bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed adaptive-policy definition is plausible, but no source supports it and the filtration must be defined as pre-decision history for the conditional Bernoulli statement to be precise.

children.title: Trigger Robustness
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of refresh triggers to noisy, delayed, or misleading state signals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-threshold trigger suppressing repeated switching near a decision boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\theta_-<\theta_+\). Given the preceding binary state \(B_{k-1}\) and observed score \(\widehat h_k\), set \[B_k=\begin{cases}1,&\widehat h_k\ge\theta_+,\\0,&\widehat h_k\le\theta_-,\\B_{k-1},&\theta_-<\widehat h_k<\theta_+ .\end{cases}\] If \(\widehat h_k=h+e_k\), the true score \(h\) is fixed, and \(|e_k|\le\varepsilon< (\theta_+-\theta_-)/2\), observation noise alone cannot cause both an off-to-on and an on-to-off transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separated thresholds create a dead band that prevents bounded noise from repeatedly toggling a fixed underlying score in both directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Noise cannot cause both switching directions while the true score remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Hysteretic Refresh Trigger

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic stability test for a threshold-based refresh decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(s)=\mathbf 1\{h(s)\ge\theta\}\), where \(|h(s)-h(s')|\le Ld(s,s')\) with \(0\le L<\infty\). If \(|h(s)-\theta|>L\delta\), then \(B(s')=B(s)\) for every \(s'\) satisfying \(d(s,s')\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold decision is invariant throughout a perturbation ball when its score margin exceeds the largest possible score error.
knowledge_statements.title: Margin Robustness of Threshold Triggers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrarily small alternating observation errors destabilize a single-threshold trigger.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B_k=\mathbf 1\{\widehat h_k\ge\theta\}\), take the constant true score \(h_k=\theta\) and observations \(\widehat h_k=\theta+(-1)^k\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon>0\). Then \(B_k\) alternates at every iteration although the true score never changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero margin, arbitrarily small alternating noise makes a single-threshold trigger chatter indefinitely.
assumptions_latex: The trigger has one threshold and no hysteresis.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Chattering at Zero Margin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-level robustness for randomized binary refresh decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized binary trigger is a Markov kernel K from a metric space (\mathcal S,d) to \{0,1\}. It is \omega-robust if \|K(s,\cdot)-K(s',\cdot)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\omega(d(s,s')) for all s,s', where \omega is nondecreasing and \omega(0)=0. Writing q(s)=K(s,\{1\}), \|K(s,\cdot)-K(s',\cdot)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=|q(s)-q(s')|, which also equals the minimum disagreement probability over all couplings of the two decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearby states induce nearby Bernoulli refresh laws; total variation equals both the probability difference and the optimal coupled disagreement probability.
assumptions_latex: K(s,\cdot) is a probability law on \{0,1\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Total-Variation Robustness of Randomized Triggers
Trigger Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of refresh probabilities under perturbations of the trigger state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal S,d)\) be the trigger-state metric space. A state-dependent refresh trigger \(q:\mathcal S\to[q_{\min},q_{\max}]\) is \((L_q,q_{\min})\)-robust if \[|q(s)-q(s')|\leq L_q d(s,s')\quad\text{for all }s,s'\in\mathcal S,\qquad q_{\min}>0.\] If Bernoulli decisions at \(s\) and \(s'\) are generated by the same uniform random variable, their disagreement probability is exactly \(|q(s)-q(s')|\), and is therefore at most \(L_qd(s,s')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust trigger is Lipschitz in its observed state and retains a positive minimum refresh probability; coupled decisions then rarely disagree under small perturbations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|q(s)-q(s')|\leq L_qd(s,s')\) and \(\mathbb P(B(s)\neq B(s'))\leq L_qd(s,s')\) under common-uniform coupling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and the common-uniform coupling claim is standard, but the proposed robustness notion lacks a cited source and should explicitly require a finite nonnegative Lipschitz constant.

children.title: Full-Gradient-Free Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initial estimator construction without an exact pass over every component.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbiased Initialization Need Not Be Realization-Wise Accurate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation family separating unbiasedness from deterministic initialization accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=2\) and scalar component gradients \(a_1=M\), \(a_2=-M\), the full gradient is zero. A uniformly sampled singleton initializer satisfies \(g_0\in\{-M,M\}\), so \(\mathbb E[g_0]=0\) but \(|g_0|=M\) almost surely. The realized initialization error is therefore arbitrarily large as \(M\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased proper-mini-batch initializer can be inaccurate on every realization when component gradients cancel.
assumptions_latex: One of the two components is sampled uniformly.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Initialization Need Not Be Realization-Wise Accurate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional error of a uniform without-replacement initial reference estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i=\nabla f_i(x_0)\), \(\bar a=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\), and let \(S_0\) be conditionally uniform over subsets of size \(b\). For \(g_0=b^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_0}a_i\), \[\mathbb E[g_0\mid x_0]=\bar a,\qquad \mathbb E[\|g_0-\bar a\|^2\mid x_0]=\frac{n-b}{b(n-1)}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|a_i-\bar a\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform without-replacement mini-batch initialization is conditionally unbiased and has the standard finite-population variance correction.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(x_0\), \(S_0\) is uniform over all subsets of size \(b\).
All component gradients at \(x_0\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[g_0\mid x_0]=\nabla F(x_0)\) with the displayed conditional mean-square error.

notation.meaning: full gradient at the initial point

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Population Variance of Mini-Batch Initialization
Full-Gradient-Free Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mini-batch construction of the initial stored gradient reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), choose \(x_0\), sample a nonempty proper subset \(S_0\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) uniformly without replacement, and initialize \[y_0=x_0,\qquad g_0=\frac{1}{|S_0|}\sum_{i\in S_0}\nabla f_i(y_0).\] No full component-gradient pass is performed. Conditional on \(y_0\), the estimator satisfies \(\mathbb E[g_0\mid y_0]=\nabla F(y_0)\). The subsequent variance-reduced method starts from the state \((x_0,y_0,g_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the reference gradient with a uniformly sampled proper mini-batch, obtaining an unbiased estimate without evaluating all component gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) and every \(f_i\) is differentiable at \(x_0\).
\(S_0\) is a uniformly sampled subset of fixed size \(1\leq |S_0|<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_0=|S_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_0}\nabla f_i(x_0)\) and \(\mathbb E[g_0\mid x_0]=\nabla F(x_0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The initialization algorithm and unbiasedness claim are plausible, but no source is given and uniform fixed-size sampling must be specified conditionally independently of the component gradients given the initialization state.

children.title: Full-Gradient-Free Refresh
children.top_down_role: Reference renewal without exact full-gradient recomputation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value-Dependent Batch Selection Can Bias Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of conditional unbiasedness when the current batch is selected from current component values without correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let scalar component gradients at the refresh point be \(a_1=0\) and \(a_2=2\), whose mean is \(1\). If a singleton selection rule uses current-value side information and always selects the larger component, then the unweighted refreshed estimate is \(g=2\) almost surely, so \(\mathbb E[g]=2\ne1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting the refresh batch from current component values biases the unweighted mini-batch average unless the sampling probabilities are corrected.
assumptions_latex: The selection rule always chooses the component with larger current gradient.

notation.meaning: component gradient at the refresh point

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Dependent Batch Selection Can Bias Refresh

Let \(\mathcal F_k^-\) contain the complete history and refreshed point \(y_{k+1}\) before batch sampling. If \(S_k\), conditional on \(\mathcal F_k^-\), is uniform over subsets of fixed size \(1\le b_k<n\), then for \(g_{k+1}=b_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_k}

abla F(y_{k+1}),\] and \[\mathbb E[\|g_{k+1}-
abla F(y_{k+1})\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k^-]= rac{n-b_k}{b_k(n-1)} rac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_i(y_{k+1})-
abla F(y_{k+1})\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditionally uniform proper mini-batch refresh is unbiased given the full pre-sampling history and has exact finite-population variance.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_k^-\), \(S_k\) is uniform over subsets of size \(b_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The refreshed reference is conditionally unbiased with the displayed conditional mean-square error.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Finite-Population Error at Refresh
Full-Gradient-Free Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mini-batch replacement of a gradient reference during execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a declared refresh iteration \(k\), set the new reference point to \(y_{k+1}=x_k\), sample a nonempty proper subset \(S_k\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) uniformly without replacement, and compute \[g_{k+1}=\frac{1}{|S_k|}\sum_{i\in S_k}\nabla f_i(y_{k+1}).\] At a non-refresh iteration, retain \((y_{k+1},g_{k+1})=(y_k,g_k)\). Each refresh uses \(|S_k|<n\) component-gradient evaluations and satisfies \(\mathbb E[g_{k+1}\mid y_{k+1}]=\nabla F(y_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each refresh, replace the reference gradient by an unbiased proper-mini-batch estimate and retain the old reference otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) is conditionally uniform of fixed size \(1\leq |S_k|<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[g_{k+1}\mid y_{k+1}]=\nabla F(y_{k+1})\) using fewer than \(n\) component gradients per refresh.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but no source is supplied and conditional uniformity must be stated relative to the complete pre-sampling history to justify the displayed conditional expectation.

children.title: Initialization-to-Refresh Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between approximate initialization choices and later refresh mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite compatibility check when an analysis uses only first and second conditional moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose admissibility at \(y\) is defined by \[\mathbb E[g\mid y]=\nabla F(y),\qquad \mathbb E[\|g-\nabla F(y)\|^2\mid y]\le V(y).\] If both the initialization kernel and every refresh kernel satisfy these conditions with the same envelope \(V\), then they are compatible for every argument that uses no other property of their conditional laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a moment-based analysis, common conditional unbiasedness and variance bounds certify initialization-to-refresh compatibility.
assumptions_latex: The downstream argument uses no estimator property beyond the displayed conditional moments.
The same variance envelope \(V(y)\) is required at initialization and refresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both kernels belong to the same moment-defined admissible family.

notation.meaning: allowed conditional mean-square error at reference point y

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Invariant Compatibility Check

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional criterion ensuring initialization and refresh preserve one reference-state invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_0(y,\cdot)\) be the conditional law of an initialized reference estimate and \(K_r(y,\cdot)\) the conditional law used at refreshes. Given an admissible family \(\mathfrak K(y)\), initialization and refresh are compatible when \[K_0(y,\cdot)\in\mathfrak K(y)\quad\text{and}\quad K_r(y,\cdot)\in\mathfrak K(y)\] for every admissible reference point \(y\). Every invariant expressed solely through membership in \(\mathfrak K(y)\) then holds after initialization and after each refresh.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization and refresh are compatible when both conditional estimator laws belong to the same admissible family at every reference point.
assumptions_latex: The reference point is measurable before estimator randomness is drawn.
\(\mathfrak K(y)\) contains every conditional-law property used by the downstream analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same reference-law invariant holds at time zero and after every refresh.

notation.meaning: admissible family of estimator laws at reference point y

knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle Kernel Compatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Later Unbiased Refreshes Do Not Repair an Incompatible Base Case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an all-constructions invariant when initialization and refresh satisfy different guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an analysis requires \(\mathbb E[g_k\mid y_k]=
abla F(y_k)\) for every constructed reference. Even if every later refresh is conditionally unbiased, an initialization with \(\mathbb E[g_0\mid y_0]
e
abla F(y_0)\) violates the invariant at \(k=0\). An induction using this invariant is therefore invalid before the first compatible refresh.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible later refreshes do not retroactively repair an initialization that violates the required all-iterations invariant.
assumptions_latex: The analysis requires conditional unbiasedness for every constructed reference, including initialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The required invariant fails at iteration zero regardless of later refresh laws.
knowledge_statements.title: Later Unbiased Refreshes Do Not Repair an Incompatible Base Case
Initialization-to-Refresh Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common invariant for initial and subsequently refreshed references.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G(y,\xi)\) be the randomized estimator used to construct a reference gradient at point \(y\). Initialization and refresh are compatible with parameters \((\sigma^2,b)\) if both use the same estimator family and every constructed pair \((y,g)\), including \((y_0,g_0)\), satisfies \[g=\mathcal G(y,\xi),\qquad \mathbb E[g\mid y]=\nabla F(y),\qquad \mathbb E[\|g-\nabla F(y)\|^2\mid y]\leq\frac{\sigma^2}{b}.\] Thus any convergence invariant stated for a freshly constructed reference also holds at iteration zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization and later refreshes are compatible when they use one estimator family satisfying the same unbiasedness and variance invariant.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable at every admissible reference point.
\(\mathcal G(y,\xi)\) has finite conditional second moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y_0,g_0)\) and every refreshed \((y,g)\) satisfy the same unbiasedness and variance conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the compatibility leaf, but the estimator invariant and its claimed convergence consequence have no supporting citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Expected Convergence of Constant-Parameter RPDG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected Bregman-distance and averaged-objective rates for constant-parameter RPDG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau_t=\tau\), \(\eta_t=\eta\), and \(\alpha_t=\alpha\in(0,1)\). If \[(1-\alpha)(1+\tau)\le p_i,\qquad \eta\le\alpha(\mu+\eta),\qquad \eta\tau p_i\ge\frac{4L_i}{m}\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] then, for every \(k\ge1\), \[\mathbb E[V(x^k,x^*)]\le\left(1+\frac{L_f\alpha}{(1-\alpha)\eta}\right)\alpha^kV(x^0,x^*),\] and \[\mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x^k)-\Psi(x^*)]\le\alpha^{k/2}\left(\alpha^{-1}\eta+\frac{3-2\alpha}{1-\alpha}L_f+\frac{2L_f^2\alpha}{(1-\alpha)\eta}\right)V(x^0,x^*),\] where \(\theta_t=\alpha^{-t}\) and \(\bar x^k=(\sum_{t=1}^k\theta_t)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^k\theta_tx^t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated constant-parameter conditions, RPDG converges geometrically in expected Bregman distance, and its weighted averaged iterate has expected objective error decreasing as alpha to the power k over two.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is an optimal solution of the stated problem}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A telescoping finite-sum RPDG guarantee under coupled weight, stepsize, and sampling conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\theta_t\ge0\) and the RPDG parameters satisfy, for all indicated indices, \[\theta_t\bigl(p_i^{-1}(1+\tau_t)-1\bigr)\le p_i^{-1}\theta_{t-1}(1+\tau_{t-1}),\qquad \theta_t\eta_t\le\theta_{t-1}(\mu+\eta_{t-1}),\] \[\frac{\eta_k}{4}\ge\frac{L_i(1-p_i)^2}{m\tau_kp_i},\qquad \frac{\eta_{t-1}}2\ge\frac{L_i\alpha_t}{m\tau_tp_i}+\frac{(1-p_j)^2L_j}{m\tau_{t-1}p_j},\] \[\frac{\eta_k}{2}\ge\frac{\sum_{i=1}^m p_iL_i}{m(1+\tau_k)},\qquad \alpha_t\theta_t=\theta_{t-1}.\] Then, for every \(k\ge1\) and \(z=(x,y)\in Z\), \[\sum_{t=1}^k\theta_t\mathbb E\!\left[Q((x^t,\widehat y^t),z)\right]\le \eta_1\theta_1V(x^0,x)-(\mu+\eta_k)\theta_k\mathbb E[V(x^k,x)]+\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_1\bigl(p_i^{-1}(1+\tau_1)-1\bigr)W_i(y_i^0,y_i).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-Regularization Reduction to a Strongly Convex Finite Sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic reduction from general-convex finite sums to strongly convex finite-sum subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\) be convex, let \(x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\) satisfy \(\|x_0-x_\star\|\le R\), and define \(F_\mu(x)=F(x)+\frac\mu2\|x-x_0\|^2\). If \(\mathbb E[F_\mu(\widehat x)-\min F_\mu]\le\varepsilon/2\) and \(\mu=\varepsilon/R^2\), then \(\mathbb E[F(\widehat x)-F(x_\star)]\le\varepsilon\). The regularized objective remains a finite sum by replacing each component with \(f_i(x)+\frac\mu2\|x-x_0\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small common quadratic converts a general convex finite sum into a strongly convex one; solving the regularized problem to half the target accuracy yields the desired original-objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex and attains its minimum at \(x_\star\).

notation.meaning: initial distance bound to a minimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Regularization Reduction to a Strongly Convex Finite Sum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated general-convex rate obtained by quadratic regularization and a strongly convex Katyusha subroutine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i, where each f_i is convex and L-smooth, and suppose x_\star\in\arg\min F satisfies \|x_0-x_\star\|\le R. Set \mu=\varepsilon/R^2 and F_\mu(x)=F(x)+(\mu/2)\|x-x_0\|^2. If a strongly convex Katyusha variant attains expected F_\mu-gap \delta using O((n+\sqrt{n(L+\mu)/\mu})\log(\Delta_\mu/\delta)) component-gradient evaluations, then running it with \delta=\varepsilon/2 yields \mathbb E[F(\widehat x)-F^*]\le\varepsilon using O\!\left(\left[n+\sqrt{\frac{nLR^2}{\varepsilon}}\right]\log\frac{2\Delta_\mu}{\varepsilon}\right) component-gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic regularization followed by strongly convex Katyusha gives the accelerated general-convex dependence, with a logarithm inherited from this reduction.
assumptions_latex: f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R is convex and L-smooth for every i.
x_\star\in\arg\min F and \|x_0-x_\star\|\le R, with R>0.
The selected strongly convex Katyusha subroutine satisfies the stated component-gradient bound.

If a strongly convex SVRG variant attains expected F_\mu-gap \delta using O((n+(L+\mu)/\mu)\log(\Delta_\mu/\delta)) component-gradient evaluations, then running it with \delta=\varepsilon/2 yields \mathbb E[F(\widehat x)-F^*]\le\varepsilon using O\!\left(\left[n+\frac{LR^2}{\varepsilon}\right]\log\frac{2\Delta_\mu}{\varepsilon}\right) component-gradient evaluations.

x_\star\in\arg\min F and \|x_0-x_\star\|\le R, with R>0.
The selected strongly convex SVRG subroutine satisfies the stated component-gradient bound.

General Convex Finite-Sum Rate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative component-gradient complexities in smooth convex finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), where every \(f_i\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth, and suppose a minimizer \(x_\star\) satisfies \(\|x_0-x_\star\|\leq R\). In the component-gradient oracle model, standard nonaccelerated variance-reduced families attain expected error at most \(\varepsilon\) with complexity of order \[n+\frac{LR^2}{\varepsilon},\] while accelerated finite-sum variance-reduced families attain the benchmark order \[n+\sqrt{\frac{nLR^2}{\varepsilon}},\] up to universal constants and method-specific logarithmic factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth convex finite sums, nonaccelerated and accelerated variance reduction exhibit distinct dependence on sample size and target accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is convex and has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: initial distance bound to a minimizer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is suitable, but the rates aggregate unspecified method families and unresolved logarithmic factors without an authoritative theorem-level source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epochwise Oracle Accounting from a Snapshot Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional conversion of an epochwise snapshot contraction into component-gradient complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a snapshot method contracts its expected snapshot gap by a factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\) per epoch. If every epoch computes one \(n\)-component full gradient and performs \(m\) inner updates, each using two component-gradient evaluations with no reuse, then \(S\) epochs cost \(S(n+2m)\). For initial gap \(\Delta_0\) and \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta_0\), \(S=\left\lceil\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\) suffices, giving \(N_{\mathrm{grad}}\leq(n+2m)\left\lceil\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given an epochwise contraction, total oracle work is the number of epochs times one full gradient plus the inner-loop component-gradient cost.
assumptions_latex: Each epoch costs exactly \(n+2m\) component-gradient evaluations.
The expected snapshot gap contracts by at most \(\rho\) per epoch.

Given snapshot \(\widetilde x_s\), compute \(g_s=

Let \(n=1\) and \(f_1(x)=F(x)=Lx^2/2\). For every snapshot \(\widetilde x\), \(v_t=
abla f_1(x_t)-
abla f_1(\widetilde x)+
abla F(\widetilde x)=Lx_t\), so \(x_{t+1}=(1-\eta L)x_t\). If \(\eta=2/L\) and \(x_0
e0\), the iterates alternate without converging; if \(\eta>2/L\), their magnitudes diverge. Hence no general snapshot-SVRG convergence theorem can permit \(\eta\ge2/L\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), where every \(f_i\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth and \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. In each epoch, compute \(
abla F(\widetilde x_s)\), perform \(m\) updates using \(v_t=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{i_t}(\widetilde x_s)+
abla F(\widetilde x_s)\) and \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta v_t\), and select the next snapshot according to the standard averaged-iterate convention. If \(0<\eta<1/(2L)\) and \[ho= rac{1}{\mu\eta(1-2L\eta)m}+ rac{2L\eta}{1-2L\eta}<1,\] then \(\mathbb E[F(\widetilde x_s)-F(x_\star)]\leqho^s[F(\widetilde x_0)-F(x_\star)]\).
