children.title: Gradient-Mapping Measures
children.top_down_role: Stationarity criteria based on composite or proximal gradient mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Mapping Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite stationarity certificate for a smooth term plus a proper closed convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+r\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and \(r:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\eta>0\), define \(x^+:=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta\nabla f(x))\) and \(G_\eta(x):=\eta^{-1}(x-x^+)\). The gradient-mapping stationarity measure is \(S_G(x):=\|G_\eta(x)\|\). For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the point \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stationary in this measure when \(S_G(x)\le\varepsilon\). Moreover, \(G_\eta(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial r(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping measures composite stationarity; its vanishing is equivalent to the regularized first-order inclusion.

notation.meaning: proximal operator of the scaled regularizer

It implies \(\mathbb E[\|G_\eta(X)\|]\le\varepsilon\) and, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\|G_\eta(X)\|>\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt\delta}\right)\le\delta.\] These criteria must be distinguished from a deterministic bound at every realized output.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-to-Composite Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction to gradient norm and conversion to a composite subgradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient for some \(L>0\), let \(r:\mathbb{R}^d	o(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and set \(F:=f+r\). For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(0<\eta\le L^{-1}\), define \(x^+:=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta
abla f(x))\) and \(G_\eta(x):=\eta^{-1}(x-x^+)\). Here \(\partial F(z):=
abla f(z)+\partial r(z)\) denotes the composite subdifferential. If \(r\equiv0\), then \(G_\eta(x)=
abla f(x)\). In general, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^+))\le(1+L\eta)\|G_\eta(x)\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a regularizer, the mapping equals the gradient; in the composite case, its norm bounds the composite subgradient residual at the proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz for some \(L>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient Mapping Is Bounded by the Original-Point Composite Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse comparison from a composite subgradient residual at the input point to the gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be differentiable and \(r\) be proper, closed, and convex. For any \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial r\) and \(\eta>0\), define \[G_\eta(x)=\eta^{-1}\!\left[x-\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta\nabla f(x))\right].\] Then \[\|G_\eta(x)\|\le \operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla f(x)+\partial r(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping norm is no larger than the least composite subgradient norm at the original point.

children.title: Computable Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Observable residual criteria usable without access to an unknown optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Computable Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable proximal residual formed from a finite-sum gradient estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(r:\mathbb{R}^d	o(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and set \(F:=f+r\). For \(x,v\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\eta>0\), define \(\widehat x^+:=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta v)\), \(\widehat G_\eta(x;v):=\eta^{-1}(x-\widehat x^+)\), and \(G_\eta(x):=\eta^{-1}(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta
abla f(x)))\). Then \(\|\widehat G_\eta(x;v)-G_\eta(x)\|\le\|v-
abla f(x)\|\) and \(\|G_\eta(x)\|\le\|\widehat G_\eta(x;v)\|+\|v-
abla f(x)\|\). Consequently, for every \(\delta\ge0\), the condition \(\|v-
abla f(x)\|\le\delta\) gives the computable certificate \(\|G_\eta(x)\|\le\|\widehat G_\eta(x;v)\|+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimator-based proximal residual, together with a quantitative bound on the gradient-estimation error, certifies an upper bound on the exact gradient-mapping norm.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Exact-Residual Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-level conversion from computable estimator residuals to the exact proximal-gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,V)\) be random in the composite setting of the immutable residual certificate. If \(\mathbb E\|\widehat G_\eta(X;V)\|^2\le a\) and \(\mathbb E\|V-\nabla f(X)\|^2\le b\), then, for every \(\theta>0\), \[\mathbb E\|G_\eta(X)\|^2\le(1+\theta)a+(1+\theta^{-1})b.\] In particular, \(\mathbb E\|G_\eta(X)\|^2\le2a+2b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean-square bounds on the observable residual and estimator error jointly bound the mean-square exact gradient mapping.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(r\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\eta>0\), \(a,b\ge0\), and the displayed second moments are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Mean-Square Exact-Residual Certificate

children.title: Estimator-Stability Certificates
children.top_down_role: Observable indicators of estimator drift, variance, or reference degradation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional variance reduction for a uniform fixed-size minibatch of table discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be uniform among size-\(b\) subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and set \(Z_B:=b^{-1}\sum_{i\in B}(d_i-\bar d)\). For \(n>1\), \[\mathbb E[\|Z_B\|^2\mid d_1,\ldots,d_n]=\frac{n-b}{b(n-1)}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|d_i-\bar d\|^2.\] For \(n=b=1\), the variance is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling a fixed-size minibatch without replacement multiplies centered table variance by the finite-population factor.
assumptions_latex: The minibatch is uniform among all size-\(b\) subsets.
knowledge_statements.title: Without-Replacement Minibatch Stability Factor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional variance represented by centered SAGA-type table discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_i:=
abla f_i(x)-y_i\), \( ar d:=n^{-1}\sum_i d_i\), and let \(I\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For \(v:=
abla f_I(x)-y_I+n^{-1}\sum_jy_j\), \[v-
abla f(x)=d_I- ar d,\qquad \mathbb E[\|v-
abla f(x)\|^2\mid x,y]= rac1n\sum_i\|d_i\|^2-\| ar d\|^2.\] Thus the uncentered table-discrepancy upper bound is attained exactly when \( ar d=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A SAGA-type estimator's conditional variance equals the average squared table discrepancy minus the squared mean discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Gradient-Table Variance Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-level stability certificate for same-sample recursive gradient differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_t=v_{t-1}+
abla f_{I_t}(x_t)-
abla f_{I_t}(x_{t-1})\), where \(I_t\) is conditionally uniform and \(x_{t-1},x_t,v_{t-1}\) are measurable before sampling. Define \(e_t=v_t-
abla F(x_t)\), \(a_i=
abla f_i(x_t)-
abla f_i(x_{t-1})\), and \( ar a=n^{-1}\sum_i a_i\). Then \(\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\|e_{t-1}\|^2+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|a_i- ar a\|^2\). Consequently, any bound \(Q_t\) on the displayed empirical variance certifies \(\mathbb E[\|e_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le\|e_{t-1}\|^2+Q_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive estimator carries its previous squared error and adds exactly the conditional variance of its same-sample gradient difference.

notation.meaning: component gradient difference across the current step

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Estimator Error-Energy Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variance scaling for independent replicated estimator samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_1,\ldots,V_b\) be conditionally independent copies of an unbiased estimator \(V\) given a state \(\mathcal G\), and let \(\bar V_b=b^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^bV_r\). Then \(\mathbb E[\bar V_b\mid\mathcal G]=\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal G]\) and \(\mathbb E[\|\bar V_b-\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal G]\|^2\mid\mathcal G]=b^{-1}\mathbb E[\|V-\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal G]\|^2\mid\mathcal G]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditionally independent with-replacement minibatch divides an unbiased estimator's conditional variance certificate by its batch size.
assumptions_latex: The samples are conditionally independent and identically distributed given \(\mathcal G\).
The conditional second moment is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: With-Replacement Minibatch Stability Factor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditional stability representation for nonuniform component sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_i>0\) with \(\sum_iq_i=1\), let \(I\) have probabilities \(q_i\), define \(d_i=
abla f_i(x)-y_i\), \( ar d=n^{-1}\sum_i d_i\), and set \(v= ar y+d_I/(nq_I)\), where \( ar y=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i\). Conditional on \(x,y\), \(\mathbb E[v]=
abla f(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\|v-
abla f(x)\|^2=\sum_iq_i\|d_i/(nq_i)- ar d\|^2=n^{-2}\sum_i\|d_i\|^2/q_i-\| ar d\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability reweighting preserves unbiasedness under importance sampling, and the exact variance exposes the penalty from small sampling probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The table and current point are fixed before sampling.
knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampled Table-Estimator Variance Formula
Estimator-Stability Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum table discrepancy certifying conditional variance of a SAGA-type estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and define \(f:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\). For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), store vectors \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), write \(y:=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)\), and set \( ar y:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i\). Conditional on \(x\) and \(y\), let \(I\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and define \(v:=
abla f_I(x)-y_I+ ar y\) and \(D(x,y):=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_i(x)-y_i\|^2\). Then \(\mathbb{E}[v\mid x,y]=
abla f(x)\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|v-
abla f(x)\|^2\mid x,y]\le D(x,y)\). Hence \(D(x,y)\le\sigma^2\), for \(\sigma\ge0\), certifies conditional estimator variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The average discrepancy of a gradient table upper-bounds the conditional variance of its SAGA-type estimator.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(x\) and \(y\), \(I\) is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[v\mid x,y]=\nabla f(x)\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|v-\nabla f(x)\|^2\mid x,y]\le D(x,y)\).

children.title: Residual Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where accessible residuals cease to track the intended performance target.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbiasedness Does Not Ensure Realized Residual Reliability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An unbiased estimator can yield a zero observable residual with positive probability at a nonstationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=ax\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(a
e0\), and let \(r\equiv0\). Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and define \(V=0\) with probability \(1-p\) and \(V=a/p\) with probability \(p\). Then \(\mathbb E[V]=a=
abla F(x)\), but with probability \(1-p\), \[\widehat G_\eta(x;V)=0\quad	ext{while}\quad G_\eta(x)=a
e0.\] Thus unbiasedness alone does not provide a realized stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an unbiased estimator can produce a zero computable residual at a nonstationary point with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[V]=\nabla F(x)\), yet \(\mathbb P\{\widehat G_\eta(x;V)=0,\ G_\eta(x)\ne0\}=1-p\).

notation.meaning: probability of the compensating nonzero estimator value

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiasedness Does Not Ensure Realized Residual Reliability
Residual Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator-based residuals are unreliable without quantitative estimator-error control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the one-dimensional smooth problem \(F(x)=ax\) with \(a
e0\), no regularizer, and any \(\eta>0\). If an estimator returns \(v=0\), then its computable residual is \(\widehat G_\eta(x;v)=v=0\), whereas the exact stationarity measure is \(G_\eta(x)=
abla F(x)=a
e0\). Thus a small estimator-based residual alone cannot certify stationarity. Reliability requires an accompanying deterministic, expected, or high-probability control of \(\|v-
abla F(x)\|\); unbiasedness by itself does not supply such a realized-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy residual can vanish at a nonstationary point; estimator-error control is essential for reliability.

children.title: Expected-Value Certificates
children.top_down_role: Performance certificates expressed through expectation over algorithmic randomness.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Value Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-level stationarity guarantee for a randomized finite-sum method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the random output of an optimization method, including all sampling and output-selection randomness, and let \(S:\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)\) be a measurable stationarity measure. An expected squared-stationarity certificate at accuracy \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is the inequality \(\mathbb{E}[S(X)^2]\le\varepsilon^2\). For smooth problems one may take \(S(X)=\|\nabla F(X)\|\); for composite problems one may take \(S(X)=\|G_\eta(X)\|\). The expectation must be over every random choice used to construct \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expected-value certificate bounds the mean squared stationarity measure of the randomized output.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tail-Integral Representation of an Expected Squared Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent tail-area formulation for a nonnegative stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonnegative measurable random variable \(Z=S(X)\), \(\mathbb E[Z^2]=\int_0^\infty2t\,\mathbb P(Z>t)\,dt\), with both sides allowed to be infinite. Hence \(\mathbb E[S(X)^2]\le\varepsilon^2\) is equivalent to \(\int_0^\infty2t\,\mathbb P(S(X)>t)\,dt\le\varepsilon^2\), and it implies \(\mathbb E[S(X)]\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mean-squared stationarity certificate is exactly an integrated tail bound and also bounds the mean residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Integral Representation of an Expected Squared Certificate

children.title: High-Probability Certificates
children.top_down_role: Performance certificates controlling failure probability at a chosen confidence level.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail-probability stationarity guarantee with explicit failure probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a random output and let \(S:\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)\) be a measurable stationarity measure. For accuracy \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and confidence parameter \(\delta\in(0,1)\), a high-probability stationarity certificate is \(\mathbb{P}(S(X)\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\), equivalently \(\mathbb{P}(S(X)>\varepsilon)\le\delta\). The probability covers all internal sampling, random initialization, and randomized output selection. The pair \((\varepsilon,\delta)\) must therefore accompany the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A high-probability certificate limits the chance that the output's stationarity measure exceeds the stated accuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantile Form of a High-Probability Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent quantile characterization of a tail-probability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonnegative measurable residual \(Z=S(X)\), define \(q_{1-\delta}(Z)=\inf\{t\ge0:\mathbb P(Z\le t)\ge1-\delta\}\). Then \(\mathbb P(Z\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\) if and only if \(q_{1-\delta}(Z)\le\varepsilon\), under this left-quantile convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A high-probability residual certificate is equivalently an upper bound on the corresponding residual quantile.

notation.meaning: left quantile at confidence level one minus delta

knowledge_statements.title: Quantile Form of a High-Probability Certificate

children.title: Confidence-Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Complexity and assumption costs associated with strengthening expectation guarantees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confidence improvement from independent certified runs when success is recognizable through an observable score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose independent outputs \(X_1,\ldots,X_r\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(S(X_j)>\varepsilon)\le p<1\). Then \(\mathbb P(\min_jS(X_j)>\varepsilon)\le p^r\). If the output with smallest observable value or valid upper certificate of \(S\) can be selected, \(r=\lceil\log(1/\delta)/\log(1/p)\rceil\) runs give failure probability at most \(\delta\), multiplying the run cost by \(r\). Without a valid selection score, existence of a successful run does not identify a certified output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent repetition reduces failure probability geometrically, but selecting the successful output requires an observable valid certificate score.
assumptions_latex: Every run has failure probability at most \(p<1\).
For output selection, \(S(X_j)\) is observable or has a valid observable upper certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Repetition Confidence Amplification
Confidence-Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversions between expected and high-probability stationarity guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z:=S(X)\) be a nonnegative measurable random variable, let \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and let \(\delta\in(0,1)\). If \(\mathbb{E}[Z^2]\le\varepsilon^2\), then \(\mathbb{P}(Z\le\varepsilon/\sqrt{\delta})\ge1-\delta\). Conversely, if \(B\ge0\), \(Z\le B\) almost surely, and \(\mathbb{P}(Z\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\), then \(\mathbb{E}[Z^2]\le(1-\delta)\varepsilon^2+\delta B^2\). Without an almost-sure bound or comparable tail control, a high-probability certificate alone need not control \(\mathbb{E}[Z^2]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expected squared residual gives a high-probability bound with accuracy weakened by the inverse square root of the failure probability; the reverse conversion requires bounded or otherwise controlled tails.
assumptions_latex: For the reverse implication, \(B\ge0\) and \(Z\le B\) almost surely.

children.title: Dense Gradient Tables
children.top_down_role: Explicit component-gradient storage using dense representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incremental Exact-Mean Maintenance for a Dense Table
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintaining the table average after one dense row replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(\bar y=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i\). When row \(i\) changes from \(y_i\) to \(y_i^+\), set \(\bar y^+=\bar y+n^{-1}(y_i^+-y_i)\) and store \(y_i\leftarrow y_i^+\). The update uses \(\Theta(d)\) arithmetic and d extra scalar words.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact mean of a dense gradient table can be maintained with one vector correction per changed row.
assumptions_latex: The old row and exact old average are available.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Exact-Mean Maintenance for a Dense Table

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator property enabled by a dense table and its exact maintained mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For uniform \(i\), arbitrary stored vectors \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\), and \(\bar y=n^{-1}\sum_jy_j\), the estimator \(v_i=\nabla f_i(x)-y_i+\bar y\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_i[v_i]=\nabla F(x)\). If a cached vector \(z\) replaces \(\bar y\), unbiasedness holds exactly when \(z=\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the sampled row and adding the exact table mean is unbiased for any table contents.
assumptions_latex: The added mean equals the mean of the currently stored rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Table-Correction Unbiasedness
Dense Gradient Tables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit full-vector storage for every component-gradient memory entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(f:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\) be a finite-sum objective on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\) be the remembered gradient associated with component \(i\). A dense gradient table is a matrix \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\) whose row \(Y_{i,:}=y_i^\top\) stores every coordinate of \(y_i\). Excluding fixed indexing metadata, its storage is \(M_{\mathrm{dense}}:=nd\) scalar words. Reading, replacing, or differencing one complete row costs \(\Theta(d)\) scalar operations and memory accesses. The representation is exact for arbitrary vectors \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense table stores every coordinate of each component's remembered gradient, using nd scalar words and linear-in-d work for a full-row access.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{dense}}=nd\) scalar words, and one full-row access costs \(\Theta(d)\).

children.title: Sparse Gradient Tables
children.top_down_role: Explicit component-gradient storage exploiting sparse support.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact maintenance of the average represented by a sparse gradient table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar y=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n y_k\), replacing row \(y_i\) by \(y_i'\) and setting \(\bar y\leftarrow\bar y+n^{-1}(y_i'-y_i)\) preserves the average invariant. With supports \(S_i,S_i'\), the correction takes \(O(|S_i|+|S_i'|)\) coordinate work. A dense representation of \(\bar y\) additionally occupies \(\Theta(d)\) values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One sparse row replacement updates the exact table average by traversing the old and new supports, although the average itself may require dense storage.
assumptions_latex: The previous row is available before replacement.
Sparse unions and coordinate updates cost constant time per visited coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Incremental Table-Average Maintenance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding cost beyond the stored nonzero values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\). A row-compressed table stores \(M\) coordinate indices and \(n+1\) row offsets, hence uses \(\Theta(M+n)\) machine words including its values when each field fits in one word. Explicit coordinate indices require \(M\lceil\log_2 d\rceil\) bits, and offsets require \((n+1)\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\) bits under fixed-width encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse tables require one index per nonzero and row metadata in addition to their values.
assumptions_latex: Rows use a compressed sequential representation.
Indices and offsets are stored explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Index and Row-Metadata Overhead

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Rows Can Have a Dense Average
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of row sparsity to imply sparsity of the maintained aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=d\), let \(y_i=e_i\). Every row is one-sparse, but \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i=n^{-1}\mathbf 1\) has support \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\). Thus sparse row storage alone does not guarantee a sparse table average or sublinear aggregate storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even one-sparse rows can sum to a dense average.
assumptions_latex: \(e_i\) is the i-th coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Rows Can Have a Dense Average
Sparse Gradient Tables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-indexed exact storage for structurally sparse component-gradient memories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), and for each \(i=1,\ldots,n\), let \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\) have support \(S_i:=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:(y_i)_j\ne0\}\) and support size \(s_i:=|S_i|\). A sparse gradient table stores the pairs \((j,(y_i)_j)\) for \(j\in S_i\), with omitted coordinates interpreted as zero. Its value storage is \(M_{\mathrm{values}}:=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\) scalar words, in addition to support indices and row metadata. Under a sequential sparse-row layout, accessing or updating row \(i\) costs \(\Theta(s_i)\) value accesses. This representation reconstructs every \(y_i\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse table stores exactly the nonzero coordinates of each remembered gradient, using one stored value per nonzero and row work proportional to the row's support size.
assumptions_latex: Rows use a sequential sparse layout.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{values}}=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\), and row \(i\) requires \(\Theta(s_i)\) value accesses.

notation.meaning: nonzero support of the i-th remembered gradient

children.title: Density Crossover
children.top_down_role: Storage or access regimes where sparse representation loses its advantage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-versus-sparse full-row processing under an explicit linear cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row with \(s\) stored nonzeros, suppose \(T_d=c_dd\) and \(T_s=c_ss+c_h\), where \(c_d,c_s>0\) and \(c_h\ge0\). Then sparse processing is faster exactly when \(s<(c_dd-c_h)/c_s\). A positive threshold exists only if \(c_dd>c_h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse row access wins only below an implementation-dependent nonzero threshold.
assumptions_latex: The stated linear access-cost model applies.
Both representations perform the same logical row operation.
knowledge_statements.title: Access-Time Density Crossover

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Single Density Threshold Across Resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of storage and access crossovers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The storage comparison \((1+\alpha)q+hn<nd\) and rowwise time comparison \(c_ss_i+c_h<c_dd\) use independent implementation parameters and different density summaries. Neither inequality implies the other without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representation can save memory while slowing access, or accelerate access while using more memory.
assumptions_latex: Storage and access use the stated explicit models.
No relation between storage and timing constants is assumed.
knowledge_statements.title: No Single Density Threshold Across Resources
Density Crossover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory threshold separating dense and sparse gradient-table representations under an explicit overhead model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(s_i\in\{0,\ldots,d\}\) be the stored nonzero count in row \(i\), and define \(q:=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\) and \(\rho:=q/(nd)\). Measure memory in scalar-word equivalents. Suppose sparse support indices require \(\alpha q\) words and sparse row metadata require \(hn\) words, where \(\alpha,h\ge0\). In this model, \(M_{\mathrm{dense}}:=nd\) and \(M_{\mathrm{sparse}}:=(1+\alpha)q+hn\). Sparse storage is memory-preferable exactly when \((1+\alpha)q+hn<nd\). If \(h<d\), this condition is equivalent to \(\rho<(1-h/d)/(1+\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the explicit index-and-row-overhead model, sparse storage uses less memory exactly below the overhead-adjusted average-density threshold.

notation.meaning: per-nonzero index overhead in scalar-word equivalents
per-row metadata overhead in scalar-word equivalents

children.title: Compressed Gradient Memories
children.top_down_role: Stored estimator state represented through quantized or coded compression.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compression Payload Does Not Determine Total Memory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between compressed updates and compressed persistent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each of \(n\) decoded memories \(h_i\in\mathbb R^d\) remains persistently stored as a dense vector, then that table occupies \(nd\) scalar words even when each update message uses fewer than \(d\) coordinates or finitely many bits. A total-memory reduction requires counting encoded states, decoded caches, residuals, codebooks, and decoder metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small compressed update messages do not reduce total memory if dense decoded component states remain live.
assumptions_latex: All persistent live state is counted.
Each retained decoded component memory is an arbitrary dense d-vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{persistent}}\ge nd\) scalar words when all \(h_i\) are stored densely.
knowledge_statements.title: Compression Payload Does Not Determine Total Memory

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual feedback for lossy compressed memory increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For intended increments \(\Delta_t\), define \(r_0=0\), \(q_t=Q(\Delta_t+r_t)\), \(h_{t+1}=h_t+q_t\), and \(r_{t+1}=\Delta_t+r_t-q_t\). Then \(h_T=h_0+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Delta_t-r_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error feedback retains cumulative compression error in a residual instead of discarding it.
assumptions_latex: Compressor outputs, residuals, and intended increments share one vector space.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Feedback Memory Invariant
Compressed Gradient Memories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines componentwise gradient memories represented through randomized compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the finite sum \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), a compressed gradient memory consists of states \(z_i\) and decoders \(D_i\) such that the stored surrogate is \(h_i=D_i(z_i)\). After component \(i_t\) is queried at \(x_t\), its state is updated by \(z_{i_t}^{t+1}=U_{i_t}(z_{i_t}^t,Q_t(\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)-h_{i_t}^t))\), while other states remain unchanged. Here \(Q_t\) maps into a representation using fewer than \(d\) real coordinates or an explicitly bounded number of bits; it may be randomized and lossy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressed memory stores encoded, possibly lossy component-gradient corrections and decodes them into surrogates used by a finite-sum method.
assumptions_latex: The encoder, decoder, and state-update maps are defined on every generated iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_i^t=D_i(z_i^t)\) is an approximate stored gradient whose representation cost is below that of a dense \(d\)-vector.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and bounding the encoded correction does not by itself establish that the complete persistent state costs less than a dense gradient vector.

children.title: Sketched Gradient Memories
children.top_down_role: Stored estimator state represented through randomized low-dimensional sketches.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Universal Exact Recovery from a Proper Linear Sketch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension boundary for exact reconstruction of arbitrary gradient memories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S\in\mathbb R^{r\times d}\) and \(r<d\), then distinct \(g,g'\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfy \(Sg=Sg'\). Hence no reconstruction map \(R\) can obey \(R(Sg)=g\) for every \(g\in\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-dimensional linear sketch cannot exactly recover every dense gradient.

notation.meaning: Null space of the sketching operator.

knowledge_statements.title: No Universal Exact Recovery from a Proper Linear Sketch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery for gradients in a fixed low-dimensional subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be k-dimensional and let \(S\in\mathbb R^{r\times d}\) be injective on \(U\). Then a linear \(R:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^d\) exists with \(R(Sg)=g\) for all \(g\in U\). Necessarily \(r\ge k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch exactly stores gradients from a known subspace when its restriction to that subspace is injective.
assumptions_latex: Every remembered gradient belongs to the fixed subspace \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists R:\forall g\in U,\ R(Sg)=g\), and \(r\ge\dim U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Subspace-Exact Sketched Memory
Sketched Gradient Memories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-sketch representation of approximate component-gradient tables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=[g_1,\ldots,g_n]\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}\) denote a gradient table. A linear sketched memory stores \(Y=SG\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), where \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\) and \(r<d\), together with a reconstruction map \(R:\mathbb{R}^r\to\mathbb{R}^d\). Its component surrogate is \(h_i=R(Y_{:i})=R(Sg_i)\). Replacing column \(g_i\) by \(g_i+\Delta_i\) requires only the sketch update \(Y_{:i}\leftarrow Y_{:i}+S\Delta_i\); exact recovery occurs whenever \(R(Sg_i)=g_i\) on the specified admissible gradient class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketched memory stores lower-dimensional linear measurements of each component gradient and reconstructs surrogates from those measurements.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(R\) are fixed between any two declared sketch-refresh events.
Each stored component gradient belongs to the domain of \(R\circ S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation uses \(rn\) stored scalars for \(Y\), excluding the shared descriptions of \(S\) and \(R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is coherent, but no source supports its use as a finite-sum gradient-memory model, and the exact-recovery claim depends on an unspecified admissible class.

children.title: Memory-Fidelity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between storage reduction and estimator information loss.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fidelity depends on centered component errors rather than a common offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e_i=c\) for every component, then \(e_i-\bar e=0\), so \(v_i=\nabla f_i(x)-h_i+\bar h\) equals the estimator formed from \(g_i\). Component-dependent errors can instead change variance through their covariance with \(a_i-\bar a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared offset cancels exactly; only centered component-dependent error affects this estimator.
assumptions_latex: The same offset is added to every component surrogate.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Mode Memory Errors Cancel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative estimator degradation caused by approximate memories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=a_i-\bar a\) and \(E=e_i-\bar e\). For every \(\gamma>0\), \(\mathbb E\|A-E\|^2\le(1+\gamma)\mathbb E\|A\|^2+(1+\gamma^{-1})\mathbb E\|E\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimator variance is controlled by the exact-memory discrepancy and centered approximation error.
assumptions_latex: The vectors have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.title: Centered-Error Variance Bound
Memory-Fidelity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates representation cost from the error introduced into a gradient-table estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n f_j(x)\), let \(g_i,e_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and set \(h_i=g_i+e_i\), \( ar h=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n h_j\), and \( ar e=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\). For an index \(i\) sampled uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \(v_i=
abla f_i(x)-h_i+ ar h\), \(a_i=
abla f_i(x)-g_i\), and \( ar a=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n a_j\). Then \(\mathbb{E}_i[v_i]=
abla F(x)\) and \(v_i-
abla F(x)=(a_i- ar a)-(e_i- ar e)\). Thus the memory approximation affects the estimator variance through the centered errors \(e_i- ar e\), while storage cost depends on the representation of the surrogates \(h_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the exact average of approximate stored surrogates preserves unbiasedness, while centered memory errors alter the estimator variance.
assumptions_latex: The sampled index is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
The aggregate \(\bar h\) is the exact average of the decoded surrogates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}_i[v_i]=\nabla F(x)\) and \(\mathbb{E}_i\lVert v_i-\nabla F(x)\rVert^2=\mathbb{E}_i\lVert(a_i-\bar a)-(e_i-\bar e)\rVert^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Surrogate Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents component surrogates by shared parameters and per-component metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit surrogate memory for \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) is a state \((\theta,m_1,\ldots,m_n)\) with decoding maps \(D_i\) such that \(h_i=D_i(\theta,m_i)\in\mathbb{R}^d\). The full table \((h_i)_{i=1}^n\) is not materialized. The representation is exact for a prescribed surrogate class \(\mathcal H\) when every \((h_1,\ldots,h_n)\in\mathcal H\) has such a state and all required operations—decoding a queried \(h_i\), updating its metadata, and obtaining \(n^{-1}\sum_i h_i\)—return the same values as the corresponding explicit-table operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Implicit storage reconstructs each surrogate from shared state and component metadata while preserving specified table operations.
assumptions_latex: The decoder domains contain every reachable shared and component state.
The admissible surrogate class \(\mathcal H\subseteq(\mathbb{R}^d)^n\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The memory cost is the representation size of \((\theta,m_1,ldots,m_n)\), rather than necessarily \(nd\) stored scalars.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract representation fits the topic, but no source establishes the required interface operations or cost model. The conclusion also contains the malformed text 'ldots' in place of \ldots.

children.title: Lazy Coordinate Implementations
children.top_down_role: Deferred coordinate maintenance for avoiding unnecessary dense updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Coordinate Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deferred realization of coordinatewise affine updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the dense reference iteration be \(x_j^{t+1}=\phi_{t,j}(x_j^t)\), where \(\phi_{t,j}(u)=a_{t,j}u+b_{t,j}\) and \(b_{t,j}=0\) for \(j\notin S_t\). Store \(\widehat x_j=x_j^{\tau_j}\) and its logical time \(\tau_j\). Define \(\Phi_{s:t,j}=\phi_{t-1,j}\circ\cdots\circ\phi_{s,j}\) for \(s<t\), with \(\Phi_{t:t,j}\) the identity. Before reading coordinate \(j\) at logical time \(t\), set \(\widehat x_j\leftarrow\Phi_{\tau_j:t,j}(\widehat x_j)\) and \(\tau_j\leftarrow t\). For each \(j\in S_t\), materialize it, apply \(\widehat x_j\leftarrow\phi_{t,j}(\widehat x_j)\), and set \(\tau_j\leftarrow t+1\). At termination time \(T\), materialize every requested output coordinate through logical time \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lazy implementation composes exactly the updates omitted since a coordinate's last materialization, applies the current active update once, and materializes requested outputs at termination.
assumptions_latex: Each coordinate update is affine and the coefficients of \(\Phi_{s:t,j}\) can be computed without enumerating all omitted iterations.
Every coordinate is materialized to the current logical time before an operation reads its value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every coordinate materialized at logical time \(t\) equals the corresponding coordinate \(x_j^t\) of the dense reference iteration.

notation.meaning: logical time represented by the stored coordinate
ordered composition of coordinate maps from iterations s through t-1

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-work bound when interval compositions are available in constant time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each required interval pair \((A_{s:t,j},B_{s:t,j})\) is obtained in \(O(1)\) time, a lazy execution with active sets \(S_0,\ldots,S_{T-1}\) uses \(O(d)\) stored coordinate values and timestamps, \(O(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}|S_t|)\) active-coordinate materialization and update work, and \(O(d)\) work to materialize a full final output. Without efficient interval queries, replay may instead cost the number of omitted updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy execution is support-proportional only when deferred interval maps can be recovered without scanning every skipped iteration.
assumptions_latex: Each interval composition is queried in constant time.
Each active coordinate receives constant additional work.
A full final vector is requested.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Materialization Work

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of independent per-coordinate replay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The eager map \((x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1+x_2,x_2)\) cannot update \(x_1\) from \((x_1,\tau_1)\) alone: states \((0,0)\) and \((0,1)\) have the same stored \(x_1\) but require different updated values. Exact laziness therefore requires materializing the dependency, storing sufficient coupled state, or composing a block map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent coordinate replay fails for coupled updates unless omitted dependencies are represented.
assumptions_latex: The lazy state for coordinate one contains no information determining coordinate two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_1^+=x_1+x_2\text{ is not determined by }(x_1,\tau_1)\text{ alone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Update Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact representation of deferred scalar affine updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi_k(u)=a_ku+b_k\), the ordered composition \(\Phi_{s:t}=\phi_{t-1}\circ\cdots\circ\phi_s\) has the form \(\Phi_{s:t}(u)=A_{s:t}u+B_{s:t}\), with \(A_{s:s}=1\), \(B_{s:s}=0\), \(A_{s:k+1}=a_kA_{s:k}\), and \(B_{s:k+1}=a_kB_{s:k}+b_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deferred interval of scalar affine updates can be summarized by one multiplier and one offset.
assumptions_latex: All deferred maps are scalar affine maps.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Composition Coefficients

children.title: Support-Aware Implementations
children.top_down_role: Execution restricted to active component or regularizer supports.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected coordinate work under component sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If component \(i\) is sampled with probability \(p_i\) and an iteration performs \(\Theta(|S_i|)\) coordinate work after support lookup, then \(\mathbb E[W]=\Theta(\sum_i p_i|S_i|)\). Uniform sampling gives \(\Theta(n^{-1}\sum_i|S_i|)\), and processing every component once costs \(\Theta(\sum_i|S_i|)\), excluding support discovery and shared-state maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support-aware work averages sampled support sizes; a full component pass costs their total size.
assumptions_latex: Per-visited-coordinate work is bounded above and below by constants.
Shared-state maintenance is accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected Support Work

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when a declared support omits a reachable nonzero coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12(x_1+x_2)^2\), \(\nabla f(x)=(x_1+x_2,x_1+x_2)\). If \(S=\{1\}\), then at \(x=(1,0)\) support-restricted evaluation omits the nonzero second coordinate, so its update differs from the dense component-gradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A declared support that misses a reachable nonzero gradient coordinate changes the logical algorithm.
assumptions_latex: Execution evaluates and updates only declared support coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Underdeclared-Support Failure
Support-Aware Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse estimator evaluation restricted to coordinates touched by the sampled component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each component gradient, maintain a support set \(S_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(\nabla f_i(x))\subseteq S_i\) for every reachable \(x\). When index \(i_t\) is sampled, materialize the coordinates in \(S_{i_t}\), evaluate the nonzero entries of \(\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)\), and update only state indexed by \(S_{i_t}\). Any dense shared term in the variance-reduced direction must either admit an equivalent support-restricted representation or be handled by an exact lazy transformation. Output coordinates are materialized before inspection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support-aware implementation touches only coordinates potentially used by the sampled component, while representing dense shared effects exactly.
assumptions_latex: Every declared \(S_i\) contains the gradient support of component \(i\) at all reachable points.
All omitted dense effects have an exact implicit or lazy representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The per-sample coordinate work is \(O(|S_{i_t}|)\), apart from representation-maintenance costs, and the logical iterate matches the dense implementation.

children.title: Deferred-Update Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency concerns arising when delayed state maintenance meets changing supports.

knowledge_statements.title: Deferred-Update Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant certifying equivalence between deferred and eagerly executed sparse updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the eager execution use coordinate maps \(\phi_{k,j}\) satisfying \(x_j^{k+1}=\phi_{k,j}(x_j^k)\). For \(s<t\), define \(T_{s:t,j}=\phi_{t-1,j}\circ\cdots\circ\phi_{s,j}\), and let \(T_{t:t,j}\) be the identity. A deferred state \((\widehat x_j,\tau_j)_{j=1}^d\) is consistent at logical time \(t\) when \(x_j^t=T_{\tau_j:t,j}(\widehat x_j)\) for every \(j\). Materialization at time \(t\) replaces \(\widehat x_j\) by \(T_{\tau_j:t,j}(\widehat x_j)\) and sets \(\tau_j=t\). If deferred maps preserve eager execution order and every coordinate-dependent read is preceded by materialization, this invariant certifies exact equivalence with the eager state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistency is certified when composing every stored coordinate with exactly the maps deferred since its recorded logical time yields the corresponding eager coordinate.
assumptions_latex: Deferred coordinate maps are composed in the same order as in the eager reference execution.
Every coordinate-dependent read is preceded by materialization to the current logical time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Materializing every coordinate at logical time \(t\) produces exactly \(x^t\).

notation.meaning: ordered composition of coordinate-j maps from iterations s through t-1
logical time represented by the stored coordinate

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Extended coordinate-friendly operators and exclusive memory access p. 142

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
source_witnesses.locator: 6.2 Extended coordinate-friendly operators and exclusive memory access p. 142

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when a coordinate-dependent read observes stale stored state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the stored value be \(\widehat x=0\) at logical time \(0\), with one deferred map \(\phi_0(u)=u+1\). At logical time \(1\), the eager value is \(1\), but reading \(\widehat x\) without materialization returns \(0\). Hence a coordinate-dependent read must first apply every deferred map through the current logical time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reading a stale stored coordinate can disagree with the eager execution even when the deferred map is correct.
assumptions_latex: A coordinate-dependent read is permitted before pending maps are materialized.
knowledge_statements.title: Unmaterialized-Read Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when noncommuting deferred maps are replayed out of eager order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^0=0\), \(\phi_0(u)=2u\), and \(\phi_1(u)=u+1\). Eager execution gives \((\phi_1\circ\phi_0)(0)=1\), whereas reversed replay gives \((\phi_0\circ\phi_1)(0)=2\). Thus retaining the deferred maps without their eager order is insufficient when they do not commute.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replaying the correct deferred maps in the wrong order can change the logical state.
assumptions_latex: Deferred replay may reverse two noncommuting eager maps.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Reversal Failure
Sparse Proximal Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which a proximal step can be executed on an active coordinate block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\sum_{j=1}^d g_j(x_j)\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\). The proximal map is support-compatible when, for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\eta>0\), \([\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g}(u)]_j=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_j}(u_j)\). Consequently, if \(u_j=x_j\) and \(x_j=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_j}(x_j)\) for all \(j\notin S\), then computing the proximal map only on \(S\) and retaining \(x_j\) outside \(S\) exactly reproduces the dense proximal update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable regularizer permits coordinatewise proximal evaluation; untouched coordinates remain exact only when their dense proximal updates are fixed points.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_j:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g}(u)=(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_j}(u_j))_{j=1}^d\), with exact restriction to \(S\) under the stated fixed-point condition.

notation.meaning: proximal map of the scaled regularizer

source_refs.locator: 10.2 The Proximal Gradient Method p. 270

source_witnesses.source_title: First-Order Methods in Optimization
source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 The Proximal Gradient Method p. 270

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic cost of exact support-restricted separable proximal evaluation, excluding dense-vector materialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(g(x)=\sum_{j=1}^d g_j(x_j)\), every scalar map \(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_j}\) costs \(O(1)\), inactive coordinates satisfy the fixed-point condition, and the iterate is stored so that retaining inactive coordinates requires no dense copy. Then the proximal portion of an update on active set \(S\) costs \(O(|S|)\), whereas explicit evaluation of all scalar proximal maps costs \(O(d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With constant-cost scalar proximal maps, certified inactive coordinates, and sparse in-place storage, proximal work scales with the active-set size.
assumptions_latex: Every coordinate outside \(S\) is certified unchanged by the dense proximal update.
No length-\(d\) output materialization is charged to the restricted proximal operation.

notation.meaning: Arithmetic work for proximal evaluation on active set S.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Proximal Work

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inactive-Coordinate Coupling for a Nonseparable Proximal Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that sparse input perturbations do not generally justify restricted proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x_1,x_2)=\frac{\lambda}{2}(x_1-x_2)^2\), where \(\lambda>0\), and let \(u=(a,0)\) with \(a\ne0\). For \(t=\eta\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g}(u)=\frac{1}{1+2t}\bigl((1+t)a,ta\bigr).\] Thus an input supported only on coordinate \(1\) produces a nonzero proximal output on coordinate \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled quadratic regularizer can make the proximal map dense: changing one coordinate moves an otherwise inactive coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Coordinate Coupling for a Nonseparable Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise extension of the immutable coordinate-separable proximal interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{B_r\}_{r=1}^m\) partition the coordinates and let \(g(x)=\sum_{r=1}^m g_r(x_{B_r})\), where every \(g_r\) is proper, closed, and convex. Then \([\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g}(u)]_{B_r}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_r}(u_{B_r})\). For active blocks \(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), evaluating only blocks in \(A\) exactly reproduces the dense proximal point when \(u_{B_r}=x_{B_r}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_r}(x_{B_r})\) for every \(r\notin A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-separable regularizer has independent block proximal maps; inactive blocks may be retained exactly only when they are fixed points of their dense block updates.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_r\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{prox}_{\eta g}(u)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_r}(u_{B_r})\bigr)_{r=1}^m\text{, with exact active-block restriction under the stated fixed-point conditions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Sparse Proximal Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact delayed evaluation of untouched coordinates for an ℓ1 proximal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g_j(t)=\lambda_j|t|\), write \(S_a(t)=\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-a)_+\). Then \(\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g_j}=S_{\eta\lambda_j}\) and \(S_a\circ S_b=S_{a+b}\) for \(a,b\ge0\). Consequently, if coordinate \(j\) receives no nonproximal perturbation during steps \(p,\ldots,q\), its omitted proximal updates can be reproduced by \(x_j\leftarrow S_{\lambda_j\sum_{r=p}^q\eta_r}(x_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive soft-thresholds add, permitting exact lazy application of omitted ℓ1 proximal updates.
assumptions_latex: No nonproximal perturbation is applied to coordinate \(j\) over the deferred steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Soft-Threshold Accumulation

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the immutable coordinate-separable fixed-point interface, its block-separable extension, sparse proximal work under explicit storage assumptions, and a nonseparable coupling failure example. Lazy update accumulation is deferred to Deferred Sparse-Update Family; full-gradient work regimes, structured shrinkage formulas, and algorithm-specific Proximal SVRG theory are excluded.

children.title: Full-Gradient Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Placement and frequency of exact full-gradient work within finite-sum methods.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-gradient accounting for periodic snapshot refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Over \(T\) inner iterations and \(q\) snapshot refreshes, exact snapshot gradients cost \(qn\) component-gradient evaluations. Without cached snapshot rows, conventional inner steps evaluate both \(\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)\) and \(\nabla f_{i_t}(\widetilde x)\), totaling \(qn+2T\). Caching all snapshot rows during refresh gives \(qn+T\) evaluations but requires \(\Theta(nd)\) dense values or the corresponding sparse-table encoding. For complete epochs of length \(m\), refresh work amortizes to \(n/m\) component gradients per inner step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduled method pays one component pass per refresh; caching snapshot rows exchanges table memory for one fewer component-gradient evaluation per inner step.
assumptions_latex: Component-gradient evaluations are the accounting unit.
Cached and uncached implementations return identical snapshot gradients.
knowledge_statements.title: Refresh Amortization and Snapshot-Table Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core estimator properties within a scheduled refresh epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With \(\mu=
abla F(\widetilde x)\), uniform component sampling, and \(v_i(x)=
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(\widetilde x)+\mu\), one has \(\mathbb E_i[v_i(x)]=
abla F(x)\). Also \(v_i(\widetilde x)=
abla F(\widetilde x)\) for every \(i\), so sampling variance vanishes at the snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The snapshot-corrected estimator is unbiased and equals the exact full gradient at the snapshot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E_i[v_i(x)]=\nabla F(x),\qquad v_i(\widetilde x)=\nabla F(\widetilde x).
knowledge_statements.title: Snapshot Estimator Unbiasedness and Interpolation
Full-Gradient Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic snapshot scheduling for finite-sum variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an epoch length \(m\geq1\), stepsize \(\eta>0\), and initial snapshot \(\widetilde x_0\). At epoch \(s\), compute \(\mu_s=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
abla f_i(\widetilde x_s)\), initialize \(x_{s,0}=\widetilde x_s\), and for \(t=0,\ldots,m-1\) sample \(i_{s,t}\) uniformly and set \(v_{s,t}=
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(x_{s,t})-
abla f_{i_{s,t}}(\widetilde x_s)+\mu_s\) and \(x_{s,t+1}=x_{s,t}-\eta v_{s,t}\). Select \(\widetilde x_{s+1}\) by a declared endpoint or within-epoch rule; stop after a declared number of epochs and return the associated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduled method periodically computes a full snapshot gradient and uses it to center stochastic component-gradient differences within an epoch.
assumptions_latex: Component indices are sampled uniformly and independently conditional on the past.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each epoch incurs \(n\) component-gradient evaluations for \(\mu_s\), plus the declared inner-loop oracle work.

notation.meaning: number of inner iterations per epoch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a recognizable scheduled snapshot-gradient scheme, but no authoritative SVRG citation or locator is supplied, and snapshot-selection variants affect the exact algorithm.

children.title: Full-Gradient Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Estimator architectures designed to operate without exact full-gradient evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle and storage costs of a fully initialized gradient-table implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initializing \(g_i^0=\nabla f_i(\alpha_i^0)\) for every component costs \(n\) component-gradient evaluations. Reusing \(\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)\) as the replacement row then costs one component-gradient evaluation per iteration, so \(T\) iterations cost \(n+T\) evaluations and require no recurring full-gradient pass. An explicit dense table uses \(\Theta(nd)\) values plus \(\Theta(d)\) for its aggregate; sparse-table costs depend on its stored nonzero count and indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully initialized table pays one component pass once, then one component gradient per iteration, trading recurring refreshes for table memory.
assumptions_latex: The newly evaluated component gradient is reused as the refreshed table row.
No additional batch refresh is performed.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental-Avoidance Resource Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when the maintained aggregate ceases to equal the table average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde g^t\) be the aggregate used and \(r_t=\widetilde g^t-n^{-1}\sum_i g_i^t\). Then \(\widetilde v_t=\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)-g_{i_t}^t+\widetilde g^t\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[\widetilde v_t\mid x_t,g^t]=\nabla F(x_t)+r_t\). Thus aggregate drift is exactly estimator bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inconsistent stored aggregate introduces bias equal to its discrepancy from the true table average.
assumptions_latex: The sampled component is conditionally uniform.
knowledge_statements.title: Average-Drift Bias

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Unbiasedness of the Table Estimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator property underlying incremental full-gradient avoidance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on \(x_t\) and stored vectors \(g_1^t,\ldots,g_n^t\), with \(\bar g^t=n^{-1}\sum_i g_i^t\), and sample \(i_t\) uniformly. For \(v_t=\nabla f_{i_t}(x_t)-g_{i_t}^t+\bar g^t\), \(\mathbb E[v_t\mid x_t,g^t]=\nabla F(x_t)\), irrespective of the reference points that produced the stored vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The table-corrected direction is conditionally unbiased whenever the maintained aggregate equals the table average.
assumptions_latex: The sampled component is conditionally uniform.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Unbiasedness of the Table Estimator
Full-Gradient Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental average-memory update avoiding scheduled full-gradient recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize reference points \(\alpha_i^0\), stored gradients \(g_i^0=
abla f_i(\alpha_i^0)\), their average \( ar g^0=n^{-1}\sum_i g_i^0\), and \(x_0\). At iteration \(t\), sample \(i_t\) uniformly, form \(v_t=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)-g_{i_t}^t+ ar g^t\), and set \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t v_t\). Refresh \(g_{i_t}^{t+1}=
abla f_{i_t}(x_t)\), set \( ar g^{t+1}= ar g^t+n^{-1}(g_{i_t}^{t+1}-g_{i_t}^t)\), and leave all other memories unchanged. Return the iterate specified by the stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incrementally maintained gradient table and its average remove the need for recurring full-gradient computations after initialization.
assumptions_latex: The sampled index is uniform conditional on the current state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar g^t=n^{-1}\sum_i g_i^t\) for every \(t\), and no scheduled full-gradient evaluation is required after initialization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incremental table-average invariant is coherent and the content kind fits, but the SAGA-style algorithm and its full-gradient-avoidance characterization lack an authoritative citation.

children.title: Scheduling-to-Avoidance Crossover
children.top_down_role: Work regimes determining whether exact scheduled refreshes remain cost-effective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer-horizon counterpart of the seed's continuous crossover model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T,m\in\mathbb N\), if a refresh occurs at the start of every nonempty epoch, \(W_S(T)=\lceil T/m\rceil C_F+TC_S\) and \(W_A(T)=C_I+TC_A\). Thus avoidance is strictly cheaper exactly when \(C_I+T(C_A-C_S)<\lceil T/m\rceil C_F\), subject to memory feasibility. The ceiling makes the exact finite-horizon boundary piecewise and potentially different from the continuous threshold using \(T/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon comparison must round the number of used epochs upward, producing a piecewise crossover.
assumptions_latex: A full refresh occurs at the start of each nonempty epoch.
All costs share one resource unit.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rounded-Epoch Crossover
Scheduling-to-Avoidance Crossover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-model threshold comparing periodic full gradients with maintained gradient memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T>0\) be an accuracy-equivalent stochastic-step horizon and let \(m>0\) be the scheduled method's epoch length. Let \(C_F,C_S,C_I,C_A\geq0\) denote, respectively, one full-gradient cost, scheduled inner-step cost, avoidance initialization cost, and avoidance per-step cost. Ignoring terminal partial-epoch rounding, the modeled works are \(W_S(T)=(T/m)C_F+TC_S\) and \(W_A(T)=C_I+TC_A\). Define \(\Delta=C_S+C_F/m-C_A\). Then \(W_A(T)<W_S(T)\) exactly when \(T\Delta>C_I\). If \(\Delta>0\), this is equivalent to \(T>C_I/\Delta\); if \(\Delta\leq0\), no positive horizon gives strict advantage when \(C_I\geq0\). The avoidance method is feasible only when its memory requirement \(M_A\) satisfies \(M_A\leq M_{\max}\), where \(M_{\max}\) is the available memory budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed accuracy-equivalent work model, full-gradient avoidance becomes cheaper only when its positive per-step saving repays initialization and its memory fits the available budget.
assumptions_latex: All costs use one fixed resource unit and remain constant over the modeled horizon.
The methods are compared at an accuracy-equivalent horizon \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Avoidance is preferred when \(T\Delta>C_I\) and \(M_A\leq M_{\max}\), with a finite crossover \(T>C_I/\Delta\) only if \(\Delta>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-synchronized aggregation over disjoint, possibly unequal data partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker \(p\) hold \(I_p\), \(n_p=|I_p|\), and compute \(v_{p,t}\) from common state \((x_t,H_t)\) with \(\mathbb E[v_{p,t}\mid\mathcal F_t]=n_p^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_p}\nabla f_i(x_t)\). After the barrier set \(v_t=\sum_p(n_p/n)v_{p,t}\), update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tv_t\), and deterministically reconcile declared memory writes before the next broadcast.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers use one snapshot, partition-size-weighted aggregation, and a deterministic memory merge before the next round.
assumptions_latex: Every worker uses the same pre-round state.
Memory writes are deterministically reconciled before the next broadcast.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Weighted Synchronous Data-Parallel Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covariance reduction for conditionally independent worker estimators, including weighted partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If worker estimators are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_t\), have covariance matrices \(\Sigma_{p,t}\), and are aggregated as \(v_t=\sum_pw_pv_{p,t}\), then \(\operatorname{Cov}(v_t\mid\mathcal F_t)=\sum_pw_p^2\Sigma_{p,t}\). Equal weights and equal covariances give \(\Sigma_t/P\). Without conditional independence, cross-covariance terms remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent weighted worker estimates have covariance equal to the weighted sum of their covariances; correlation can remove the usual one-over-P gain.
assumptions_latex: Worker estimators have finite conditional second moments.
Conditional independence holds for the simplified covariance formula.

notation.meaning: Conditional covariance of worker p's estimator.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Covariance of Worker Aggregation
Synchronous Data-Parallel Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-synchronized averaging of locally computed variance-reduced estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition or replicate the component indices across \(P\) workers and initialize a common iterate \(x_0\) and synchronized variance-reduction state \(H_0\). At round \(t\), broadcast \((x_t,H_t)\). Worker \(p\) samples a local index and computes an estimator \(v_{p,t}\) satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[v_{p,t}\mid x_t,H_t]=\nabla F(x_t)\). After all workers reach the barrier, aggregate \(\bar v_t=P^{-1}\sum_{p=1}^P v_{p,t}\), set \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t\bar v_t\), and deterministically merge the workers' memory updates into \(H_{t+1}\). Return the iterate selected by the stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers synchronously compute unbiased variance-reduced estimators, average them at a barrier, and consistently merge their memory updates.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on the synchronized state, worker estimators are unbiased for the same full gradient.
The merge rule gives every worker the same state before the next round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\bar v_t\mid x_t,H_t]=\nabla F(x_t)\); under conditional independence, \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar v_t\mid x_t,H_t)=P^{-2}\sum_{p=1}^P\operatorname{Var}(v_{p,t}\mid x_t,H_t)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Shared-Memory Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lock-free shared-memory finite-sum update with boundedly stale reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), shared state \((x,s)\), stepsize \(\eta>0\), and delay bound \(\tau\), worker \(p\) repeatedly reads a possibly inconsistent snapshot \((\hat x^k,\hat s^k)\) whose components are at most \(\tau\) committed updates old, samples \(i_k\), and forms an unbiased variance-reduced estimator \(v^k=v(i_k,\hat x^k,\hat s^k)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[v^k\mid\hat x^k,\hat s^k]=\nabla F(\hat x^k)\). It atomically commits \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta v^k\) on the affected coordinates and updates the corresponding control state. After a prescribed number \(K\) of committed updates, output \(x^K\) or a specified averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers compute variance-reduced gradients from boundedly stale shared state and atomically apply coordinate updates without a global synchronization barrier.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le k-d_j(k)\le\tau\) for every component read at committed update \(k\).
Atomic writes prevent lost updates on every affected coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta v(i_k,\hat x^k,\hat s^k)\), with \(\mathbb E[v^k\mid\hat x^k,\hat s^k]=\nabla F(\hat x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Variance-reduction control state, such as a gradient table or reference snapshot.
Possibly inconsistent stale read used to compute update k.
Uniform delay bound measured in committed updates.

children.title: Server–Worker Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Centralized coordination through parameter-server or master–worker topologies.

knowledge_statements.title: Server–Worker Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centralized message interface for distributed finite-sum variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let workers hold disjoint index sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\) partitioning \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), while a server owns the authoritative parameter and control state \((x^k,s^k)\). At logical round \(k\), the server sends a versioned state \((x^{r_p},s^{r_p},r_p)\) to worker \(p\). The worker returns a message \((u_p,r_p)\), where \(u_p\) is computed only from its local functions and the received state. The server applies an aggregation map \((x^{k+1},s^{k+1})=A_k((x^k,s^k),\{(u_p,r_p):p\in P_k\})\). A staleness policy accepts or rejects messages according to their version labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A central server versions global state, workers compute local variance-reduced messages, and the server aggregates accepted messages under an explicit staleness policy.
assumptions_latex: Each worker can evaluate \(\nabla f_i\) only for \(i\in I_p\).

notation.meaning: Finite-sum indices stored by worker p.
Version of the server state used by worker p.
Workers whose messages are accepted at round k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected locally: this estimator-aggregation condition belongs primarily to synchronous data-parallel variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(n_p=|I_p|>0\), and suppose \(\mathbb E[v_p\mid\mathcal F]=n_p^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_p}\nabla f_i(x)\). Then \(\mathbb E[\sum_p(n_p/n)v_p\mid\mathcal F]=\nabla F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition-size weighting makes locally unbiased worker estimators globally unbiased.

notation.meaning: Number of components held by worker p.
