Partition-weighted gradient aggregation was deferred to Synchronous Data-Parallel Variance Reduction. Decentralized mixing and topology-dependent costs were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Decentralized Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Peer-to-peer coordination without a permanent central aggregation point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decentralized Gradient-Tracking Interface and Conservation Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-only gradient tracking for decentralized finite-sum variance-reduced directions on a balanced network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\) agents communicate through a graph-compatible matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) satisfying \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\). Stack local iterates, trackers, and local variance-reduced gradient estimates as \(X^k\), \(Y^k\), and \(G^k\). Consider
\[X^{k+1}=WX^k-\eta Y^k,\qquad Y^{k+1}=WY^k+G^{k+1}-G^k.\]
If \(Y^0=G^0\), then for every \(k\),
\[\frac1m\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}Y^k=\frac1m\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G^k,\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\eta\bar y^k.\]
Thus the tracking correction preserves the network-average estimated direction, while consensus disagreement remains a separate state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decentralized gradient tracker mixes neighbor states and adds the change in local variance-reduced estimates; consistent initialization makes the average tracker equal the average local estimate at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: The stacked states have compatible finite dimensions.
The same left-multiplication convention is used in both recursions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m^{-1}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}Y^k=m^{-1}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G^k\) and \(\bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\eta\bar y^k\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: network averages of the primal and tracking states

knowledge_statements.title: Decentralized Gradient-Tracking Interface and Conservation Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-only debiasing interface for directed or unbalanced communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^k\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be graph-compatible and column-stochastic, \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}A^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\), with positive diagonal. Agents maintain numerator states \(z^k\), positive weights \(w^k\), and ratios \(x_i^k=z_i^k/w_i^k\): \[w^{k+1}=A^kw^k,\qquad z^{k+1}=A^kz^k-\eta g^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=z_i^{k+1}/w_i^{k+1}.\] With \(w^0=\mathbf1\), \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^k=m\). For the pure mixing part, both numerator and weight totals are preserved, and ratio normalization removes the nonuniform Perron weighting of plain column-stochastic mixing. Convergence additionally requires suitable joint connectivity, positive weights, stepsizes, and estimator control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum augments directed neighbor mixing with scalar weights and uses numerator-to-weight ratios to remove unbalanced-network bias.
assumptions_latex: \(A^k\) is graph-compatible, column-stochastic, and has positive diagonal.
\(w^0=\mathbf1\), and every used denominator is positive.
\(g^k\) stacks the declared local variance-reduced directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^k=m,\qquad x_i^k=z_i^k/w_i^k,\text{ providing ratio debiasing for column-stochastic mixing}.

notation.meaning: push-sum normalization weight at agent i
unnormalized numerator state at agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Push-Sum Decentralized Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-only primal–dual representation for consensus-constrained finite sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each agent own \(F_i\), stack local variables as \(X\), and let \(B\) be an oriented incidence matrix of a connected undirected graph. The decentralized problem \[\min_X\sum_{i=1}^m F_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad(B\otimes I)X=0\] admits the neighbor-local primal–dual interface \[\Lambda^{k+1}=\Lambda^k+\sigma(B\otimes I)\widetilde X^k,\qquad X^{k+1}=\mathcal U\!\left(X^k,G^k+(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)\Lambda^{k+1}\right),\] where \(G^k\) stacks local variance-reduced directions and \(\mathcal U\) is the local update prescribed by the selected primal–dual method. The constraint residual vanishes exactly at consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus can be represented by an incidence constraint; edge multipliers update from neighbor disagreement and correct local variance-reduced directions through neighbor-local messages.
assumptions_latex: The undirected communication graph is connected and \(B\) is an oriented incidence matrix.
Each agent can compute its local variance-reduced direction and the declared local update \(\mathcal U\).
Stepsizes and extrapolation are supplied by the selected primal–dual variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (B\otimes I)X=0\iff x_1=\cdots=x_m,\quad B\otimes I\text{ and }B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I\text{ are implementable by edge-neighbor communication}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Based Primal–Dual Consensus Interface
Decentralized Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-to-neighbor interface without an authoritative central parameter server.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected communication graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Agent \(p\) stores local state \((x_p^k,s_p^k)\) and local finite-sum data. With a mixing matrix \(W\) satisfying \(W_{pq}=0\) whenever \((p,q)\notin E\) and \(p\ne q\), one communication-computation round has the interface \(y_p^k=\sum_{q=1}^m W_{pq}x_q^k\), followed by \((x_p^{k+1},s_p^{k+1})=U_p(y_p^k,s_p^k,\xi_p^k)\), where \(\xi_p^k\) selects local component information. The global output is the agent collection or its average \(\bar x^K=m^{-1}\sum_p x_p^K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent mixes neighbor states and then applies a local variance-reduced update; no node owns the authoritative global iterate.

notation.meaning: Local variance-reduction control state at agent p.
Average of the agents' parameter vectors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the selected mix-then-update decentralized variance-reduction interface. Other decentralized methods use gradient tracking, primal–dual states, directed mixing, or different communication orderings, so this variant cannot be treated as canonical without a source.

children.title: Topology-Dependent Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Communication and synchronization limitations induced by coordination topology.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topology-induced round time in synchronous centralized execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If worker computation, critical-path communication, and serialized aggregation are nonoverlapping phases, then \(T_k=\max_{1\le p\le m}c_{p,k}+b_k+a_k\). Hence \(T_k\ge c_{q,k}\) for every worker \(q\), and \(T_k\ge b_k+a_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous centralized round is limited by its slowest worker and irreducible communication-plus-aggregation time.
assumptions_latex: Computation, critical-path communication, and serialized aggregation do not overlap.

notation.meaning: Worker-p computation time in round k.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier and Aggregator Critical-Path Bottlenecks

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consensus Contraction Is Not a Communication Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of the spectral mixing-round estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(\|W^tX-\mathbf1\bar x^\top\|_F\le\rho^t\|X-\mathbf1\bar x^\top\|_F\), choosing \(t\ge\log(1/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\) guarantees an \(\varepsilon\)-factor reduction. This upper contraction estimate alone does not prove that every consensus or optimization method needs that many rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral formula gives a sufficient pure-mixing budget, not a universal communication lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The displayed spectral contraction estimate holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\log(1/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\) is sufficient in the contraction model, not necessary for every method.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Contraction Is Not a Communication Lower Bound
Topology-Dependent Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral communication penalty for consensus-based decentralized variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix on a connected graph, and define \(\rho=\max\{|\lambda_2(W)|,|\lambda_m(W)|\}<1\). For the disagreement matrix \(X-\mathbf 1\bar x^\top\), \(t\) pure mixing rounds satisfy \[\|W^tX-\mathbf 1\bar x^\top\|_F\le \rho^t\|X-\mathbf 1\bar x^\top\|_F.\] Consequently, reducing disagreement by a factor \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(t\ge \log(1/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\) rounds in this contraction model. As \(\rho\uparrow1\), this communication requirement scales as \(O((1-\rho)^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))\), exposing a topology-dependent bottleneck independent of local gradient cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus communication slows as the mixing matrix spectral gap closes; reducing disagreement by a fixed factor then requires proportionally more rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^\top\) is doubly stochastic and respects a connected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t=O((1-\rho)^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))\) mixing rounds suffice in the spectral-contraction model.

notation.meaning: Largest nonconsensus eigenvalue magnitude of the mixing matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral contraction is standard but uncited, and it concerns pure consensus rather than the complexity of a full variance-reduced optimizer. Moreover, the displayed upper bound establishes that the stated number of rounds suffices; it does not by itself prove that every method requires that many rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-Informed Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter selection from smoothness, strong convexity, and variance information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), a regularity-informed policy is a deterministic map \((\eta,m,b,q)=\Pi(\widehat L,\widehat\mu,\widehat\sigma^2,n)\) from available regularity estimates to stepsize, epoch length, batch size, and refresh probability. Admissibility requires \(0<\eta\le c/\widehat L\) for a method-specific constant \(c>0\), \(1\le b\le n\), \(m\in\mathbb N\), and \(q\in(0,1]\). If strong convexity is used, the policy must require \(\widehat\mu>0\); otherwise it must not invoke the condition number \(\widehat L/\widehat\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose stepsize, epoch, batch, and refresh parameters from explicit regularity estimates, using strong-convexity-dependent quantities only when positive curvature is available.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat L>0\) is a declared smoothness estimate.
\(\widehat\mu\ge0\) and \(\widehat\sigma^2\ge0\) are declared curvature and variance estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\eta,m,b,q)=\Pi(\widehat L,\widehat\mu,\widehat\sigma^2,n)\) satisfies the stated admissibility constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The policy family is plausible, but no source supports this joint map or its admissibility rules. The bound involving the unspecified method-specific constant cannot be assessed independently of a particular variance-reduction method and theorem.

children.title: Backtracking Stepsizes
children.top_down_role: Stepsize selection through trial values and observable acceptance criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Stepsizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric line search using a finite-sum smoothness majorization test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^k\), trial estimate \(L_k>0\), multiplier \(\gamma>1\), and sampled test set \(B_k\), form \(v^k\) with \(\mathbb E[v^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla F(x^k)\). For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), set \(M_{k,j}=\gamma^jL_k\), \(\eta_{k,j}=1/M_{k,j}\), and \(y_{k,j}=x^k-\eta_{k,j}v^k\). Accept the first \(j\) for which \[F_{B_k}(y_{k,j})\le F_{B_k}(x^k)+\langle\nabla F_{B_k}(x^k),y_{k,j}-x^k\rangle+\frac{M_{k,j}}2\|y_{k,j}-x^k\|^2.\] Set \(x^{k+1}=y_{k,j}\), record \(L_{k+1}=M_{k,j}\), and stop under the parent method's prescribed criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase a trial smoothness estimate geometrically until a sampled finite-sum quadratic upper-bound test accepts the corresponding step.
assumptions_latex: \(F_B(x)=|B|^{-1}\sum_{i\in B}f_i(x)\) is evaluable on each test batch.
The accepted update uses the same trial point appearing in the test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=x^k-M_{k,j}^{-1}v^k\) for the first accepted trial index \(j\).

notation.meaning: Objective restricted to the line-search test batch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this sampled-objective backtracking rule for an estimator formed outside the stated test. Its termination, sampling dependence, and preservation of the parent variance-reduction guarantees require method-specific validation.

children.title: Non-Backtracking Adaptive Stepsizes
children.top_down_role: Online stepsize adjustment without repeated acceptance trials.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Backtracking Adaptive Stepsizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-shot stepsize adaptation without repeated trial-point evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given bounds \(0<\eta_{\min}\le\eta_{\max}\), initialize \(\eta_0\in[\eta_{\min},\eta_{\max}]\). At iteration \(k\ge1\), compute the variance-reduced estimator \(v^k\) and the secant quantities \(s_k=x^k-x^{k-1}\) and \(y_k=v^k-v^{k-1}\). Define \(r_k=\langle s_k,y_k\rangle/\|s_k\|^2\) when \(\|s_k\|>0\) and \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle>0\); otherwise retain the previous estimate. Set \(\eta_k=\operatorname{clip}(1/r_k,\eta_{\min},\eta_{\max})\) and perform the single update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv^k\). Output the parent method's prescribed terminal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate local curvature from consecutive iterates and gradient estimators, clip its reciprocal, and take one update without a line-search loop.
assumptions_latex: \(v^k\) is the parent variance-reduced gradient estimator at \(x^k\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the stated stepsize interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The title does not determine a secant rule, and no source supports this chosen variant. The fallback case says to retain a previous estimate without defining the stored curvature value or the resulting stepsize, leaving the algorithm incomplete.

children.title: Adaptation Stability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of stepsize adaptation to stochastic noise or changing local regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictability and boundedness conditions preventing unstable feedback from adaptive stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the history before sampling the component used at iteration \(k\). A stepsize adaptation is stable when \(\eta_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and there exist deterministic constants \(0<\eta_{\min}\le\eta_{\max}<\infty\) and \(C_\eta<\infty\) such that, almost surely, \[\eta_{\min}\le\eta_k\le\eta_{\max},\qquad |\eta_{k+1}-\eta_k|\le C_\eta\eta_k.\] If the parent method requires a smoothness safety margin, stability additionally imposes \(\eta_{\max}\le c/L\) for its stated constant \(c\). These predicates prevent look-ahead dependence and unbounded multiplicative stepsize changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable adaptation chooses stepsizes from past information, keeps them in a fixed positive interval, and limits their relative change.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_k)\) records all information available before iteration-k sampling.
The parent method declares any required smoothness safety constant \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k\) is predictable, uniformly bounded, and has bounded relative variation almost surely.

notation.meaning: Pre-sampling information history at iteration k.
Smoothness constant used by the parent method.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Predictability and boundedness are meaningful conditions, but the proposed relative-change predicate is not a canonical definition of adaptation stability and is not shown sufficient for any identified parent theorem.

children.title: Adaptive Epoch Policies
children.top_down_role: Online adjustment of epoch length or inner-loop duration.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Epoch Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online choice of inner-loop length from a measurable progress statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At epoch \(s\), let \(\tilde x_s\) be the reference point and let \(R_s\ge0\) be an \(\mathcal F_s\)-measurable statistic, such as a normalized gradient-mapping estimate. Given thresholds \(0<a<b\), factor \(\gamma>1\), and bounds \(1\le m_{\min}\le m_{\max}\), update \[m_{s+1}=\begin{cases}\min\{\lceil\gamma m_s\rceil,m_{\max}\},&R_s>b,\\ \max\{\lfloor m_s/\gamma\rfloor,m_{\min}\},&R_s<a,\\ m_s,&a\le R_s\le b.\end{cases}\] Run exactly \(m_{s+1}\) variance-reduced inner updates before constructing \(\tilde x_{s+1}\). Stop according to the parent method and output its prescribed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lengthen or shorten the next variance-reduction epoch according to a predeclared progress statistic, while enforcing finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_{s+1}\in\{m_{\min},\ldots,m_{\max}\}\) is fixed before the next epoch's samples are drawn.

notation.meaning: Number of inner updates in epoch s.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source selects this threshold-based epoch rule. The statistic is only exemplified rather than defined, so the policy's mathematical behavior and compatibility with a variance-reduction convergence theorem cannot be assessed.

children.title: Adaptive Batch Policies
children.top_down_role: Online adjustment of mini-batch size or composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Batch Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch-size control using an empirical estimator-variance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), draw a pilot batch and compute component corrections \(z_i^k\) whose mean estimates the required variance-reduced direction. For a candidate batch size \(b_k\), let \(v_k=b_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in B_k}z_i^k\) and let \(S_k^2\) be the pilot empirical second moment about its mean. Given tolerance \(\theta>0\), choose the smallest allowed \(b_k\in\mathcal B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfying \(S_k^2/b_k\le\theta^2\max\{\|v_k\|^2,\delta^2\}\), where \(\delta>0\). Use \(v_k\) in \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv_k\), and output the parent method's prescribed terminal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the smallest permitted batch whose estimated mean variance is small relative to the update direction, with a positive safeguard near stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Pilot corrections are conditionally sampled according to the parent estimator.
\(\mathcal B\) is nonempty and contains a fallback batch size.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the empirical-variance policy. The candidate batch mean depends on the batch size being selected, and the scalar meaning of the vector-valued empirical second moment is not defined; the pilot-to-candidate sampling protocol is also unclear.

children.title: Adaptive Refresh Policies
children.top_down_role: Online adjustment of estimator-reference renewal frequency.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Refresh Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent refresh of the reference gradient or gradient table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k,s^k)\) be the iterate and variance-reduction control state. Before sampling iteration \(k\), compute an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable refresh probability \(q_k=Q(R_k)\in[q_{\min},1]\), where \(q_{\min}>0\) and \(R_k\) is a declared staleness or progress statistic. Draw \(U_k\) conditionally uniformly on \([0,1]\). If \(U_k\le q_k\), replace \(s^k\) by an exact refreshed state \(\mathcal R(x^k)\); otherwise retain \(s^k\). Construct the prescribed unbiased variance-reduced estimator from the resulting state, update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_kv^k\), and stop under the parent criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh variance-reduction state with a predictable, state-dependent probability bounded away from zero, then form the usual estimator and update.

notation.meaning: Stored control variate, table, or reference-gradient state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The refresh mechanism and the claimed construction of an unbiased estimator depend on the particular control state and estimator. No direct source identifies conditions under which this adaptive refresh probability preserves the required estimator or convergence properties.

children.title: Coupled Adaptation Effects
children.top_down_role: Interactions among epoch, batch, and refresh controls when adjusted simultaneously.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Adaptation Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint control condition for stepsize, batching, epoch length, and refresh frequency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For adaptive parameters \((\eta_k,b_k,m_k,q_k)\), define the effective noise budget \(N_k=\eta_k^2\mathbb E[\|v^k-\nabla F(x^k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\) and the expected refresh gap \(G_k=1/q_k\). A coupled policy is admissible for a parent convergence theorem when its parameters are predictable and there exist constants \(\bar\eta,\bar N,\bar G<\infty\) such that, almost surely, \[0<\eta_k\le\bar\eta,\qquad N_k\le\bar N,\qquad G_k\le\bar G,\qquad 1\le b_k\le n,\qquad 1\le m_k<\infty.\] Any stronger descent, summability, or contraction inequalities required by the parent theorem must hold jointly after substitution of all four schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive schedules must be assessed jointly because stepsize, estimator variance, epoch length, and refresh frequency enter the same convergence inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The parent method specifies the estimator \(v^k\) and its convergence inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete adapted schedule satisfies the parent theorem's inequalities simultaneously, not parameter by parameter.

notation.meaning: Expected refresh gap under probability q_k.
Information available before iteration-k random sampling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits a joint admissibility condition, but the listed boundedness predicates are not sufficient for a general convergence theorem. Because the decisive inequalities are deferred to an unspecified parent theorem and no source is supplied, the claimed condition cannot be validated.

children.title: Parameter-Free Variance Reduction
children.top_down_role: Variance-reduced methods whose stated operation avoids problem-dependent parameter input.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines parameter-free at the algorithmic-policy level, independently of any particular variance-reduced estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the finite-sum objective \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), let \(\mathcal H_k\) contain the sampled indices, queried function values or gradients, iterates, and internal randomness observed through iteration \(k\). A variance-reduction method is parameter-free if every step size, batch size, refresh decision, and stopping decision at iteration \(k\) is an \(\mathcal H_k\)-measurable function fixed by the algorithm, with no user-supplied numerical parameter depending on unknown smoothness, strong-convexity, variance, accuracy, or horizon constants. Universal numerical constants and the known component count \(n\) are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All operational parameters are determined from observed oracle history and universal constants, without user-supplied problem constants, target accuracy, or iteration horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) is accessed through component oracles.
The component count \(n\) may be known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method's complete parameter policy is determined by \(\mathcal H_k\), universal constants, and optionally \(n\).

notation.meaning: Oracle and algorithmic history available through iteration k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational definition separating parameter-free policies from methods requiring unknown problem constants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational definition is coherent, but no cited source establishes this particular meaning of parameter-free variance reduction or its permitted inputs.

children.title: Almost Tune-Free Variance Reduction
children.top_down_role: Variance-reduced methods retaining only limited or weakly sensitive tuning choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Almost Tune-Free Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines low-tuning methods that estimate or bracket required scales online.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variance-reduction method for \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) is almost tune-free if its user inputs contain no problem-dependent numerical constant, while its operational parameters may be selected by data-dependent tests using only observed oracle information. Such tests may employ backtracking, doubling, restarts, or confidence levels fixed independently of the instance. The designation permits universal constants and known structural inputs such as \(n\), but requires every estimate of smoothness, variance, curvature, or horizon to be constructed during execution rather than supplied in advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method needs no problem-dependent numerical input but may estimate required scales online through backtracking, doubling, restarts, or related tests.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm can evaluate the acceptance tests required by its adaptation rule.
Known structural data, including \(n\), are distinguished from unknown numerical scales.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All problem-dependent numerical scales used by the method are inferred from oracle observations during execution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: low-tuning classification based on online estimation of otherwise tuned constants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition substantially overlaps the parameter-free sibling. A source is needed to justify the term and identify a mathematically stable distinction between the two categories.

children.title: Hidden Tuning Dependencies
children.top_down_role: Residual dependence on stopping rules, confidence choices, initialization, or implementation constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Tuning Dependencies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhibits an implicit smoothness dependence in a nominally fixed-step variance-reduced update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider identical components \(f_i(x)=Lx^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), so every standard unbiased control-variate estimator equals \(Lx_k\). A method using the purportedly parameter-free constant step \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta Lx_k\) satisfies \(x_{k+1}=(1-\eta L)x_k\). Convergence from every \(x_0\) requires \(0<\eta L<2\); if \(\eta L>2\), then \(|x_k|=|1-\eta L|^k|x_0|\) diverges. Thus fixing \(\eta\) without adaptation merely hides a dependence on the unknown smoothness scale \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed step advertised as tuning-free still depends on smoothness: on a rescaled quadratic it diverges whenever the step times curvature exceeds two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform convergence over \(L>0\) is impossible for a fixed positive \(\eta\); the method must know or adapt to \(L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar-quadratic stability calculation is correct and fits a failure boundary, but no source supports its use as the stated hidden-tuning taxonomy criterion.

children.title: Finite-Sum Method Suitability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural, statistical, and systems regimes in which finite-sum reuse, estimator correction, or acceleration may lose its intended advantage.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Limitations of monotone-operator analysis and acceleration boundaries
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonatomic Stream Has No Indexed Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of persistent component identities in a genuinely fresh continuous stream.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Z_1,Z_2,\ldots be independent draws from a nonatomic distribution. Then \mathbb P(Z_s=Z_t)=0 for every s\neq t, and therefore \mathbb P(\exists s<t:Z_s=Z_t)=0. A table keyed by exact sample identity is almost surely never revisited, so methods requiring later queries to the same indexed component cannot realize that reuse through this fresh-sample interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nonatomic fresh sampling, exact samples almost surely never repeat, so identity-keyed component tables receive no revisits.
assumptions_latex: Z_t\text{ are independent and identically distributed}.

notation.meaning: Fresh data item observed at call t.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonatomic Stream Has No Indexed Reuse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes within-call common randomness from persistent indexed-component reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For F(x)=\mathbb E_Z[f(x;Z)], suppose one fresh sample Z can be evaluated at both x and y. Then d=
abla f(x;Z)-
abla f(y;Z)+h(y) satisfies \mathbb E[d]=
abla F(x)-
abla F(y)+\mathbb E[h(y)]. Hence d is unbiased for 
abla F(x) exactly when \mathbb E[h(y)]=
abla F(y). This uses within-call common randomness, not later revisitation of a persistent index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Streaming paired differences can use one fresh sample at two points, but require an unbiased anchor and do not constitute indexed reuse.
assumptions_latex: The same fresh sample Z is used in both gradient terms.

notation.meaning: Possibly random anchor estimator at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Fresh-Sample Paired-Difference Alternative
Effectively Infinite or Changing Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies control-variate bias when the finite-sum population changes after snapshot construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_t(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_{i,t}(x)\), sample \(I\) uniformly, and retain a snapshot gradient \(
abla F_s(\widetilde x)\) from time \(s<t\). The estimator \(v=
abla f_{I,t}(x)-
abla f_{I,t}(\widetilde x)+
abla F_s(\widetilde x)\) obeys \(\mathbb E[v\mid x,\widetilde x]=
abla F_t(x)+b_{s,t}(\widetilde x)\), where \(b_{s,t}(z)=
abla F_s(z)-
abla F_t(z)\). Hence snapshot reuse is unbiased only when the aggregate gradient at the reference point has not changed; an effectively unbounded stream provides no fixed component population to revisit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A snapshot from an earlier data population introduces bias equal to the change in aggregate gradient at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimator is unbiased for \(\nabla F_t(x)\) if and only if \(b_{s,t}(\widetilde x)=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct expectation identity for a stale control variate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed stale-snapshot bias identity is correct, but the extension from a changing finite population to an effectively unbounded stream requires supporting literature.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact collision probability and the sharp first-revisit scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For m\leq n independent uniform draws from n indices, \mathbb P(\text{no repeat})=(n)_m/n^m=\prod_{k=0}^{m-1}(1-k/n). If m/\sqrt n\to c\in[0,\infty), then \mathbb P(\text{at least one repeat})\to1-e^{-c^2/2}; if m/\sqrt n\to\infty, the repeat probability tends to one. Thus m\asymp\sqrt n is the sharp first-revisit scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first repeated component occurs at the birthday scale, m proportional to the square root of n.
assumptions_latex: Indices are sampled independently and uniformly from \{1,\ldots,n\}.
m\leq n\text{ for the displayed falling-factorial formula}.
knowledge_statements.title: Birthday-Scale Reuse Transition
Weak Component-Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses sampling collisions to characterize when table or snapshot reuse is intrinsically rare.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m\) component indices are sampled independently and uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The probability of at least one repeated index is at most \(\binom m2/n\). Consequently, if \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), this probability tends to zero as \(n\to\infty\). In that regime, with high probability no sampled component is revisited during the computational horizon, so component-specific stored gradients cannot supply repeated-component information; any advantage must instead arise from aggregate snapshots or additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before roughly the square-root-of-population sampling scale, repeated component visits are unlikely, limiting the value of component-specific gradient tables.
assumptions_latex: Indices are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement.
The computational horizon uses \(m\) component queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), then \(\mathbb P(\text{some repeated index})\to0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: union bound for the finite-population collision probability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The collision bound and asymptotic conclusion are correct. The interpretation as a suitability boundary for gradient-table reuse needs an inspectable source.

children.title: Heterogeneous Components
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes driven by strong variation across component scales, curvature, noise, or supports.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support requirement for importance-weighted control-variate sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i, the ordinary inverse-probability estimator requires p_i>0 for every component whose gradient can affect \nabla F. If p_j=0 for such a component, sampled terms cannot supply its contribution through (np_I)^{-1}; unbiased full-gradient estimation is impossible unless that contribution is separately evaluated or reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonredundant component cannot receive zero sampling probability unless its contribution is obtained separately.
assumptions_latex: Only sampled component gradients and declared deterministic corrections are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_j=0\text{ for a nonredundant component}\Rightarrow\text{the ordinary inverse-probability estimator cannot be unbiased for }\nabla F.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Probability Component Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Heterogeneity Penalty for Uniform Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform sampling relative to smoothness-proportional sampling in the seed bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For L_i>0, let B(p)=n^{-2}\sum_iL_i^2/p_i. Uniform sampling gives B_{\mathrm{unif}}=n^{-1}\sum_iL_i^2, while minimization over positive probabilities gives B_\star=n^{-2}(\sum_iL_i)^2 at p_i=L_i/\sum_jL_j. Hence 1\leq B_{\mathrm{unif}}/B_\star=n\sum_iL_i^2/(\sum_iL_i)^2<n, and the ratio can approach n when one scale dominates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform sampling can make the heterogeneity-sensitive variance bound almost n times larger than optimal importance sampling.

notation.meaning: Coefficient of squared reference displacement in the variance bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Heterogeneity Penalty for Uniform Sampling
Heterogeneous Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows how component smoothness heterogeneity enters an importance-sampled control-variate bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each differentiable component have an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(p_i>0\) with \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and sample \(I\) with probability \(p_i\). For \(g=
abla F(y)+(np_I)^{-1}(
abla f_I(x)-
abla f_I(y))\), one has \(\mathbb E[g]=
abla F(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\|g-
abla F(x)\|^2\le n^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n L_i^2p_i^{-1}\|x-y\|^2\). Thus heterogeneous component scales directly affect the reuse error, and choosing \(p_i\) proportional to \(L_i\) minimizes this displayed upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For heterogeneous smoothness constants, control-variate variance depends on the sampling probabilities; probabilities proportional to component smoothness minimize the stated bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimator is unbiased and satisfies the stated heterogeneity-sensitive second-moment bound.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: importance-sampling variance bound follows from unbiasedness and component Lipschitz inequalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The estimator is unbiased, the second-moment bound is valid, and minimizing the displayed bound gives probabilities proportional to the component smoothness constants. No supporting variance-reduction source is cited.

children.title: Misspecified Components
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes involving corrupted, biased, stale, or structurally mismatched component models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: True gradient guarantee obtainable from a misspecified estimator residual and a verified bias bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \mathbb E[v\mid x]=
abla F(x)+b(x) and \|b(x)\|\leq\delta, then \|
abla F(x)\|\leq\|\mathbb E[v\mid x]\|+\delta. Thus \|\mathbb E[v\mid x]\|\leq\varepsilon certifies only \|
abla F(x)\|\leq\varepsilon+\delta. Without a bias bound, the surrogate residual gives no finite gradient-norm certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A misspecified estimator residual certifies true stationarity only after adding a verified bias allowance.

notation.meaning: Verified upper bound on aggregate estimator bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias-Aware Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Biased Reference Produces a False Stationary Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent model bias can make a surrogate residual vanish away from true stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let F(x)=	frac12x^2 and suppose \mathbb E[v\mid x]=x+b for a constant b
eq0. At x=-b the estimator has zero conditional mean, but 
abla F(-b)=-b
eq0. Thus a zero surrogate residual is not a stationarity certificate under persistent misspecification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant reference bias shifts the estimator's apparent stationary point away from the true one.
knowledge_statements.title: Biased Reference Produces a False Stationary Point
Misspecified Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies bias caused by reusing references computed from incorrect component models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), but suppose the stored reference for component \(i\) is computed from a surrogate \(\widehat f_i\). For uniform \(I\), define \(v=
abla f_I(x)-
abla\widehat f_I(y)+n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n
abla\widehat f_j(y)\). Then \(\mathbb E[v]=
abla F(x)\); however, if the aggregate correction is instead formed from the true gradients while the subtracted reference remains surrogate, the estimator \(w=
abla f_I(x)-
abla\widehat f_I(y)+
abla F(y)\) has bias \(n^{-1}\sum_i(
abla f_i(y)-
abla\widehat f_i(y))\). Consistent pairing is therefore necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surrogate component references preserve unbiasedness only when the subtracted and aggregated surrogate corrections are paired consistently; mixing surrogate and true references creates explicit bias.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed estimator \(w\) is unbiased exactly when \(\sum_i(\nabla f_i(y)-\nabla\widehat f_i(y))=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact expectation identities for consistently and inconsistently paired control variates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expectation identities and stated bias are correct, but an authoritative source is needed for interpreting inconsistent surrogate pairing as the intended misspecification boundary.

children.title: Robust Reuse Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on estimator reuse when heterogeneity or misspecification dominates correction quality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stale-snapshot bias test when old and current aggregate references are evaluable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If both aggregate gradients at y are available, define D_{s,t}(y)=\|\nabla F_s(y)-\nabla F_t(y)\|. For the stale-snapshot estimator of the deferred seed, D_{s,t}(y) equals the norm of its conditional bias. Thus D_{s,t}(y)\leq\varepsilon_b exactly certifies bias at most \varepsilon_b; if D_{s,t}(y)>\varepsilon_b, that estimator cannot have conditional mean-squared error at most \varepsilon_b^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The old-to-current aggregate-gradient difference exactly measures stale-snapshot bias.
assumptions_latex: The estimator uses the old aggregate reference as in the deferred seed.

notation.meaning: Aggregate gradient drift at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Observable Reference-Drift Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of conditional sampling variance and irreducible reuse bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a conditionally square-integrable reused estimator v of g=\nabla F_t(x), let b=\mathbb E[v\mid x]-g. Then \mathbb E[\|v-g\|^2\mid x]=\mathbb E[\|v-\mathbb E[v\mid x]\|^2\mid x]+\|b\|^2. Variance reduction cannot remove nonzero drift or misspecification bias; conditional mean-squared error at most \varepsilon^2 requires \|b\|\leq\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse MSE equals conditional variance plus squared bias, so bias above tolerance makes the target impossible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\|v-g\|^2\mid x]=\mathbb E[\|v-\mathbb E[v\mid x]\|^2\mid x]+\|b\|^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Biased-Reuse Mean-Squared-Error Decomposition
Robust Reuse Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a bounded-drift condition under which reused component references retain controlled bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For time-varying differentiable components \(f_{i,t}\), a stored reference from time \(s\) is \(\delta_{s,t}\)-robust at \(y\) when \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_{i,s}(y)-
abla f_{i,t}(y)\|\le\delta_{s,t}\). For the stale-snapshot estimator \(v=
abla f_{I,t}(x)-
abla f_{I,t}(y)+
abla F_s(y)\), uniform sampling gives \(\|\mathbb E[v]-
abla F_t(x)\|=\|
abla F_s(y)-
abla F_t(y)\|\le\delta_{s,t}\). Thus reuse has a certified bias tolerance \(\varepsilon\) whenever \(\delta_{s,t}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale reference remains robust when average component-gradient drift is bounded; that bound directly controls the estimator's bias.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reuse bias is at most \(\delta_{s,t}\), and hence at most \(\varepsilon\) if \(\delta_{s,t}\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Average component-gradient drift between reference and current times.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: triangle inequality applied to the exact stale-snapshot bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bias bound follows from the stated drift condition, and condition is an appropriate content kind. The proposed robustness terminology and tolerance interpretation lack a cited source.

children.title: Stale-Snapshot Degradation
children.top_down_role: Estimator deterioration caused by outdated global reference points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth two-component family attaining the generic snapshot variance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(f_1(x)=\tfrac{L}{2}x^2\), \(f_2(x)=-\tfrac{L}{2}x^2\), and sample \(I\) uniformly. Then \(F\equiv0\). With snapshot \(\widetilde x=0\), the snapshot estimator equals \(v=Lx\) or \(-Lx\) with equal probability, so \(\mathbb E[v]=0\) and \(\mathbb E\lvert v-\nabla F(x)\rvert^2=L^2\lvert x-\widetilde x\rvert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic snapshot-displacement variance bound is attained by a two-component smooth finite sum.

notation.meaning: Stored global snapshot, here equal to zero.

Stale-Snapshot Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds snapshot-estimator variance by the distance from the current iterate to the snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), assume every \(
abla f_i\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, and sample \(I\) uniformly. The snapshot estimator \(v=
abla f_I(x)-
abla f_I(\widetilde x)+
abla F(\widetilde x)\) is unbiased and satisfies \(\mathbb E\|v-
abla F(x)\|^2\le L^2\|x-\widetilde x\|^2\). Hence the generic variance guarantee deteriorates quadratically with snapshot displacement, motivating refresh before the snapshot becomes too remote.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The variance of a snapshot control variate is bounded by smoothness squared times the squared distance between the current iterate and snapshot.

children.title: Gradient-Table Degradation
children.top_down_role: Estimator deterioration caused by unevenly aged or inaccurate component memories.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unbiasedness boundary when subtraction and centering use different stored tables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), let \(I\) be uniform, and set \(v=\nabla f_I(x)-\alpha_I+n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\beta_j\). Then \(\mathbb E[v]-\nabla F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n(\beta_j-\alpha_j)\). Hence \(v\) is unbiased exactly when the two table aggregates agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A table estimator is unbiased exactly when the references used for subtraction and centering have equal aggregates.

notation.meaning: Reference included in the centering aggregate.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias from Inconsistent Table Aggregation
Gradient-Table Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses gradient-table quality through the discrepancies of stored component references.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\), let \(\alpha_i\) be a stored approximation to \(
abla f_i(x)\), and sample \(I\) uniformly. The table estimator \(v=
abla f_I(x)-\alpha_I+n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_j\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[v]=
abla F(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\|v-
abla F(x)\|^2\le n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\|
abla f_i(x)-\alpha_i\|^2\). Therefore outdated or inaccurate entries degrade the variance guarantee through their mean squared discrepancy, although consistent aggregation preserves unbiasedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistently aggregated gradient table remains unbiased, while its variance is controlled by the mean squared error of its stored component gradients.
assumptions_latex: The same stored entries \(\alpha_i\) are used in subtraction and aggregation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimator is unbiased and its conditional variance is bounded by the table's mean squared gradient discrepancy.

notation.meaning: Stored gradient reference for component i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The centering identity and mean-square discrepancy bound are correct. A gradient-table variance-reduction source is required, including support for treating this degradation phenomenon as a property in the exact container.

children.title: Reference-Age Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where estimator quality becomes highly sensitive to reference age.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Age Alone Does Not Control Reference Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of an age-only discrepancy bound without trajectory control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(L>0\) and \(M>0\), let \(f(x)=\tfrac{L}{2}x^2\), take \(x_{k-1}=0\), \(x_k=M/L\), and store \(\alpha^k=\nabla f(x_{k-1})\). The reference age is one, but \(\lvert\nabla f(x_k)-\alpha^k\rvert=M\). Thus even fixed unit age permits arbitrarily large reference error when iterate displacement is uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-iteration-old reference can have arbitrarily large error if the intervening iterate movement is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.title: Age Alone Does Not Control Reference Error
Reference-Age Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts component-reference age into a deterministic gradient-discrepancy bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(
abla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz and the stored entry at iteration \(k\) is \(\alpha_i^k=
abla f_i(x_{k-	au_i^k})\), where \(	au_i^k\) is its age. Then \(\|
abla f_i(x_k)-\alpha_i^k\|\le L_i\sum_{r=k-	au_i^k}^{k-1}\|x_{r+1}-x_r\|\). If every increment is at most \(D\), this becomes \(\|
abla f_i(x_k)-\alpha_i^k\|\le L_iD	au_i^k\). Thus the table-variance bound can grow quadratically in reference age without stronger trajectory control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored gradient's error grows at most linearly with its age under bounded iterate increments, causing a potentially quadratic contribution to variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_i(x_k)-\alpha_i^k\|\le L_iD\tau_i^k\) under the bounded-increment condition.

notation.meaning: Age of component i's stored reference at iteration k.
Uniform bound on successive iterate displacement.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lipschitz continuity combined with a telescoping path-length bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Lipschitz and path-length bounds are correct, and squaring them permits a quadratic age contribution to the table-variance bound. The age-sensitivity interpretation and selected role need a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothness Bound for Accumulated Recursive Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the mean-square error of an unrefreshed same-sample recursive estimator by cumulative squared path length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(\nabla f_i\) be \(L_i\)-Lipschitz and let \(\overline L_2^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nL_i^2\). Under the conditional sampling assumptions of the recursive-error identity, \[\mathbb E\|e_K\|^2\leq \mathbb E\|e_0\|^2+\overline L_2^2\sum_{k=1}^K\mathbb E\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|^2.\] A finite squared path length therefore bounds accumulated estimator error, but does not by itself force that error to vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component smoothness bounds recursive estimator error by its initial error plus mean-squared smoothness times cumulative squared displacement.
assumptions_latex: Conditionally on the pre-sampling history, \(I_k\) is uniform and \(x_k,x_{k-1},v_{k-1}\) are fixed.
All displayed second moments are finite.

notation.meaning: Recursive gradient-estimation error at step k

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness Bound for Accumulated Recursive Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth finite-sum example in which recursive estimator error grows linearly over unrefreshed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=2\), \(d=1\), \(f_1(x)=\tfrac L2x^2\), and \(f_2(x)=-\tfrac L2x^2\), so \(F\equiv0\). Set \(x_k=kh\), \(v_0=0\), and \[v_k=v_{k-1}+f'_{I_k}(x_k)-f'_{I_k}(x_{k-1}),\] where the \(I_k\) are independent and uniform on \(\{1,2\}\). Then \(e_k=Lh\sum_{j=1}^k\sigma_j\) for independent Rademacher variables \(\sigma_j\), and \[\mathbb E[e_k]=0,\qquad \mathbb E[e_k^2]=kL^2h^2.\] Hence unbiased increments do not prevent unbounded mean-square accumulation without refresh or damping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two opposite quadratic components and constant displacement, the recursive estimator is a random walk with exactly linear mean-square growth.
assumptions_latex: The component indices are independent and uniformly sampled.
No estimator refresh or damping is performed after initialization.

notation.meaning: Rademacher sign determined by the sampled component
Constant displacement between consecutive query points

review_flags: The example concerns estimator stability along a prescribed query path; it does not assert divergence of a particular optimization algorithm.

Recursive Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the exact mean-square error recursion for a SARAH-type recursive estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I_k\) be conditionally uniform and independent of the past, and define \(v_k=v_{k-1}+
abla f_{I_k}(x_k)-
abla f_{I_k}(x_{k-1})\). With \(e_k=v_k-
abla F(x_k)\) and \(\Delta_{i,k}=
abla f_i(x_k)-
abla f_i(x_{k-1})\), one has \(\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal H_{k-1}]=e_{k-1}\) and \(\mathbb E[\|e_k\|^2\mid\mathcal H_{k-1}]=\|e_{k-1}\|^2+\mathbb E[\|\Delta_{I_k,k}-
abla F(x_k)+
abla F(x_{k-1})\|^2\mid\mathcal H_{k-1}]\). Nonnegative increment variances therefore accumulate until an exact or sufficiently accurate refresh resets the error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive gradient estimator carries its previous error forward and adds a nonnegative component-difference variance at every unrefreshed step.
assumptions_latex: Conditionally on \(\mathcal H_{k-1}\), \(I_k\) is uniform and \(x_k,x_{k-1},v_{k-1}\) are fixed.
