children.title: Distributed Method Selection
children.top_down_role: Method choices for multi-worker environments with communication or synchronization costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Method Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-model selection among linearly convergent distributed finite-sum methods admissible for the available network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m}F_i(x)\), where worker \(i\) stores \(F_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\mathcal A\) be a nonempty finite set of distributed variance-reduction methods compatible with the network, delay model, and memory budget. For each \(a\in\mathcal A\), suppose its error sequence satisfies \(\Delta_{a,k}\le \rho_a^k\Delta_0\) with \(\rho_a\in(0,1)\), and one effective iteration uses \(q_a\) local component-gradient evaluations and \(r_a\) communication rounds. Given \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta_0\) and unit costs \(\tau_g,\tau_c>0\), select
\[
a^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\mathcal A}\left\lceil\frac{\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho_a}\right\rceil(q_a\tau_g+r_a\tau_c).
\]
This rule minimizes the stated predicted cost among the admissible distributed methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among the distributed variance-reduced methods satisfying the network, delay, and memory constraints, select one with the smallest predicted cost to reach the target accuracy under the stated contraction and additive resource-cost model.
assumptions_latex: \(q_a,r_a\ge 0\), and the resource counts and positive unit costs \(\tau_g,\tau_c\) are stationary.
Every method in \(\mathcal A\) satisfies the imposed topology, delay, and memory constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\star\) minimizes the stated predicted wall-clock cost over \(\mathcal A\).

notation.meaning: Error bound for method a after k effective iterations, its common initial bound, and the target tolerance.
Local component-gradient evaluations and communication rounds per effective iteration.
Time per local gradient evaluation and per communication round.

children.title: Communication–Computation Crossovers
children.top_down_role: Deployment regimes where communication burden changes the preferred variance-reduction family.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication–Computation Crossovers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock crossover condition for two linearly convergent finite-sum methods under an additive resource-cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For methods \(a\) and \(b\), let
\[
K_j=\left\lceil\frac{\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho_j}\right\rceil,
\qquad T_j=K_j(q_j\tau_g+r_j\tau_c),
\qquad j\in\{a,b\},
\]
where \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta_0\), \(\rho_j\in(0,1)\), \(q_j,r_j\ge0\), and \(\tau_g,\tau_c>0\). Method \(a\) is preferable under this model exactly when \(T_a\le T_b\). Writing \(\gamma=\tau_c/\tau_g\), a nondegenerate crossover occurs at
\[
\gamma^\star=\frac{K_bq_b-K_aq_a}{K_ar_a-K_br_b}
\]
when \(K_ar_a\ne K_br_b\) and \(\gamma^\star\ge0\). Method \(a\) is preferable for \(\gamma\le\gamma^\star\) if \(K_ar_a-K_br_b>0\), and for \(\gamma\ge\gamma^\star\) if \(K_ar_a-K_br_b<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated contraction and additive cost model, two methods cross over where their predicted times agree; the preferred side is determined by their total gradient work, communication rounds, and communication-to-gradient unit-cost ratio.
assumptions_latex: Both methods use the same initial error bound \(\Delta_0\) and target tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign of \(T_a-T_b\), equivalently the stated inequality in \(\gamma\), determines the communication–computation crossover under the additive model.

notation.meaning: Iterations predicted for method j to reach the target tolerance.
Gradient evaluations and communication rounds per iteration of method j.

children.title: Coordination Topology Constraints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disconnected Topologies Cannot Compute Global Average Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-flow obstruction for global coordination across disconnected worker components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be disconnected, and let \(V=V_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_2\) be a partition into nonempty sets with no edge between them. For any distributed protocol in which workers initially know only their local values and messages traverse only edges of \(G\), exact global average consensus at every worker for every initialization \((z_i^0)_{i\in V}\) is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disconnected worker graph cannot support exact global averaging under neighbor-only communication.
assumptions_latex: Workers initially know only their local values.
Messages may traverse only edges of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No such protocol can make every worker output \(|V|^{-1}\sum_{i\in V}z_i^0\) for every initialization.

notation.meaning: initial value held by worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Topologies Cannot Compute Global Average Consensus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Disagreement Contraction for Symmetric Mixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-round rate under a symmetric average-preserving topology-supported mixing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) be symmetric, satisfy \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and have zeros outside the diagonal and edges of a fixed undirected graph. Put \(J=p^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\beta=\|W-J\|_2\). If \(\beta<1\), then \(z^{k+1}=Wz^k\) preserves the average and satisfies \[\|z^k-Jz^0\|_2\le\beta^k\|(I-J)z^0\|_2.\] If \(\|(I-J)z^0\|_2>\varepsilon\), then \(k\ge\left\lceil\log(\|(I-J)z^0\|_2/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\beta)\right\rceil\) rounds suffice for disagreement at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric mixing matrix contracts disagreement geometrically at the magnitude of its largest nonconsensus eigenvalue.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) respects the fixed undirected communication graph.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Connectivity for Time-Varying Doubly Stochastic Mixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous average consensus over changing directed or undirected communication supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_k\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) be nonnegative and doubly stochastic. Assume every diagonal entry and every positive entry is at least \(\alpha>0\), and the union of the directed support graphs over each \(B\)-step window is strongly connected. With \(J=p^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\), there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), depending only on \(p,\alpha,B\), such that \[\|W_{k-1}\cdots W_s-J\|_2\le C\lambda^{k-s}\qquad(k>s).\] Hence \(z^{k+1}=W_kz^k\) preserves the average and converges geometrically to average consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive doubly stochastic mixing reaches average consensus geometrically when every bounded window of directed support graphs is jointly strongly connected.
assumptions_latex: Every diagonal entry and every positive entry is uniformly bounded below by \(\alpha>0\).
Every union of \(B\) consecutive directed support graphs is strongly connected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Push-Sum Consensus on a Fixed Directed Topology
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed-network admissibility when doubly stochastic mixing is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) be nonnegative, column stochastic, primitive, and supported on a fixed strongly connected directed communication graph. Initialize \(s^0\in\mathbb R^p\), \(w^0=\mathbf1\), and iterate \(s^{k+1}=As^k\), \(w^{k+1}=Aw^k\). Then \(w_i^k>0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), and \[\frac{s_i^k}{w_i^k}\longrightarrow\frac1p\sum_{j=1}^p s_j^0\qquad(i=1,\ldots,p).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primitive column-stochastic mixing with push-sum ratio correction computes the global average on a fixed strongly connected directed graph.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) respects the fixed directed communication topology.
knowledge_statements.title: Push-Sum Consensus on a Fixed Directed Topology

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Need Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary distinguishing consensus from exact average consensus on an asymmetric topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[W=\begin{pmatrix}0.9&0.1\\0.2&0.8\end{pmatrix}.\] The matrix is positive and row stochastic, and its normalized stationary left vector is \(\pi=(2/3,1/3)^{\mathsf T}\). Hence \[W^kz\longrightarrow\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T}z=\mathbf1\frac{2z_1+z_2}{3},\] which differs from arithmetic-average consensus \(\mathbf1(z_1+z_2)/2\) whenever \(z_1\ne z_2\). Thus row stochasticity and consensus contraction alone do not ensure exact averaging; a uniform stationary distribution or a normalization mechanism such as push-sum is additionally required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asymmetric row-stochastic matrix can converge to a stationary-distribution-weighted consensus rather than the arithmetic average.
assumptions_latex: Coordination uses \(z^{k+1}=Wz^k\) with the displayed fixed positive row-stochastic matrix.
The desired aggregate is the arithmetic average of the two initial states.

notation.meaning: Normalized stationary left vector of the row-stochastic matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Need Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average
Coordination Topology Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed undirected-network condition for average-consensus coordination inside a distributed variance-reduction method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the worker communication graph, let \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) satisfy \(W_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\ne j\) and \(\{i,j\}\notin E\), and consider \(z^{k+1}=Wz^k\). Put \(J=p^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\). The iteration preserves the network average and converges to exact average consensus for every \(z^0\in\mathbb R^p\) precisely when
\[
W\mathbf1=\mathbf1,
\qquad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},
\qquad \rho(W-J)<1.
\]
Consequently, any distributed variance-reduction method requiring global averaging can use this linear coordination rule only if the topology admits such a mixing matrix; in particular, \(G\) must be connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consensus-based distributed method needs a topology-supported, average-preserving mixing matrix whose disagreement dynamics contract; this requirement excludes disconnected worker graphs.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a fixed undirected graph on \(p\ge2\) workers.
Coordination uses the time-invariant linear iteration \(z^{k+1}=Wz^k\).
Communication is reliable and synchronous during each consensus step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z^0\), \(W^kz^0\to Jz^0\); existence of such \(W\) requires a connected communication topology.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal averaging matrix onto the consensus subspace.
Spectral radius governing contraction of disagreement.
